subject: GK
question: Which state in India ranks first in milk production as per data of 2020-21?
solution:
***The correct answer is Gujarat***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

Gujarat's position as the leading milk-producing state in India is a result of various factors, including the state's favorable climate for dairy farming, strong cooperative dairy movement, supportive government policies, and significant investments in dairy infrastructure.

**Cooperative Dairy Movement:**

Gujarat is home to one of the most successful cooperative dairy movements in the world, spearheaded by the Gujarat Cooperative Milk Marketing Federation (GCMMF), which markets its products under the brand name "Amul." The cooperative model involves millions of dairy farmers who are organized into cooperatives and collectively own and manage the dairy business. This cooperative structure ensures that dairy farmers receive fair prices for their milk and have access to various support services, including veterinary care, feed, and technical assistance.

**Dairy Infrastructure:**

Gujarat boasts a robust dairy infrastructure, including milk collection centers, chilling plants, processing units, and distribution networks. This infrastructure ensures the efficient collection, processing, and distribution of milk and dairy products across the state and beyond. The state government and dairy cooperatives have made significant investments in modernizing and expanding this infrastructure to meet the growing demand for milk and dairy products.

**Government Support:**

The Government of Gujarat has been proactive in supporting the dairy sector through various policies, schemes, and initiatives aimed at promoting dairy farming, enhancing productivity, and improving the livelihoods of dairy farmers. These initiatives include subsidies for the purchase of milch animals, provision of quality feed and fodder, training and extension services, and incentives for dairy cooperatives to invest in infrastructure and technology upgrades.

**Favorable Agro-climatic Conditions:**

Gujarat's agro-climatic conditions, characterized by moderate temperatures and adequate rainfall, are conducive to dairy farming. The state has abundant grazing lands, fodder resources, and water availability, which support the rearing of dairy animals and the production of high-quality milk. Additionally, the state's diverse agricultural landscape enables the cultivation of various fodder crops essential for dairy animal nutrition.

**Market Orientation:**

Gujarat's dairy sector is highly market-oriented, with a focus on value addition and diversification of dairy products. Apart from liquid milk, Gujarat produces a wide range of dairy products such as butter, ghee, cheese, yogurt, ice cream, and flavored milk, catering to domestic and international markets. The state's emphasis on product innovation, quality assurance, and branding has helped to establish a strong presence in the dairy market.

question: Malavikagnimitra, a drama of the 5th century CE, was written by _______.

The correct answer is __**Kalidasa**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kalidasa,** a prominent figure in classical Sanskrit literature, authored the renowned play **"Mālavikāgnimitram" **during the **5th century CE**.
 
• Set in the backdrop of Pushyamitra Shunga's reign, the five-act drama revolves around King Agnimitra's affection for Mālavikā, the maid of his chief queen.
 
• Its captivating storyline, the play is also esteemed as a comprehensive discourse on dramatic art, featuring intricate details such as the Rajasuya sacrifice and insightful theories on music and acting.
 
• Kalidasa himself, a luminary of the Gupta era, is best known for his contributions to Sanskrit literature, which primarily draw from Hindu Puranic narratives and philosophical themes.
 
• His literary legacy encompasses three plays, two epic poems, and two shorter compositions, showcasing his mastery over various genres within Sanskrit literature.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Acharya Pingala,** an ancient Indian poet and mathematician, left a significant mark with his seminal work "Chandaḥśāstra," also known as the Pingala-sutras. This treatise, composed in the late Sūtra style, delves into Sanskrit prosody across eight chapters, although its full comprehension often necessitates supplementary commentary.
 
• **Harisena**, a distinguished Sanskrit poet and court official in the 4th century, held a prominent position in the court of Gupta emperor Samudragupta. His most acclaimed composition, composed around 345 CE, is an ode to the valor of Samudragupta, immortalized on the Allahabad Pillar.
 
• **Bhavabhūti**, an eminent scholar from the 8th century, earned renown for his plays and poetry composed in Sanskrit. Often hailed as the counterpart to Kalidasa, his works, particularly the "Uttararamacarita," showcase his expertise in evoking the sentiment of compassion, earning him the epithet "Poet of Karun Rasa."

question: Who among the following has written the biography of Buddha, Buddhacharita?

The correct answer is __**Ashvaghosha**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ashvaghosha,** a poet and** Buddhist philosopher **from northern India in the** early second century CE**, authored the **Buddhacharita**, an epic Sanskrit poem depicting the** life of Gautama Buddha**.
 
• This significant work, categorized as a **Mahakavya, **resembles other Indian epic poems like the Ramayana and Mahabharata in style.
 
• The Buddhacharita narrates the key events in Buddha's life, drawing from authentic religious sources.
 
• Regarded as a sacred religious text, the Buddhacharita offers a meticulously structured account of Buddha's life, demonstrating restraint in its depiction of his miracles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ashvaghosha's composition** showcases his profound understanding of Indian mythology,** pre-Buddhist philosophy,** and diverse themes such as war, love, and statecraft.
 
• Comprising 28 cantos, the Buddhacharita presents the first 14 cantos in Sanskrit, while Chinese and Tibetan translations preserve all 28 chapters.
 
• **Dharmakṣema **crafted a Chinese rendition in 420 AD, while an anonymous author produced a Tibetan adaptation in the 7th or 8th century, believed to be more faithful to the original Sanskrit text.

question: Which of the following works was authored by Varahamihira?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brihat Samhita**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Brihat Samhita** is an ancient Sanskrit text composed by **Varahamihira**, a renowned Indian astronomer, mathematician, and astrologer.
 
• This work is considered an encyclopedic compilation, covering diverse topics such as astronomy, astrology, geography, architecture, weather prediction, gemology, and horticulture.
 
• Varahamihira lived during the Gupta Empire and was one of the **Navaratnas** (nine jewels) in the court of King Yashodharman.
 
• The Brihat Samhita is famous for its scientific approach and practical knowledge, showcasing advanced insights into various disciplines.
 
• The text also includes chapters on planetary movements and their effects, providing valuable information that is still studied in astrology and astronomy today.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mrichchakatika**

 
 
• Mrichchakatika, also known as “The Little Clay Cart,” is an ancient Sanskrit play written by **Shudraka**.
 
• The play is a classic example of Indian drama, showcasing themes of love, political intrigue, and social justice.
 
• The central story revolves around the romantic relationship between Charudatta, a Brahmin merchant, and Vasantasena, a courtesan.
 
• It is celebrated for its realistic portrayal of human emotions and life in ancient India.
 
 
 
• **Sushruta Samhita**
 
 
• The Sushruta Samhita is one of the foundational texts of Ayurveda, attributed to **Sushruta**, an ancient Indian surgeon.
 
• It is a comprehensive treatise on surgery, medicine, and health practices, detailing procedures for various surgical techniques, including rhinoplasty (plastic surgery).
 
• The text also introduces concepts of anatomy, pharmacology, and patient care.
 
• Sushruta Samhita is considered a pioneering work in the field of medicine and is still referenced in modern Ayurvedic practices.
 
 
 
• **Dashakumaracharita**
 
 
• Dashakumaracharita is a Sanskrit prose narrative attributed to **Dandin**, an ancient Indian writer.
 
• The work is divided into ten chapters and narrates the adventures of ten princes, exploring themes of heroism, romance, and morality.
 
• It is known for its elaborate and poetic descriptions, showcasing the cultural and social life of ancient India.
 
• Dandin’s work reflects his mastery of prose writing and storytelling techniques.

• His notable works include *Kulothunga Cholan Ula*, *Rajasooyam*, and *Saraswati Andhadhi*.

• He is known for his Jain literary contributions, but there is no evidence linking him to *Virasoliyam*.

question: Which of the following rulers founded the Nalanda University?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumaragupta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumaragupta I**, the ruler of the **Gupta Empire**, established **Nalanda University**, which became an important center of learning in ancient India.
 
• The university was founded during the reign of Kumaragupta I around the **5th century CE**, and it flourished as a renowned center for **Buddhist studies**, philosophy, and other disciplines.
 
• Nalanda University was known for its **residential system of education**, housing over 10,000 students and teachers from different parts of Asia.
 
• The university attracted scholars from countries like **China**, **Tibet**, **Korea**, and **Central Asia**. Famous visitors like **Xuanzang** and **I-Tsing** documented their experiences at Nalanda.
 
• Kumaragupta I was instrumental in laying the foundation of Nalanda University, making it a symbol of the **intellectual and cultural achievements** of the Gupta period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Nalanda University:**

 
 
• Located in **Bihar, India**, Nalanda was one of the oldest universities in the world and a major center for **Buddhist education and research**.
 
• The university featured a massive library called the **Dharmaganja**, which housed thousands of manuscripts on various subjects.
 
• Subjects taught included **Buddhist scriptures**, **logic**, **medicine**, **mathematics**, **astronomy**, **philosophy**, and **literature**.
 
• The university was destroyed in the **12th century** by the invasion of **Bakhtiyar Khilji**, marking the end of its glory.
 
 
 
• **Kumaragupta I:**
 
 
• He ruled during the **5th century CE** and was one of the prominent rulers of the **Gupta dynasty**.
 
• Kumaragupta I is remembered for his contributions to cultural and intellectual advancements during his reign.
 
• He issued several **coins and inscriptions**, reflecting the prosperity of the Gupta Empire under his rule.
 
• His reign marked significant developments in **education**, **architecture**, and **religious practices**.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire, often referred to as the **Golden Age of India**, flourished between the **4th and 6th centuries CE**.
 
• Known for advancements in **science**, **mathematics**, **literature**, **art**, and **architecture**.
 
• Famous scholars such as **Kalidasa**, **Aryabhata**, and **Varahamihira** thrived during this period.
 
• The Gupta rulers were also patrons of **Buddhism**, **Hinduism**, and **Jainism**, contributing to the cultural and religious growth of the empire.
 
 
 
• **Xuanzang and Nalanda:**
 
 
• **Xuanzang**, a Chinese pilgrim and scholar, visited Nalanda University in the **7th century CE**.
 
• He documented the university's **curriculum, administration, and scholarly environment**, providing valuable insights into its functioning.
 
• Xuanzang emphasized the role of Nalanda in spreading **Buddhist teachings** across Asia.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other notable Gupta rulers:**

 
 
• **Chandragupta I:** Founder of the Gupta dynasty and instrumental in expanding its territory.
 
• **Samudragupta:** Known as the "Napoleon of India" for his military conquests and patronage of arts.
 
• **Chandragupta II:** Under his reign, India witnessed cultural and economic prosperity, including advancements in trade.
 
 
 
• **Education during Gupta period:**
 
 
• Focus on **higher education** through institutions like **Nalanda** and **Takshashila**.
 
• Subjects ranged from **philosophy**, **astronomy**, and **logic** to **medicine** and **mathematics**.

subject: GK
question:
Consider the following Assertion (A) and Reason (R) and choose the

**Assertion (A) - **Modern technological development plays a very important role in determining the location of urban settlements.

**Reason (R) - **The location of the earliest urban settlement was dependent upon water, building material and fertile land.

options.text: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A.
A is true, but R is false.
A is false, but R is true.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Assertion (A): Modern technological development plays a very important role in determining the location of urban settlements**:

 
 
• Modern technology influences urban settlement locations by introducing factors like connectivity, infrastructure, and accessibility.
 
• Technological advancements, such as the development of transport networks, telecommunication systems, and energy resources, have made certain locations more favorable for urban settlements.
 
• Urban planning today relies heavily on tools such as GIS (Geographic Information Systems), satellite imaging, and data analytics to determine optimal locations for settlements.
 
• Factors like proximity to industries, trade hubs, and economic zones are influenced by technological advancements. ***Hence, Assertion (A) is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Reason (R): The location of the earliest urban settlements was dependent upon water, building material, and fertile land:**
 
 
• Historical urban settlements, such as those in Mesopotamia, the Indus Valley, and Egypt, were established near rivers for water supply and fertile land for agriculture.
 
• Availability of building materials like clay, stone, and wood influenced settlement locations.
 
• These factors were crucial before the advent of modern technology, as they ensured basic survival and facilitated the growth of civilizations. ***Hence, Reason (R) is correct.***
 
 
 
• **Relationship between Assertion (A) and Reason (R):**
 
 
• While both statements are true, the Reason (R) does not directly explain Assertion (A).
 
• Modern technological development now plays a dominant role in determining settlement locations, unlike historical times when water, building material, and fertile land were primary considerations.
 
• The two concepts represent different time periods and factors influencing urban settlement decisions. ***Hence, Option 2 is the correct answer.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors influencing modern urban settlements:**

 
 
• Modern urban centers are influenced by factors such as **proximity to industries**, **availability of resources**, and **transportation networks**.
 
• **Smart cities** and urban planning projects aim to integrate technology to optimize resource utilization and connectivity.
 
• Examples include cities like Bengaluru in India, known for its IT hubs, and Shenzhen in China, a global manufacturing center driven by technological advancements.
 
 
 
• **Historical factors influencing urban settlements:**
 
 
• Ancient cities like Mohenjo-Daro and Harappa were located near rivers for water supply and agricultural benefits.
 
• Other examples include the Nile Valley in Egypt, which thrived due to the fertile land provided by the Nile River.
 
• Building materials like mud bricks and stones were essential in determining settlement locations.
 
 
 
• **Technological advancements in urban planning:**
 
 
• Tools like **GIS** and satellite imaging allow planners to analyze geographical data effectively.
 
• Technologies like IoT (Internet of Things) are being employed in smart city initiatives to manage resources efficiently.
 
• Energy-efficient planning, renewable resources, and green architecture are modern technological trends shaping urban settlements.
 
 
 
• **Examples of modern urban planning:**
 
 
• **Masdar City** in the UAE is a sustainable urban settlement utilizing advanced technology.
 
• Indian initiatives like the **Smart Cities Mission** focus on modernizing urban areas with technology-driven infrastructure.
 
• China's **Xiong'an New Area** is a planned smart city integrating advanced technology for urban development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key differences between historical and modern urban settlement factors:**

 
 
• Historical factors included **natural resources**, **fertile land**, and **water supply**.
 
• Modern factors emphasize **technology**, **connectivity**, and **economic opportunities**.
 
• Historical settlements were primarily influenced by survival needs, whereas modern settlements are shaped by technological and economic progress.
 
 
 
• **Role of technology in urban development:**
 
 
• Technological tools enable efficient planning, resource allocation, and disaster management in urban centers.
 
• Advancements in renewable energy and green infrastructure are shaping sustainable urban settlements.
 
• Examples include the use of **solar energy**, **energy-efficient architecture**, and **automated transportation systems**.
 
 
 
• **Historical examples:**
 
 
• Ancient cities like Babylon, Rome, and Athens developed based on water sources, fertile lands, and construction resources.
 
• In India, cities like Varanasi and Jaipur were influenced by trade routes and natural resources.

question: Which of the following ancient Indian sites is famous for its chaityas and viharas carved into rock?

__
 
• The **Ajanta Caves** are located in the **Aurangabad district** of **Maharashtra** and comprise about **30 rock-cut Buddhist monuments** excavated into a **basaltic horseshoe-shaped cliff**.
 
• These caves were developed in two phases, starting from the **2nd century BCE** (**Satavahana period**) and continuing to the **5th and 6th centuries CE** (**Vakataka period**).
 
• The site is categorized into two main types of structures: **Chaityas**, which served as **prayer halls** containing a stupa, and **Viharas**, which were **monastic residential quarters** for monks.
 
• The **Chaitya halls** (such as Caves 9, 10, 19, and 26) feature vaulted ceilings and polished stone, while the **Viharas** consist of central halls surrounded by sleeping cells.
 
• The caves are famous for their **mural paintings** and sculptures that depict scenes from the **Jataka tales** and the various lives of **Gautama Buddha**.

• Located in **Tamil Nadu**, it was the capital of the **Medieval Cholas** and is home to the **Brihadisvara Temple**, built by **Raja Raja Chola I**.
 
 
 
• **Mahabalipuram**:
 
 
• Situated in **Tamil Nadu**, it is known for **Pallava rock-cut architecture**, including the **Pancha Rathas** and the **Shore Temple**, but it is primarily a Hindu site.
 
 
 
• **Hampi**:
 
 
• Located in **Karnataka**, it served as the capital of the **Vijayanagara Empire** and features structural temples like the **Virupaksha Temple** and the **Stone Chariot** at **Vittala Temple**.

question: The First Jain Council was convened at Pataliputra by whom?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sthulabahu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **First Jain Council** was convened at **Pataliputra** (modern-day Patna) during the reign of King Chandragupta Maurya.
 
• The council was held under the leadership of **Sthulabahu**, who was one of the prominent Jain monks of that period.
 
• The primary objective of the council was to compile and preserve Jain teachings and scriptures after the departure of Jain monks to different regions.
 
• This council led to the division of Jainism into two major sects: **Svetambara** (white-clad) and **Digambara** (sky-clad).
 
• **Sthulabahu** played a significant role in organizing the Jain monks and ensuring that teachings were documented to avoid loss of the original doctrines.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Jain Councils:**

 
 
• There were two major Jain Councils in history, the first at **Pataliputra** under **Sthulabahu** and the second at **Valabhi**.
 
• The **Second Jain Council** at Valabhi was convened by Jain monks under the leadership of **Devardhi Kshamashramana** in the 5th century CE.
 
 
 
• **Division of Jainism:**
 
 
• The division into **Svetambara** and **Digambara** sects occurred due to differences in practices, particularly regarding clothing and ascetic lifestyle.
 
• The **Svetambara sect** believed in wearing white clothes, while the **Digambara sect** practiced nudity as a symbol of complete renunciation.
 
 
 
• **Jain Scriptures:**
 
 
• The Jain texts compiled during the councils are known as **Agamas**, which are the canonical scriptures of Jainism.
 
• These texts contain teachings of Lord Mahavira and earlier Tirthankaras.
 
 
 
• **Historical Context:**
 
 
• King Chandragupta Maurya, a patron of Jainism, played a significant role in supporting Jain monks and their endeavors.
 
• Jainism flourished during his reign, and the council at Pataliputra marked an important milestone in preserving Jain doctrines.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Sthulabahu:**

 
 
• He is recognized as a significant Jain monk who played a pivotal role in organizing the First Jain Council.
 
• His leadership ensured the preservation of Jain teachings during a period of expansion and migration of Jain monks.
 
 
 
• **Pataliputra:**
 
 
• Pataliputra was a major center of religious and cultural activities during the Mauryan Empire.
 
• It served as the venue for several significant religious councils, including those of Jainism and Buddhism.
 
 
 
• **Jainism's Historical Contributions:**
 
 
• Jainism emphasizes non-violence (**Ahimsa**), truth (**Satya**), and asceticism as central principles.
 
• The preservation of Jain teachings through councils helped maintain the faith's relevance and spread across India.

question: What kind of architectural feature are the Jain temples known for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Highly intricate marble carvings**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jain architecture** is renowned for its superlative use of **white marble**, featuring carvings so delicate and precise they are often compared to **fine lace** or ivory work.
 
• The **Dilwara Temples** on **Mount Abu** in **Rajasthan**, constructed between the **11th and 13th centuries CE**, serve as the most prominent examples of this **intricate marble craftsmanship**.
 
• The **Ranakpur Jain Temple** in the **Pali district** is another architectural marvel, featuring **1,444 uniquely carved marble pillars** where no two pillars share the same design.
 
• Architectural elements such as **ceilings**, **doorways**, and **toranas** (arches) are decorated with complex **floral motifs**, **geometric patterns**, and figures of **Vidyadevis** (goddesses of knowledge).
 
• The use of **Makrana marble** allowed artisans to achieve a level of **translucent detailing** and deep undercutting that is rare in other temple architectures of **India**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Maru-Gurjara Architecture:**

 
 
• This style originated in **Western India** (Gujarat and Rajasthan) and is characterized by its focus on **structural ornamentation** and **sculptural beauty**.
 
• It emphasizes the **Shikhara** (temple spire) and the **Mandapa** (pillared hall) as central aesthetic components.
 
 
 
• **Gothic vaults and arches:**
 
 
• These are defining features of **European Medieval architecture**, utilizing **pointed arches** and **flying buttresses**, which are absent in traditional Jain structures.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with other styles:**
 
 
• While **Chola architecture** is known for massive **stone structures** and **bronze icons**, and **Indo-Islamic architecture** features **large domes**, Jain architecture remains distinct through its **micro-level marble ornamentation**.

question: Who among the following Mauryan king fasted to death and died at Shravanabelagola?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **Chandragupta Maurya.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chandragupta** lived as an ascetic at **Shravanabelagola** for several years before fasting to death as per the practice of sallekhana, according to the Digambara legend.
 
• **Chandragupta** was the founder of the **Mauryan dynasty **(reigned c. 321–c. 297 BCE) and the first emperor to unify most of India under one administration.
 
• He is credited with saving the country from maladministration and freeing it from foreign domination.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

**Bindusara - **

 
• Bindusara, also known as Bindusara Maurya, was the 2nd Mauryan emperor, who seized the throne in 297 BCE.
 
• He was a Greek Amitrochates (b.c 320 BCE—died 272/3 BCE).
 
• According to Greek historians, he was known as Amitrochates, which is derived from the Sanskrit word amitraghata, which means “destroyer of opponents.”

**Dasharatha - **

 
• Dasaratha Maurya, grandson of Ashoka the Great, ruled as the fourth emperor of the Mauryan Empire from 232 BCE to 224 BCE. Here's a detailed breakdown of his reign:
 
• **Background:**
 
 
• Ascended the throne after his grandfather, Ashoka.
 
• Unlike Ashoka, who was known for his military conquests before embracing Buddhism, Dasaratha's reign is associated with the decline of the Mauryan Empire.
 
 
 
• **Challenges during his reign:**
 
 
• Loss of Territories: Several regions of the vast Mauryan Empire declared independence during Dasaratha's rule. This weakened the empire's central authority.
 
• Limited Ability: Historians believe Dasaratha may not have possessed the strong leadership qualities needed to hold the empire together.
 
 
 
• **Positive aspects:**
 
 
• Continued Ashoka's Policies: Dasaratha is known for upholding the social and religious policies established by his grandfather, particularly the promotion of Dharma (righteousness) and non-violence.
 
• Patronage of Ajivikas: Inscriptions in the Barabar Caves suggest Dasaratha may have patronized the Ajivika sect, a non-vedic philosophical tradition that existed alongside Buddhism during that period.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Dasaratha's reign is considered a turning point in Mauryan history. The decline of the empire that began under him continued in the following years.
 
• He was the last Mauryan emperor to leave behind epigraphical evidence (inscriptions) of his rule.
 
• Dasaratha's successor was his cousin, Samprati, who attempted to revive the empire.
 
 
 
• **Ashoka - **
 
 
• Ashoka the Great (r. 268-232 BCE) was the third king of the Mauryan Empire (322-185 BCE)
 
• He is best known for his renunciation of war, development of the concept of dhamma (pious social conduct), and promotion of Buddhism as well as his effective reign of a nearly pan-Indian political entity.

question: What is the classical feature of Ashokan pillars? Greitas zivitat amestu fatuan aur 8?

options.text: They had capitals topped with lion sculptures.
They were only found in South India.
They were made of bronze and silver.

solution:
The correct answer is __**They had capitals topped with lion sculptures.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Ashokan pillars are a series of monolithic stone columns built during the reign of Emperor Ashoka, who ruled the Maurya Empire from 268–232 BCE.
 
• A defining feature of these pillars is their capitals, which are often topped with sculptures of animals, most famously lions, symbolizing strength, courage, and the spread of Dharma.
 
• The most renowned example is the Lion Capital of Ashoka at Sarnath, which features four lions seated back-to-back and serves as the national emblem of India today.
 
• The pillars were also inscribed with Ashoka's edicts, which communicated ethical and moral principles rooted in Buddhism.
 
• The Ashokan pillars were masterfully crafted using highly polished sandstone, showcasing exceptional Mauryan artistry and craftsmanship.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: They were only found in South India.**
 
 
• This is incorrect as Ashokan pillars were primarily located in northern and central India, including regions like Bihar, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, and Gujarat.
 
• They were strategically placed near important trade routes, cities, and sites of Buddhist significance to ensure Ashoka's messages reached a wide audience.
 
• South India, while influenced by Ashokan policies, does not have any known Ashokan pillars.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: They were made of bronze and silver.**
 
 
• This is incorrect as Ashokan pillars were constructed from sandstone, not metals like bronze or silver.
 
• The sandstone used was often sourced from quarries in Chunar (Uttar Pradesh) or Mathura and transported to the pillar sites.
 
• The smooth polish and intricate carvings on these pillars highlight the technological advancements of the Mauryan era.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: They served as fire altars.**
 
 
• This is incorrect as the purpose of Ashokan pillars was not religious rituals involving fire but rather to disseminate the principles of Dhamma (moral law).
 
• The inscriptions on the pillars emphasized non-violence, respect for all living beings, and the promotion of social harmony.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: Ashokan Pillars**
 
 
• The Ashokan pillars are among the earliest known examples of monumental stone art in India.
 
• They reflect Emperor Ashoka's adoption of Buddhism and his efforts to propagate its principles through visual and textual means.
 
• These pillars remain an enduring symbol of India's cultural and historical heritage.

question: In which of the following languages did Amoghavarsha write Kavirajamarga?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kannada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Kavirajamarga 

 
 
• **Kavirajamarga **is the earliest available work on** rhetoric, poetics, and grammar in the Kannada language.**
 
• It was inspired by or written in part by the famous** Rashtrakuta King Amoghavarsha I,** and some historians claim it is based partly on the **Sanskrit text Kavyadarsha.**
 
• Some historians believe Kavirajamarga may have** been co-authored by a poet in the king's court, the Kannada language theorist Sri Vijaya.**
 
• The name literally means **"Royal Path for Poets" **and was written as a guide book for poets and scholars (Kavishiksha).
 
• From references made in this writing to earlier **Kannada poetry and literature, **it is clear that a considerable body of work in prose and poetry must have existed in the preceding centuries.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Amoghvarsha (814-878):

 
 
• ​He was one of the greatest Rashtrakuta rulers and the successor of Govind III.
 
• He set up a new capital at Manyakheta (now Malkhed in Karnataka state).
 
• He preferred literature and religion over war.
 
• Kavirajamarga in Kannada and Prashnottara Ratnamalika in Sanskrit are famous literary works by him.
 
• Amoghavarsha patronized Jainism, Buddhism, and Hinduism.
 
• He was converted to Jainism by Jinasena, a Jain monk.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Indo Greeks.

1. The most celebrated Indo-Greek ruler was Menander.

2. Menander has been identified with King Milinda mentioned in the famous Buddhist text Milindapanho.

3. Milindapanho contains philosophical questions that Milinda asked Amrapali.

4. Impressed by the answers, King Milinda accepted Buddhism as his religion. Which among the above statements are correct.
solution:
The Correct Answer is **Only 1, 2 and 4.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Menander, a celebrated Indo-Greek ruler
 
 
• Hence **statement 1 is correct.**
 
 
 
• He is indeed identified with King Milinda in the Buddhist text Milindapanho
 
 
• Hence **statement 2 is correct.**
 
 
 
• In which records philosophical dialogues between King Milinda and the monk Nagasena, not Amrapali.
 
 
• Hence **statement 3 is incorrect.**
 
 
 
• These discussions led King Milinda to embrace Buddhism, showcasing the historical intertwining of Greek and Buddhist cultures.
 
 
• Hence **statement 4 is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Indo-Greek Kingdom**, or Graeco-Indian Kingdom, also known historically as the Yavana Kingdom, was a Hellenistic-era Greek kingdom covering various parts of Afghanistan, the northwest regions of the Indian subcontinent, (all of present Pakistan), and a small part of Iran; from 180 B.C.E. to around 10 C.E.
 
• The kingdom began when the Greco-Bactrian king **Demetrius invaded India in 180 B.C.E**., ultimately creating an entity that seceded from the powerful **Greco-Bactrian Kingdom** centred in Bactria.

question: Pulakeshin II belonged to which of the following dynasties?

The correct answer is **__Chalukya Dynasty.__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Chalukya dynasty **ruled large parts of **Southern and central India **between the 6th and 12th centuries.
 
• The dynasty is divided into three distinct yet related branches:
 
 
• The **Badami Chalukyas (Early Chalukyas) **(543 to 753) CE.
 
• The **Eastern Chalukyas **(624 to 1070) CE.
 
• The **Western Chalukyas (Later Chalukyas) **(973 to 1189) CE.
 
 
 
• The temple architecture in Badami, Aihole and Pattadakal (a UNESCO World Heritage site) was constructed by Chalukyas.
 
• They supported Hinduism primarily, but significant Jain influences can be seen during their tenure.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

subject: GK
question: Which among the following statements is NOT true about Kanishka?

options.text: He patronized Buddhist scholars Vasumitra, Asvagosha and Nagarjuna.
He convened the Fourth Buddhist Council.
Kanishka was succeeded by his son Vasudeva.
The famous physician Charaka was patronized by him.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Kanishka was succeeded by his son Vasudeva.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Kanishka was not succeeded by his son Vasudeva. Instead, Vasudeva I was another ruler of the Kushana dynasty who ruled after Kanishka's successors.
 
• There is no historical evidence to suggest that Kanishka was directly succeeded by Vasudeva as his son. Historical records indicate a series of rulers following Kanishka before Vasudeva came to power.
 
• Vasudeva I was the last prominent ruler of the Kushana dynasty, and his reign marked the decline of the empire.
 
• The confusion arises because Vasudeva is often associated with the late Kushana rule, but he was not a direct successor of Kanishka.
 
• Historians rely on inscriptions and coins from the era to reconstruct the succession of Kushana rulers, and these records do not support the claim that Kanishka was succeeded by his son Vasudeva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kanishka's patronage of Buddhist scholars (Option 1):**

 
 
• Kanishka was a great patron of Buddhism and supported prominent Buddhist scholars such as Vasumitra, Asvaghosa, and Nagarjuna.
 
• Asvaghosa was a renowned poet and philosopher who composed "Buddhacharita," a biography of Buddha.
 
• Nagarjuna is credited with founding the Madhyamaka school of Mahayana Buddhism and made significant contributions to Buddhist philosophy.
 
• Vasumitra presided over the Fourth Buddhist Council under Kanishka's rule.
 
 
 
• **Fourth Buddhist Council (Option 2):**
 
 
• Kanishka convened the Fourth Buddhist Council in Kundalvana (present-day Kashmir), which played a significant role in the development of Mahayana Buddhism.
 
• The council was presided over by Vasumitra and co-chaired by Asvaghosa.
 
• It was during this council that Mahayana Buddhism was formally codified, and significant Buddhist texts were compiled and translated into Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Charaka's association with Kanishka (Option 4):**
 
 
• Charaka, the famous ancient physician and author of "Charaka Samhita," is believed to have been patronized by Kanishka.
 
• Charaka Samhita is one of the foundational texts of Ayurveda and focuses on internal medicine.
 
• Under Kanishka's patronage, Charaka made significant contributions to the field of medicine, including advancements in healthcare and surgery.

question: Dakshinchitra was compiled during the reign of which Pallava ruler?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahendravarman I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dakshinchitra** is an ancient treatise or a commentary on the art of **painting** that provides insights into the aesthetic traditions of early **South India**.
 
• The work was compiled under the royal patronage of the **Pallava** ruler **Mahendravarman I**, who reigned from approximately **600 to 630 CE**.
 
• **Mahendravarman I** was a great scholar and artist, often referred to by the title **Chitrakarapuli** (Tiger among painters) due to his profound mastery and promotion of the fine arts.
 
• He was also known as **Vichitrachitta** (Curious-minded), reflecting his innovative approach to temple architecture, specifically the introduction of **rock-cut temples** in the **Tamil** country, such as the **Mandagapattu** temple.
 
• His interest in documentation and theory led to the compilation of **Dakshinchitra**, which served as a significant reference for the **Pallava** style of mural painting, remnants of which can be found in **Sittannavasal**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Narasimhavarman I**:

 
 
• He was the son and successor of **Mahendravarman I**, famously known as **Mamalla** (the great wrestler).
 
• He is credited with the creation of the monolithic **Rathas** and the shore temple complex at **Mahabalipuram**.
 
• He achieved a major military victory over the **Chalukya** king **Pulakeshin II**, earning the title **Vatapikonda**.
 
 
 
• **Sivaskandavarman**:
 
 
• He was an early ruler of the **Pallava Dynasty** during the 4th century CE.
 
• He is known from the **Hirahadagalli** and **Mayidavolu** inscriptions and is recognized for performing **Vedic** sacrifices like the **Ashvamedha**.
 
 
 
• **Vijayaskandavarman**:
 
 
• Another early **Pallava** monarch who contributed to the consolidation of the kingdom before the rise of the **Imperial Pallavas**.

question: The Garuda pillar at Besnagar was erected by:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Heliodorus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Garuda pillar at Besnagar**, also known as the **Heliodorus Pillar**, is one of the earliest known examples of an Indian pillar erected by a foreigner.
 
• It was erected by **Heliodorus**, a Greek ambassador from the court of **Antialcidas**, the Indo-Greek king of Taxila, around the **2nd century BCE**.
 
• The pillar was dedicated to **Vasudeva (Vishnu)**, showcasing the influence of Vaishnavism during that period.
 
• Heliodorus inscribed the pillar with a dedication, in Brahmi script, which explains that he was a devotee of Vasudeva and commissioned the pillar to honor him.
 
• This pillar is located in **Vidisha (Besnagar)**, Madhya Pradesh, and is a significant archaeological site for understanding the cultural and religious exchange between Greeks and Indians during ancient times.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Heliodorus and His Significance:**

 
 
• Heliodorus was a Greek ambassador sent by Antialcidas, a ruler of the Indo-Greek kingdom, to the court of the Shunga king **Bhagabhadra**.
 
• The inscription on the Garuda pillar is one of the earliest records of a foreigner adopting Indian religious practices, specifically Vaishnavism.
 
• The pillar inscription refers to Heliodorus as a **Bhagavata**, indicating his devotion to Vasudeva (an early form of Vishnu).
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features of the Garuda Pillar:**
 
 
• The pillar is topped with a **Garuda**, the mythical bird and vehicle of Vishnu, symbolizing the deity's presence.
 
• It is made of sandstone and stands approximately **6.7 meters** tall.
 
• The pillar inscription is written in Brahmi script and Prakrit language, emphasizing its historical and linguistic importance.
 
 
 
• **Influence of Indo-Greek Culture:**
 
 
• The erection of the Garuda pillar symbolizes the cultural and religious interactions between the Greeks and Indians during the Indo-Greek period.
 
• It highlights the spread and acceptance of Indian religions, particularly Vaishnavism, beyond its native followers.
 
 
 
• **Other Options Explanation:**
 
 
• **Menander:** Menander I (Milinda) was an Indo-Greek king known for embracing Buddhism, not Vaishnavism. He is associated with the Buddhist text **Milinda Panha**.
 
• **Pushyamitra Sunga:** Pushyamitra Sunga was the founder of the Sunga dynasty, known for his patronage of Hinduism, but he had no connection to the Garuda pillar.
 
• **Kanishka:** Kanishka, the Kushan emperor, was a prominent patron of Buddhism and had no link to the Garuda pillar.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Garuda pillar** is a testimony to the early spread of **Vaishnavism** and its acceptance by people from different cultures.
 
• This inscription is one of the **earliest known inscriptions** in India that confirms the worship of Vasudeva as a supreme deity.
 
• The pillar serves as an example of the fusion of **Greek and Indian cultures**, particularly during the Indo-Greek period in Indian history.
 
• It provides valuable insights into the religious and diplomatic relations during the **2nd century BCE**.

question: Vichitrachitta, Chitrakarapuli, and Chaityakari are the titles given to which of the following rulers?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahendravarman I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Mahendravarman I** was a ruler of the Pallava dynasty in South India, reigning from approximately **600 CE to 630 CE**. He was a significant patron of arts and architecture.
 
• He was bestowed with titles such as **Vichitrachitta** (curious-minded), **Chitrakarapuli** (tiger among artists), and **Chaityakari** (temple builder) due to his contributions to temple architecture and his innovative mind.
 
• Mahendravarman I introduced the **rock-cut architecture** style in South India, which marked the beginning of the Dravidian style of temple construction. His creations are evident in places like **Mahabalipuram**.
 
• Under his reign, the Pallava dynasty saw significant developments in **art, literature, and culture**. He was also a playwright and musician, authoring works like **Mattavilasa Prahasana**, a Sanskrit play.
 
• Mahendravarman I was initially a Jain but later converted to **Shaivism**, which influenced his temple-building activities dedicated to Lord Shiva.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Mahendravarman I's Contributions:**

 
 
• He is credited with constructing some of the earliest examples of **rock-cut temples** in South India, such as the **Mandagapattu temple** in Tamil Nadu, which is dedicated to the Hindu trinity (Brahma, Vishnu, and Shiva).
 
• The temples built during his period reflect a transition from wooden structures to **stone architecture**, showcasing durability and artistic intricacies.
 
 
 
• **Other Titles of Mahendravarman I:**
 
 
• Vichitrachitta (curious-minded): Reflects his intellectual curiosity and innovation in art and architecture.
 
• Chitrakarapuli (tiger among artists): Highlights his exceptional artistic abilities and patronage of art.
 
• Chaityakari (temple builder): Points to his pioneering contributions to temple construction.
 
 
 
• **Pallava Dynasty:**
 
 
• The Pallavas ruled parts of South India between the **3rd and 9th centuries CE**.
 
• They are renowned for their contributions to **Dravidian architecture**, particularly in Mahabalipuram and Kanchipuram.
 
 
 
• **Other Rulers in the Options:**
 
 
• **Kirtivarman I:** A ruler of the Chalukya dynasty; he is not associated with the titles mentioned in the question.
 
• **Narasimhavarman II:** A Pallava king known for his architectural contributions but not associated with the specific titles mentioned.
 
• **Parantaka I:** A Chola king known for his military conquests and temple-building activities but not linked to the given titles.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Mattavilasa Prahasana:** This satirical play written by Mahendravarman I mocks religious hypocrisy and the confusion among religious sects of his time.
 
• **Conversion to Shaivism:** His conversion from Jainism to Shaivism had a significant impact on his patronage of Shaivite temples and art.
 
• **Legacy:** Mahendravarman I's architectural innovations laid the groundwork for later Pallava kings, such as Narasimhavarman I, who further expanded the temple-building tradition.

question: Who was the last ruler of the Sunga Dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Devabhuti**__.

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devabhuti**, also known as **Devabhumi**, was the **tenth** and the **last ruler** of the **Sunga Dynasty**, reigning from approximately **83 BCE** to **73 BCE**.
 
• According to the **Puranic** texts and the **Harshacharita** written by **Banabhatta**, Devabhuti was described as a weak and dissolute ruler who was overly fond of the company of women, leading to his downfall.
 
• His reign came to a violent end in **73 BCE** when he was assassinated by his own minister, **Vasudeva Kanva**. This event marked the total collapse of the **Sunga Empire** and the rise of the **Kanva Dynasty** in **Magadha**.
 
• The **Sunga Dynasty** overall lasted for about **112 years**, serving as a critical period for the revival of **Brahmanical traditions** and the patronage of art and architecture, notably the expansion of the **Sanchi Stupa** and the **Bharhut Stupa**.

 **Additional Information__**

 
• **Vasudeva**
 
 
• He was the **Amatya** (minister) of Devabhuti who orchestrated the king's murder to seize the throne.
 
• He founded the **Kanva Dynasty**, which ruled for a short period of approximately **45 years**.
 
 
 
• **Pushyamitra Sunga**
 
 
• He was the **founder** of the Sunga Dynasty and the **Senapati** (Commander-in-Chief) of the last Mauryan King, **Brihadratha**.
 
• He ascended the throne in **185 BCE** and is famous for performing two **Ashvamedha Yagyas** (horse sacrifices) to assert his imperial authority.
 
 
 
• **Agnimitra**
 
 
• The son of Pushyamitra Sunga, he served as the **second ruler** of the dynasty and was previously the **Viceroy of Vidisha**.
 
• He is the central protagonist of **Kalidasa's** first Sanskrit play, **Malavikagnimitram**, which depicts his love for the princess **Malavika**.

solution:
__

The correct answer is __**Rashtrakutas**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Tripartite Struggle**, also known as the** Kannauj Triangle Wars,** unfolded in the 9th century as a fierce conflict between three powerful empires: the Gurjara-Pratihara Empire, the Pala Empire, and the Rashtrakuta Empire.
 
• These empires vied for control over the Gangetic region in northern India, with the pivotal battleground being the fertile area of Kannauj.
 
• The Rashtrakutas, initially feudatories of the Chalukyas, established their dominance and had their capital at Manyakheta or Malkhed near Sholapur.
 
• They emerged victorious in the Tripartite Struggle, defeating both the Palas and the Pratiharas, thereby consolidating their influence over the region.
 
• This conflict marked a significant chapter in Indian history, shaping the political landscape of northern India during the medieval period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Rashtrakutas **were a prominent Indian dynasty that held sway over extensive territories across the Indian subcontinent from the 6th to the 10th centuries CE.
 
• The earliest known Rashtrakuta inscription dates back to the 7th century, recorded on a copper plate grant that delineates their authority from Manapur, a city located in Central or West India.
 
• Additional inscriptions from the same era mention other Rashtrakuta rulers, including those of Achalapur and Kannauj.
 
• Despite their historical significance, controversies persist regarding the origins of the early Rashtrakutas, their native homeland, and even their language.
 
• Scholars continue to explore various theories and hypotheses to shed light on these aspects of Rashtrakuta history, contributing to ongoing debates within the field of Indian history and archaeology.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Maratha Empire** was a significant Indian power in the early modern era and later evolved into a confederation that governed large swathes of the Indian subcontinent during the 18th century.
 
• **The Cholas** are remembered as one of the longest-reigning dynasties in southern India.
 
• **The Chera dynasty, **a Hindu dynasty from the Sangam age, unified various regions along the western coast and western ghats of southern India to establish the early Chera empire.

• The **Kadai Yelu Vallalgal**, also known as the **Seven Last Patrons** of the **Sangam Era**, were celebrated chieftains known for their extraordinary **philanthropy** and support for **Tamil poets**.
 
• The seven patrons include **Pari**, **Pegan**, **Kari**, **Ay**, **Adiyaman**, **Nalli**, and **Ory**. They were independent rulers of hilly regions who prioritized welfare and art over territorial expansion.
 
• **Nediyon** is not part of this specific group. The name **Nediyon** is often associated with the early **Pandyan Dynasty** kings, specifically **Nilantharu Thiruvir Pandyan**, or used as a poetic reference to a tall, primordial king in **Tamil literature**.

• **Adiyaman**: Also known as **Adiyaman Neduman Anchi** of **Tagadur**, he gifted a rare, immortality-granting **Black Gooseberry (Nelli)** to the renowned poetess **Avvaiyar**.
 
• **Pegan**: The chieftain of the **Aavi** tribe in the **Palani Hills**, he was moved by a shivering **peacock** and covered it with his expensive silk shawl.

question: Which of the following were **NOT **a part of a citadel in Harrapan architecture?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Residential buildings for masses.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

**The most interesting urban feature of the Harappan civilization is its town planning.**

 
• The citadel contains** large structures **which might have functioned as administrative or ritual centres.
 
• In some cities of the Indus Valley Civilization, special buildings were constructed on the citadel.
 
 
• For example, in Mohenjodaro, a very special tank, which archaeologists call the Great Bath, was built in the citadel area.
 
• Perhaps important people took a dip in this tank on special occasions.
 
• Other cities, such as Kalibangan and Lothal had fire altars, where sacrifices may have been performed.
 
• And some cities like Mohenjodaro, Harappa, and Lothal had elaborate storehouses.
 
 
 
• The **residential buildings are built in the lower town. Hence they are not part of the citadel.**
 
• The streets intersect each other at right angles in a criss-cross pattern.
 
• It divides the city into several **residential blocks**. The main street is connected by narrow lanes.
 
• The doors of the houses opened in these lanes and not the main streets.
 
• The houses of common people, however, differed in size from **single-room houses in Harappa to bigger structures**. The houses were largely built of **burnt bricks.**

question: Mohenjodaro site of Harappan civilisation is situated on the bank of which river?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indus river**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Mohenjo-daro **is situated on the right (west) bank of the lower** Indus River **in **Larkana District**, **Sindh, Pakistan**.
 
• Positioned on a Pleistocene ridge within the floodplain of the Indus, it lies approximately 28 kilometres (17 mi) from the town of Larkana.
 
• This archaeological site, built **around 2500 BCE**, represents the largest settlement of the **ancient Indus Valley Civilization **and stands as one of the earliest major cities in the world.
 
• It flourished contemporaneously with civilizations in ancient Egypt, Mesopotamia, Minoan Crete, and Norte Chico.
 
• Mohenjo-daro remained undiscovered until the 1920s, and since then, extensive excavation has been carried out at the site.
 
• In recognition of its historical significance, Mohenjo-daro was designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 1980, marking it as the first such site in South Asia.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Indus River** is a** transboundary river** spanning across Asia, serving as a vital waterway in **South and Central Asia**.
 
• Stretching over 3,120 kilometers (1,940 mi), the river originates from mountain springs northeast of Mount Kailash in Western Tibet.
 
• It then traverses northwestward through the disputed region of Kashmir before sharply bending to the left beyond the Nanga Parbat massif.
 
• Continuing its course, the river flows south-by-southwest through Pakistan, ultimately reaching the Arabian Sea near the port city of Karachi.

subject: GK
question: Which among the following statements is TRUE about the Rig Vedic Society?

options.text: The Rig Vedic society was matrilineal.
The head of the family was known as Vishaypati.
Apala, Visvavara, Ghosa, and Lopamudra were prominent women poets of the Rig Vedic period.
Child marriage and the practice of Sati were prevalent.

solution:
The correct answer is __**Apala, Visvavara, Ghosa, and Lopamudra were prominent women poets of the Rig Vedic period.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rig Vedic society** was primarily **patriarchal** (patrilineal) in nature, where the eldest male member or father held authority over the family unit. Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.
 
• The basic unit of society was the **Kula** (family). The head of the family was known as the **Kulapa** or **Grihapati**, whereas the **Vishaypati** was the head of a **Vish** (a group of villages). Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.
 
• Women in the **Early Vedic period** enjoyed a high status and were provided opportunities for spiritual and intellectual development. Renowned female scholars like **Apala**, **Visvavara**, **Ghosa**, and **Lopamudra** attained the status of **Rishis** and composed several hymns in the **Rig Veda**. Hence, statement 3 is correct.
 
• Social evils like **child marriage** and the custom of **Sati** were generally non-existent during this era. Girls were married only after attaining maturity, and they often had a say in choosing their life partners. Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Administrative Hierarchy**:

 
 
• **Kula**: The smallest unit, headed by the **Kulapa**.
 
• **Grama**: A collection of families, headed by the **Gramani**.
 
• **Vish**: A tribal division composed of several villages, led by the **Vishaypati**.
 
• **Jana**: The highest political or tribal unit, ruled by the **Rajan** (King).
 
 
 
• **Position of Women**:
 
 
• Women were allowed to attend assemblies like the **Sabha** and **Vidatha**.
 
• The practice of **Niyoga** (widow remarriage) was permitted, especially if the woman was childless.
 
• They were entitled to undergo the **Upanayana** ceremony and receive an education.
 
 
 
• **Social Practices**:
 
 
• The society was divided into four **Varnas** (Brahmins, Kshatriyas, Vaishyas, and Shudras), but the system was flexible and based on occupation rather than birth during the **Early Vedic** stage.
 
• Monogamy was the standard, although **polygyny** was sometimes practiced by the nobility and **Rishis**.

__
 
• **Manipuri dance,** a classical dance form originating from the **northeastern Indian state of Manipur,** draws its inspiration from the divine love tales of Radha and Krishna, commonly known as **Rasleela themes**.
 
• This dance form is renowned for its grace, fluid movements, and intricate costumes, which collectively evoke the essence of devotion and the playful spirit of Lord Krishna.
 
• Embedded within Manipuri dance is a deep connection to Vaishnavism, a Hindu religious tradition that reveres Lord Vishnu and his incarnations, particularly Krishna. As such, the dance serves as a manifestation of religious and philosophical ideals, reflecting the spiritual beliefs of the Manipuri people.
 
• Rasleelas, performances depicting the divine love of Radha and Krishna, hold special significance in Manipuri culture and are often showcased during festivals.
 
• Through these performances, Manipuri dance not only celebrates the rich cultural heritage of the region but also serves as a means of spiritual expression and devotion to the divine.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sattriya dance,** a classical dance form originating from Assam, revolves around Vaishnavite themes, distinguishing it from Manipuri Rasleela.
 
• **Mohiniyattam, **a classical dance form native to Kerala, is celebrated for its graceful and feminine movements, often depicting themes of love and devotion. 
 
• **Kathak,** a classical dance form from North India, incorporates stories of Radha and Krishna alongside various other themes.

• **Alarmel Valli **is an Indian classical dancer and choreographer and a foremost exponent of the **Pandanallur style** dance form of **Bharatanatyam**. 
 
• She established The Dipasikha Dance Foundation in Chennai in 1984, where she imparts training in Bharatanatyam.
 
• In 1991, Alarmel Valli became the second youngest dancer to receive the Padma Shri from the Government of India, following Vyjayanthimala.
 
• She was honored with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2001 by India's National Academy for Music, Dance, and Drama.

• This style is esteemed for its intricate choreography, including the renowned Nine or Ten Tanjore Quartet pada-varnams.
 
• Pillai, credited with the choreography of these masterpieces, introduced distinctive hand gestures known as "hands" and also crafted the adavu choreography for the swara passages.

• **Kuchipudi, from Andhra Pradesh**
 
• **Manipuri, from Manipur**
 
• **Mohiniyattam, from Kerala**
 
• **Odissi, from Odisha**
 
• **Sattriya, from Assam**
 
 
 
• The Indian Ministry of Culture additionally includes Chhau, from Eastern India (Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal), making a total of nine recognized classical dance styles.

• **Bharatanatyam, **a classical dance form from **Tamil Nadu,** traces its roots to the ancient dance known as **Sadir Attam.**
 
• Originally called** Sadir or Dasi Attam**, Bharatanatyam evolved from the** temple dance tradition of Sadir Attam.**
 
• **E Krishna Iyer and Rukmini Devi Arundale **played key roles in transforming Sadir into Bharatanatyam, particularly by refining the Pandanallur style of dance.
 
• The name Bharatanatyam translates to "the pure form." Historically, Sadir Attam was performed by Devadasis, meaning "Servants of God." However, in modern Tamil, the term "Devar-Adiyar" is often used derogatorily, equating it with "prostitute."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• **Kuchipudi **is a dance-drama performance originating from the village of Kuchipudi in Andhra Pradesh, India. It is one of the eight major classical dances of India, acknowledged by the Sangeet Natak Akademi and the Ministry of Culture.
 
• **Mohiniyattam** is an Indian classical dance form originating from the state of Kerala.
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical Indian dance-drama form with a history spanning 300 years, originating in Kerala in the 17th century.

• **Ammannur Madhava Chakyar **was a revered exponent of** Kutiyattam,** a traditional **Sanskrit theatrical art** form originating from **Kerala**.

subject: GK
question: What is the predominant theme of Manipuri dance?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Devotion and love**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Manipuri dance**, also known as Jagoi, primarily revolves around themes of devotion and love, especially the divine love of Lord Krishna and Radha.
 
• It is a classical dance form originating from the northeastern Indian state of Manipur, deeply intertwined with spiritual and religious traditions.
 
• The dance is inspired by the **Vaishnavism tradition**, which emphasizes the worship and adoration of Lord Krishna.
 
• Manipuri dance performances often depict stories from the **Bhagavata Purana**, focusing on Krishna's playful and divine interactions, including the Raslila.
 
• The movements of Manipuri dance are soft, graceful, and fluid, symbolizing devotion and purity, with performers often portraying the mood of Bhakti (devotion).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **War and victory**

 
 
• This theme is not central to Manipuri dance but is often found in folk dance forms or martial arts-inspired performances like Chhau or Kalaripayattu, which emphasize bravery, physical strength, and combat.
 
• Chhau dance, for example, incorporates battle themes and heroic tales, showcasing vigorous and athletic movements.
 
 
 
• **Celebration of harvest**
 
 
• While Manipuri dance does not focus on harvest celebrations, several Indian folk dances like Bihu (Assam), Ghoomar (Rajasthan), and Garba (Gujarat) represent agrarian themes and harvest festivities.
 
• These dances celebrate community bonding, agricultural prosperity, and seasonal changes through vibrant costumes and rhythmic movements.
 
 
 
• **Storytelling**
 
 
• Manipuri dance incorporates storytelling elements through its depiction of mythological tales, but storytelling is not its predominant theme.
 
• Other Indian classical dance forms like Kathak and Bharatanatyam emphasize storytelling as a core aspect, using gestures (mudras) and facial expressions to narrate epic stories.
 
 
 
• **Main theme of Manipuri dance**
 
 
• Manipuri dance is unique among Indian classical dances for its emphasis on **spiritual expression** rather than technical mastery or theatrical drama.
 
• It is characterized by serene and devotional performances that reflect the cultural and religious ethos of Manipur.
 
• The dance style celebrates the **Raslila**, which portrays the divine love and union of Radha and Krishna, embodying the essence of Bhakti (devotion).

question: What is the thematic focus of the Padam item in Bharatnatyam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Love and divine affection**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Padam in Bharatnatyam is a significant component that focuses on **expressing emotions (Bhava)** through storytelling.
 
• It primarily depicts themes of **love and divine affection**, often exploring the relationship between a devotee and a deity or between lovers.
 
• Padams are known for their **slow-paced, expressive movements** that emphasize subtle facial expressions and intricate hand gestures (mudras).
 
• The lyrics of Padams are usually composed in Tamil, Telugu, or Sanskrit and are often devotional in nature, **describing the longing of a devotee for the divine or the yearning of a lover**.
 
• This segment of Bharatnatyam allows the dancer to demonstrate their **abhinaya (expressive skills)**, making it a deeply emotional and spiritual performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Devotional praise:**

 
 
• This theme is explored in the **Alarippu** and **Varnam** sections of Bharatnatyam, where the dancer praises deities and showcases devotion through rhythmic movements and expressions.
 
• However, while devotional praise is a significant element in Bharatnatyam, it is more general and does not specifically define the Padam, which focuses on love and divine affection.
 
 
 
• **Abstract dance:**
 
 
• Abstract dance refers to dance forms that do not tell a story but instead focus on **pure movement, rhythm, and patterns**.
 
• In Bharatnatyam, this is represented by the **Nritta** aspect, including dances like Jatiswaram and Tillana, which emphasize technical precision and rhythmic beauty rather than emotions or storytelling.
 
• Padams, on the other hand, are highly expressive and narrative-focused, distinguishing them from abstract dance.
 
 
 
• **Rhythmic patterns:**
 
 
• Rhythmic patterns are a hallmark of the Nritta component of Bharatnatyam, where intricate footwork and synchronized movements with music are emphasized.
 
• While rhythm is integral to all aspects of Bharatnatyam, it is not the primary focus of Padams, which center on emotional expression rather than intricate rhythmic patterns.

question: Which of these is NOT a feature of Kathakali performances?

options.text: Actors use facial expressions and hand gestures
The performance is silent with no vocalization

solution:
The correct answer is __**The performance is silent with no vocalization**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathakali performances are not silent;** they are accompanied by vocalization, including live singing and narration.
 
• Live singing in Kathakali is performed by vocalists who narrate the story in Malayalam, adding depth and context to the performance.
 
• The actors use intricate facial expressions, hand gestures (mudras), and body movements to depict emotions and narratives in sync with the music and vocals.
 
• The entire performance is a blend of dialogue and musical instruments, such as chenda, maddalam, and cymbals, creating a rich audio-visual experience.
 
• Silence is not a feature of Kathakali, as the vocal and instrumental components play a significant role in engaging the audience.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Masked performances:**
 
 
• While Kathakali does not involve masks, the actors use intricate makeup styles and elaborate costumes. The makeup itself serves as a mask, transforming the actors into mythological and divine characters.
 
• The makeup is categorized into types, such as Pacha (green), Kathi (knife), and Kari (black), representing different character traits like heroism, villainy, or evil.
 
 
 
• **Actors use facial expressions and hand gestures:**
 
 
• Facial expressions (Navarasas) and hand gestures (Mudras) are fundamental to Kathakali performances.
 
• These elements help narrate stories from Hindu epics like the Mahabharata and Ramayana in a visually compelling manner.
 
• The facial expressions are highly exaggerated to convey emotions clearly even to distant viewers.
 
 
 
• **The performance includes live singing:**
 
 
• Live singing, known as Sopanam, is integral to Kathakali performances.
 
• Specialized vocalists sing verses in Malayalam, often adapted from classical texts, which are synchronized with the actors’ actions.
 
• The singers are accompanied by traditional instruments like chenda (drum) and maddalam, adding rhythm and intensity to the performance.

question: What is the primary source of Kathakali's dramatic stories?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Indian epics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Kathakali** is a classical dance-drama form that originated in **Kerala, India**. It is famous for its elaborate costumes, intricate makeup, and expressive storytelling.
 
• The primary source of dramatic stories in Kathakali is derived from **Indian epics**, mainly the **Mahabharata** and the **Ramayana**. These epics provide a rich repository of themes and characters for Kathakali performances.
 
• Stories are mostly presented through a combination of dance, music, and acting, with performers depicting mythological characters and narrating epic tales.
 
• Kathakali involves highly stylized movements and gestures, which are used to communicate the emotions and actions of characters described in the **epics**.
 
• The performances are usually set during the night and can last for several hours, covering major episodes from the epics like the battle between **Rama and Ravana** or **Duryodhana’s defeat** in the Mahabharata.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Indian Epics:**

 
 
• The **Mahabharata** and **Ramayana** are two of the greatest epics in Indian literature, written by **Vyasa** and **Valmiki**, respectively.
 
• The **Mahabharata** is considered the longest epic in the world, containing over 100,000 shlokas and narrating the story of the **Kauravas** and **Pandavas**.
 
• The **Ramayana** narrates the life and adventures of **Lord Rama**, including his battle against the demon king **Ravana**.
 
• Both epics contain moral lessons, philosophical insights, and divine interventions, making them ideal for performance art such as Kathakali.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Kathakali:**
 
 
• Kathakali combines **music, dance, drama, and elaborate costumes** to narrate stories.
 
• The makeup in Kathakali is highly detailed and symbolic, with **green** representing noble characters like gods and heroes, and **red** depicting demons or villains.
 
• The musical instruments used include the **chenda**, **maddalam**, and **edakka**, which enhance the dramatic effect.
 
• Kathakali traditionally begins with a ceremonial introduction called the **kalasam**.
 
 
 
• **Other Sources of Kathakali Stories:**
 
 
• While Indian epics are the primary source, some stories are adapted from **Puranas**, such as the **Bhagavata Purana**.
 
• Local legends and folklore occasionally supplement the repertoire, but they are not as central as the epics.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Kathakali:**
 
 
• Kathakali is an integral part of Kerala’s culture and is recognized globally as a unique art form.
 
• It serves as a medium to preserve and propagate the **mythological and philosophical heritage** of India.
 
• UNESCO has acknowledged Kathakali as a significant contributor to **intangible cultural heritage**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Costumes:** The costumes are elaborate and consist of a **skirt, headgear, ornaments, and makeup**. They symbolize the character being portrayed.
 
• **Gestures:** Kathakali relies heavily on **hand gestures (mudras)** and facial expressions to narrate the story.
 
• **Training:** Kathakali performers undergo rigorous training, including mastering breath control and flexibility. They often start at an early age.
 
• **Performance Structure:** The performance includes a **prelude, main act, and concluding segments**, all set to traditional music.

• The name is derived from its primary weapons: **Thang** (sword) and **Ta** (spear), though practitioners also utilize the **Chungoi** (shield) and various other bladed instruments.
 
• It features two main components: the **ritualistic** aspects related to tantric practices and the **physical** aspects involving high-energy combat sequences, complex footwork, and athletic maneuvers.
 
• Historically, this art form was a vital defense mechanism for the **Meitei** warriors of the **Manipur Kingdom**; however, it was suppressed during the **British colonial era** and later revived as a performing art.

• **Sankirtana**:
 
 
• This is a ritualistic performance involving **singing**, **drumming**, and **dancing**, primarily practiced by the **Vaishnava** community in Manipur.
 
• It was recognized by **UNESCO** in **2013** as part of the **Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity**.
