question: Where did Bharatanatyam originate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tamil Nadu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bharatanatyam** originated in **Tamil Nadu**, a southern state of India. It is one of the oldest classical dance forms in the country.
 
• This dance form is deeply rooted in **Hindu religious traditions** and was initially performed in temples as a form of devotion to deities, particularly Lord Shiva and Vishnu.
 
• Bharatanatyam is known for its **rigorous footwork**, graceful movements, and intricate gestures (mudras) that convey stories and emotions.
 
• The dance form is accompanied by **Carnatic music**, which enhances the storytelling aspect through rhythm, melody, and lyrics.
 
• Bharatanatyam is regarded as a **Natya Yoga**, a form of spiritual expression and meditation through art.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **History and Origin:**

 
 
• Bharatanatyam has its origins in the temples of **Tamil Nadu**, where it was performed by **Devadasis** as part of religious rituals.
 
• The dance form is mentioned in ancient texts such as the **Natya Shastra**, written by **Bharata**, which is considered the foundation of Indian classical dance and drama.
 
• Over time, Bharatanatyam transitioned from a temple art to a performance art, gaining recognition on global stages.
 
 
 
• **Key Features:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is characterized by **Angika (body movements)**, **Vachika (speech)**, **Aharya (costume)**, and **Sattvika (emotion).**
 
• The performers wear traditional costumes adorned with intricate jewelry and makeup, which enhance the visual appeal and expressiveness of the dance.
 
• The dance includes various postures, such as the **Aramandi** (half-seated position), which is a hallmark of Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Musical Accompaniment:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam uses **Carnatic music**, incorporating instruments such as the **mridangam**, **violin**, **flute**, and **veena.**
 
• The dance is performed to compositions of saints like **Tyagaraja**, **Muthuswami Dikshitar**, and **Shyama Shastri.**
 
 
 
• **Global Recognition:**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam is now practiced and performed worldwide, symbolizing the **rich cultural heritage** of India.
 
• Many prominent dancers, such as **Rukmini Devi Arundale**, have played a significant role in reviving and popularizing Bharatanatyam.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Other Dance Forms from Southern India:**

 
 
• **Kerala:** Known for **Mohiniyattam** and **Kathakali**, which are classical dance-drama traditions.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh:** Famous for **Kuchipudi**, a classical dance form that blends narrative and performance.
 
• **Karnataka:** Home to **Yakshagana**, a traditional theatre form combining dance, music, and dialogue.
 
 
 
• **Distinctive Features of Bharatanatyam:**

• The dance form is often performed solo, allowing the dancer to showcase their skill and devotion.

__
 
• **Bharhut sculpture**, an early Indian sculpture of the Shunga period (mid-2nd century BCE) that decorated the great stupa, or relic mound, of Bharhut, in** Madhya Pradesh state.**

question: In which city is the sculptural panel of "Descent of the Ganges" located?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahabalipuram**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The "Descent of the Ganges" is a famous sculptural panel located in **Mahabalipuram**, Tamil Nadu, India.
 
• It is one of the largest open-air rock reliefs in the world, measuring approximately 29 meters in length and 13 meters in height.
 
• The panel depicts the story of the sacred river Ganges descending to Earth from the heavens, as per Hindu mythology, with the help of Lord Shiva.
 
• This magnificent sculpture showcases intricate carvings of gods, demigods, animals, and other celestial beings, representing the divine event.
 
• Mahabalipuram, also known as Mamallapuram, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its group of monuments including rock-cut caves, temples, and sculptures from the Pallava period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ellora:**

 
 
• Ellora is a UNESCO World Heritage Site located in Maharashtra, India, and is famous for its rock-cut caves dating back to the Rashtrakuta dynasty.
 
• It consists of 34 caves, including Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain temples and monasteries, showcasing India's religious diversity.
 
• The most notable structure is the Kailasa Temple (Cave 16), a monolithic rock-cut temple dedicated to Lord Shiva.
 
 
 
• **Pattadakal:**
 
 
• Pattadakal, located in Karnataka, is another UNESCO World Heritage Site renowned for its blend of Dravidian (Southern) and Nagara (Northern) architectural styles.
 
• The site includes a group of Hindu and Jain temples from the 7th and 8th centuries, built during the reign of the Chalukya dynasty.
 
• The Virupaksha Temple and Mallikarjuna Temple are prime examples of exquisite Chalukyan architecture.
 
 
 
• **Badami:**
 
 
• Badami, also in Karnataka, is famous for its rock-cut cave temples, built during the Chalukya dynasty in the 6th and 7th centuries.
 
• The site includes four main cave temples carved into sandstone cliffs, dedicated to Hindu deities such as Shiva and Vishnu, and one Jain temple.
 
• Badami is also known for its ancient inscriptions and scenic location surrounded by hills and lakes.

question: In which of the following shapes is the famous Sun Temple at Konark designed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**A gigantic chariot**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sun Temple at Konark** is located in the state of **Odisha, India**, and is a **UNESCO World Heritage Site**. It is one of the most famous temples in India dedicated to the Sun God.
 
• It is designed in the shape of **a gigantic chariot**, symbolizing the **chariot of the Sun God Surya**. The temple features twelve pairs of elaborately carved stone wheels, which represent the chariot wheels.
 
• The temple was constructed in the **13th century** by King **Narasimha Deva I** of the **Eastern Ganga dynasty**. It stands as a testament to the architectural brilliance of that era.
 
• The chariot is drawn by **seven horses**, representing the seven days of the week. Each horse symbolizes a day, emphasizing the Sun's movement throughout the week.
 
• The intricate carvings on the temple depict various aspects of life, including flora, fauna, deities, and celestial beings. The wheels also act as **sundials**, showcasing the advanced understanding of astronomy in ancient India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Symbolism of the Chariot:**

 
 
• The chariot design signifies the movement of the Sun across the sky, as believed in Hindu mythology. The **seven horses** pulling the chariot represent the seven colors of the rainbow and the seven chakras in the human body.
 
• The twelve pairs of wheels symbolize the **12 months of the year** and the concept of time.
 
 
 
• **Architectural Features:**
 
 
• The temple follows the **Kalinga style** of architecture, characterized by its ornate carvings, towering spires, and intricate sculptures.
 
• The main sanctum (now in ruins) was constructed to align with the first rays of the rising sun, highlighting the temple's astronomical precision.
 
 
 
• **Other Options:**
 
 
• **Lotus Flower:** While the **lotus flower** is a significant motif in Indian art and architecture, it is not the design of the Sun Temple at Konark.
 
• **Circular Stupa:** Stupas are structures associated with Buddhism and are not relevant to the Sun Temple's design.
 
• **Reclining Deity:** This refers to a deity lying in a reclining position, which is commonly associated with temples dedicated to Lord Vishnu, such as the Ranganathaswamy Temple in Srirangam.
 
 
 
• **UNESCO Recognition:**
 
 
• The Sun Temple at Konark was inscribed as a **World Heritage Site** by UNESCO in **1984** for its outstanding universal value and architectural significance.
 
• It is also known as the **"Black Pagoda"** due to its dark-colored construction materials, which served as a landmark for sailors navigating the Bay of Bengal.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The Sun Temple at Konark is part of the **Golden Triangle** of Odisha tourism, which includes **Puri** and **Bhubaneswar**.
 
• The temple is frequently celebrated in literature, art, and dance, with the **Konark Dance Festival** held annually to showcase India's classical dance forms.
 
• It is considered a masterpiece of ancient Indian architecture and is a source of inspiration for modern-day architects and historians.
 
• The temple's construction techniques and astronomical alignments continue to be studied by experts worldwide.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Indo-Saracenic** architectural style was developed during the colonial era in India, specifically in the late 19th and early 20th centuries.
 
• It is a unique blend of **Gothic, Mughal, and Hindu architectural features**, reflecting a fusion of Indian and European elements.
 
• The style was promoted by the British as a way to integrate elements of Indian architecture into colonial projects, while also showcasing their imperial dominance.
 
• Key characteristics include **domes, arches, spires, minarets, and intricate ornamentation**. Examples of this style include the **Victoria Memorial in Kolkata** and the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus in Mumbai**.
 
• The style was primarily used for public and administrative buildings such as railway stations, government offices, museums, and courts during the British colonial rule in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Colonial Baroque:**

 
 
• This style refers to the Baroque architectural influence during the colonial period.
 
• It is characterized by **grand, ornate details, dramatic use of light and shadow, and elaborate decorations**.
 
• Colonial Baroque architecture is more commonly associated with Latin American and European colonies rather than India.
 
 
 
• **Dravidian Revival:**
 
 
• This architectural movement focused on reviving traditional Dravidian architectural styles of South India.
 
• It primarily drew inspiration from **temples built during the Pallava, Chola, and Vijayanagara empires**.
 
• It is known for its **towering gopurams, intricate carvings, and pillared halls**.
 
• It is distinct from the Indo-Saracenic style, as it does not incorporate Gothic or Mughal influences.
 
 
 
• **Mughal-Gothic:**
 
 
• This term is often incorrectly used to describe the Indo-Saracenic style, but it is not a formally recognized architectural style.
 
• The term might imply the combination of Mughal and Gothic elements, but such a style does not exist independently in architectural history.
 
• The Indo-Saracenic style is the correct representation of such a fusion.
 
 
 
• **Important Examples of Indo-Saracenic Architecture:**
 
 
• The **Madras High Court**, built in 1892, is a prominent example of this style.
 
• The **Prince of Wales Museum (now Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Vastu Sangrahalaya)** in Mumbai reflects the Indo-Saracenic style.
 
• Other examples include the **Chepauk Palace in Chennai** and the **Gateway of India in Mumbai**.

question: Which of the following features are associated with the Gothic architectural style?

options.text: Pointed arches and stained glass windows

solution:
The correct answer is __**Pointed arches and stained glass windows**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gothic architecture** is a European architectural style that flourished during the **High and Late Middle Ages**, specifically from the **12th to the 16th century**. It evolved from **Romanesque architecture** and was eventually succeeded by **Renaissance architecture**.
 
• The **pointed arch** (or ogival arch) is the defining characteristic of this style. Unlike the rounded arches of earlier periods, the pointed arch allowed for **greater height** and thinner walls by directing the weight of the structure more vertically.
 
• **Stained glass windows** were extensively used to fill large wall openings, made possible by the structural support of the arches. These windows, including the famous **rose windows**, were used to illustrate biblical stories and create a luminous, ethereal atmosphere inside **Cathedrals**.
 
• Other fundamental features include **ribbed vaults**, which supported heavy ceilings with a web of stone ribs, and **flying buttresses**, which were external stone supports that carried the weight of the high roofs away from the walls.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Domes and Minarets**:

 
 
• These are primary features of **Islamic architecture** and **Mughal architecture**, seen in landmarks like the **Taj Mahal** and the **Jama Masjid**.
 
 
 
• **Flat roofs with courtyards**:
 
 
• These are characteristic of **traditional Indian housing** and **Mediterranean architecture**, designed to improve ventilation and provide private outdoor space in warm climates.
 
 
 
• **Sloping tiled roofs**:
 
 
• Commonly found in **Vernacular architecture** within regions of high rainfall, such as **Kerala** or the **Konkan coast**, to facilitate efficient water drainage.
 
 
 
• **Historical Examples**:
 
 
• Famous Gothic structures include **Notre-Dame de Paris** in France and **Westminster Abbey** in London. In India, the **Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj Terminus** (CSMT) is a premier example of the **Victorian Gothic Revival** style.

question: The Bhimakali Temple in Sarahan is a fine example of which architectural style?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kath-Kuni**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bhimakali Temple** in Sarahan, Himachal Pradesh, is a remarkable example of the **Kath-Kuni architectural style**.
 
• **Kath-Kuni** is an indigenous architectural style of the **Himalayan region**, particularly popular in Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The style prominently uses **wood and stone**, arranged alternately in layers, which gives the structure strength and makes it resistant to earthquakes.
 
• The Bhimakali Temple showcases the usage of **deodar wood** and stone, both of which are abundantly available in the region, making it environmentally sustainable and culturally significant.
 
• This architectural style is known for its **intricate carvings, sloping roofs, and stacked construction technique**, which also offers excellent insulation against the cold climate of the Himalayas.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kath-Kuni Architectural Style:**

 
 
• The term "Kath-Kuni" derives from two words in the local dialect: **"Kath," meaning wood**, and **"Kuni," meaning corner**.
 
• This technique is widely used in **temples, houses, and forts** across Himachal Pradesh and Uttarakhand.
 
• It provides **structural flexibility**, which is crucial in earthquake-prone areas like the Himalayan region.
 
• The structures often feature **flat roofs or pagoda-style roofs** made of slate, which helps in dealing with heavy snowfall.
 
 
 
• **Bhimakali Temple:**
 
 
• The Bhimakali Temple is a **900-year-old structure** and an important religious and architectural landmark in Sarahan.
 
• The temple is dedicated to **Goddess Bhimakali**, the presiding deity of the rulers of the former Bushahr state.
 
• The temple complex comprises multiple shrines, with the main temple reflecting traditional **Kath-Kuni construction methods**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Styles:**
 
 
• **Chalukyan Style:** Predominantly seen in South India, featuring intricately carved temple spires and stone construction. *This is not related to the Bhimakali Temple.*
 
• **Dravidian Style:** Characterized by towering gopurams (gateway towers) and richly decorated stone carvings, common in Tamil Nadu and Karnataka. *This does not apply to the Bhimakali Temple.*
 
• **Indo-Gothic Style:** A colonial architectural style combining Indian and Gothic elements, primarily seen in buildings constructed during British rule. *This is unrelated to the Bhimakali Temple.*
 
 
 
• **Preservation Efforts:**
 
 
• Efforts are being made to preserve the **Kath-Kuni architecture** as it represents the cultural heritage of the Himalayan region.
 
• Initiatives include workshops and training programs for local artisans to keep the tradition alive.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Kath-Kuni:**

 
 
• It is a **climate-responsive construction style**, offering natural insulation and durability.
 
• The use of **local materials** reduces the environmental impact and promotes sustainability.

question: For which architectural element is the Sidi Saiyyed Mosque in Gujarat famous for?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Lattice windows (jalis)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sidi Saiyyed Mosque**, popularly known as **Sidi Saiyyed ni Jali**, was built in **1572-73 AD** in **Ahmedabad**, **Gujarat**.
 
• It was constructed by **Sidi Saiyyed**, an Abyssinian nobleman in the service of **Bilal Jhajhar Khan**, during the reign of the last Sultan of the **Gujarat Sultanate**, **Muzaffar Shah III**.
 
• The structure is world-famous for its ten beautifully carved semi-circular **lattice windows** (**jalis**) that adorn the side and rear arches of the mosque.
 
• The most iconic of these is the **Tree of Life** jali, which features a central tree with intertwining branches and foliage, showcasing unparalleled **Indo-Saracenic** craftsmanship.
 
• The delicate stone carving is so fine that it resembles **filigree** work, representing the height of the **Gujarat School of Architecture**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Architectural Significance**:

 
 
• The **Tree of Life** design is the inspiration behind the logo of the **Indian Institute of Management Ahmedabad (IIMA)**.
 
• Unlike many other mosques of that era, the **Sidi Saiyyed Mosque** does not have a traditional courtyard, as it was built as part of the **citadel wall**.
 
• The central arch of the mosque is surprisingly devoid of a jali, likely due to the **Mughal invasion** of Gujarat in **1573** by **Emperor Akbar**, which halted the completion of the work.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Heritage**:
 
 
• The mosque is considered one of the finest examples of **Islamic art** in India, blending local **Hindu** and **Jain** motifs with Islamic architectural geometry.
 
• The city of **Ahmedabad**, where the mosque is located, was declared India's first **UNESCO World Heritage City** in **2017**.

question: M Balamuralikrishna is associated with which form of music?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Carnatic Sangeet**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **M Balamualikrishna**

 
 
• **He was an Indian Carnatic vocalist, musician, multi-instrumentalist, playback singer, composer, and character actor.**
 
• He was awarded the Madras Music Academy's Sangeetha Kalanidhi in 1978.
 
• Balamuralikrishna started his career at the age of six. In his lifetime, he gave over 25,000 concerts worldwide. 
 
• Balamuralikrishna has experimented with the Carnatic music system by keeping its rich tradition untouched.
 
• Balamuralikrishna has over 400 c**om**positions to his credit and is one of the very few people to have composed in all the 72** M**elakarta Ragas, He has created several ragas, with 4 notes and 3 notes and also has invented a new Tala system.
 
 
 
• **Carnatic Sangeet****​**
 
 
• Carnatic** music** was written to be sung, but the voice acts as an instr**um**ent, recreating, in a way, the sound of the veena.
 
• The definition of Carnatic is a place in southeast India between the Eastern Ghats and the Coromandel Coast.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Folk Music**

 
 
• Type of **traditional and generally rural music **that originally was passed down through families and other small social groups.
 
• Typically, f**olk music, like folk literature, lives in oral tradition,** it is learned through hearing rather than reading.
 
• Traditional folk music has been defined in several ways:** as music transmitted orally, as music with unknown composers**.
 
• Music that is played on traditional instruments, music about cultural or national identity, music that changes between generations (folk process), music **associated with a people's folklore**.
 
 
 
• ​**Haveli Sangeet****​**
 
 
• It is a pure form of classical music consisting of numerous alaaps, gaans and pads** sung in the temples**.
 
• Haveli Sangeet and Shastriya Sangeet are similar to each other and the age-old sangeet is dedicated in praise of the almighty. 
 
• **Haveli Sangeet is a form of Hindustani classical music sung in havelis.**
 
• The essential component is **dhrupad.**
 
• It originated in **Mathura in Braj, northern India.**
 
• It takes the form of devotional songs sung daily to Krishna by the **Pushtimarg sect**.
 
 
 
• **Hindustani Sangeet****​**
 
 
• Hindustani classical music is the classical music of the Indian subcontinent's northern regions.
 
• It's also known as Shastriya** sangeet** or North Indian classical music.
 
• Its roots can be traced back to the 12th century CE when it split from Carnatic music, the Southern classical tradition.
 
• Dhrupad, Khyal, and Tarana are the three major vocal genres or styles associated with Hindustani classical music.
 
• Dhamar, Trivat, Chaiti, Kajari, Tappa, Tap-Khyal, Ashtapadis, Thumri, Dadra, Ghazal, and Bhajan are light classical genres that do not follow the strict principles of classical music.
 
• Tansen is widely regarded as the founder of Hindustani music.
 
• Alapana__:
 
 
• The exposition of a raga or tone is known as alapana or ragam.
 
• It is the first element of Ragam Tanam Pallavi (RTP), which demonstrates a Carnatic musician's ability to comprehend a raga and compose music to accompany it.

During the modern period, Pt. V.N. Bhatkhande and Pt. V.D. Paluskar contributed significantly to Hindustani classical music by introducing a systematized ______
solution:
The correct answer is __**Notation System**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• During the modern period, Pt. Vishnu Narayan Bhatkhande and Pt. Vishnu Digambar Paluskar made significant contributions to Hindustani classical music by introducing a systematic **notation system**.
 
• The **notation system** developed by Pt. Bhatkhande enabled musicians to document and preserve musical compositions for future generations.
 
• Pt. Paluskar popularized Indian classical music by introducing it to the masses through formalized teaching methods and printed music notations.
 
• The notation system standardized the way ragas were documented, reducing ambiguity and ensuring uniformity in music education.
 
• This systematic approach played a crucial role in transforming Hindustani classical music into a structured discipline that could be learned, taught, and preserved effectively.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhakti Movement**
 
 
• The Bhakti Movement was a medieval Indian religious movement that emphasized devotion to a personal deity and rejected ritualism and caste distinctions.
 
• It was not related to Hindustani classical music directly but influenced devotional music forms such as bhajans and kirtans.
 
• Prominent figures of this movement include Mirabai, Kabir, and Tulsidas.
 
 
 
• **Stage Performance Culture**
 
 
• Stage performance culture in India evolved during the colonial and post-colonial periods as a way to present classical and folk art forms to a wider audience.
 
• While stage performances contributed to the popularization of classical music, they were not directly related to the development of a notation system.
 
• Musicians like Pt. Ravi Shankar and Ustad Bismillah Khan played a significant role in promoting Indian classical music through live performances on global stages.
 
 
 
• **Raga-Ragini Paintings**
 
 
• Raga-Ragini paintings are a form of miniature art that depict various ragas and raginis (musical modes) in Indian classical music.
 
• These paintings were popular in medieval India and are associated with the visual representation of music rather than its documentation or teaching.
 
• They are not related to the systematic development of music notations.

question:
Which of the following statements about traditional and semi-classical Indian music forms are correct?

1) Kajri is sung by women in Uttar Pradesh during the monsoon, often with night-long group dancing.

2) Qawwali, introduced by Turkish Sufis, is performed only as solo singing without chorus.

3) Tappa from Punjab features rapid, jumpy notes inspired by camel riders' songs.

4) Amir Khusro helped shape Qawwali in India as a Sufi devotional form.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 2: 1, 3, and 4 only**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kajri** is a traditional monsoon song form from **Uttar Pradesh**, sung predominantly by women during the rainy season. It involves group performances, sometimes with night-long dancing. ***Statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Qawwali**, introduced in India by **Turkish Sufis**, is a form of Sufi devotional music. However, it is performed with a chorus (not as solo singing). This includes a lead singer and accompanying group members. ***Statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **Tappa**, a semi-classical music form originating from **Punjab**, is characterized by rapid, jumpy notes. It evolved from camel riders' songs and is notable for its intricate rhythm and expressive style. ***Statement 3 is correct.***
 
• **Amir Khusro**, a revered figure in Indian classical music and Sufi tradition, played a pivotal role in shaping **Qawwali** as a devotional form in India. His contributions laid the foundation for this genre. ***Statement 4 is correct.***
 
• Thus, only statements 1, 3, and 4 are correct.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Kajri:**

 
 
• It is a seasonal folk song originating from **eastern Uttar Pradesh** and parts of **Bihar**.
 
• It is associated with the monsoon season and often depicts themes of love, longing, and separation.
 
• Kajri is popular in regions such as **Varanasi, Mirzapur, and Allahabad**.
 
 
 
• **Qawwali:**
 
 
• Qawwali is a form of Sufi devotional music that originated in the **13th century**.
 
• It is performed in a group, with a lead singer, chorus, and instrumentalists (often using harmonium and tabla).
 
• The lyrics of Qawwalis are deeply spiritual, often praising God or expressing mystical experiences.
 
• Qawwali is popular in **India, Pakistan, and Bangladesh**.
 
 
 
• **Tappa:**
 
 
• The Tappa style was developed in **Punjab** and is known for its swift, intricate, and dynamic musical notes.
 
• It was brought to the forefront of Indian classical music by **Ghulam Nabi Shori**, also known as Shori Mian.
 
• Tappa is sung in languages like Punjabi and Brajbhasha, with themes often revolving around romance.
 
 
 
• **Amir Khusro:**
 
 
• He was a 13th-century poet, musician, and scholar in the court of the Delhi Sultanate.
 
• Khusro is credited with the invention of several musical forms, including **Qawwali** and **Tarana**.
 
• He also introduced Persian and Arabic elements into Indian classical music.
 
• His contributions to Indian music remain influential, particularly in the realms of Sufi traditions and semi-classical music.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Traditional and semi-classical Indian music forms are deeply rooted in regional and spiritual traditions, often reflecting the cultural and religious diversity of India.
 
• Folk forms like Kajri and classical forms like Tappa highlight the versatility and richness of Indian music.
 
• Sufi music, as exemplified by Qawwali, bridges the gap between spirituality and art, emphasizing the universal messages of love and devotion.
 
• Amir Khusro’s contributions underscore the fusion of Indian and Persian traditions, which enriched the Indian musical heritage.

__
 
• **Kathak** is a classical dance form originating in northern India, and it is deeply intertwined with **Hindustani music.**
 
• Hindustani music provides the **rhythmic and melodic framework** for Kathak performances, using instruments like the tabla, harmonium, and sitar.
 
• Kathak dancers often perform to **classical Hindustani compositions**, including thumris, ghazals, and dadras, which highlight the emotive and expressive aspects of the dance.
 
• The ** (rhythmic cycles) in Hindustani music is crucial to Kathak, as dancers showcase intricate footwork and rhythmic patterns in sync with the music.

__
 
• **Hindustani Music:**

 
 
• It is one of the two primary traditions of Indian classical music, the other being **Carnatic music.**
 
• Hindustani music originated in the northern parts of India and has been influenced by Persian and Mughal traditions.
 
• It emphasizes **improvisation** and the development of ragas (melodic frameworks) over time.
 
• Key instruments include the tabla, sitar, harmonium, sarangi, and bansuri.
 
• Prominent forms include **dhrupad, khyal, thumri, and tappa.**
 
 
 
• **Kathak Dance:**
 
 
• Kathak is one of the eight classical dance forms of India, known for its intricate footwork, spins, and gestures (mudras).
 
• It is highly expressive and often portrays stories from **Indian mythology, particularly tales of Lord Krishna.**
 
• The term "Kathak" comes from the Sanskrit word **Katha**, meaning "story," as the dance form was initially used by storytellers to narrate tales.
 
• Kathak performances are accompanied by Hindustani music, with rhythmic cycles provided by the tabla and melodic accompaniment by instruments like the sitar and harmonium.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Genres:**
 
 
• **Carnatic music:** This is the classical music tradition of southern India, primarily associated with Bharatanatyam and Kuchipudi dance forms. It is distinct from Hindustani music.
 
• **Folk music:** While Kathak may occasionally incorporate folk elements, its foundation remains classical and rooted in Hindustani music.
 
• **Western classical music:** This genre has no direct connection to Kathak, as it belongs to an entirely different cultural and musical tradition.

• **Fusion Performances:** In modern times, Kathak has been fused with other genres of music, but its classical base in Hindustani music remains unchanged.
 
• **Famous Kathak Artists:** Renowned Kathak dancers like **Birju Maharaj** and **Shovana Narayan** have emphasized the importance of Hindustani music in their performances.
 
• **Role of Instruments:** Instruments like the **tabla** and **sitar** are not just accompaniments but play an active role in setting the mood and rhythm for Kathak performances.

question: Which devotional song form in simple Kannada, promoted by the Haridasa Movement in Karnataka, is a cornerstone of its Carnatic music tradition?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Devara Nama**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Devara Nama** is a devotional song form written in simple **Kannada** and promoted by the **Haridasa Movement** in Karnataka.
 
• It constitutes a significant part of the **Carnatic music tradition**, blending spirituality with musical expression.
 
• The lyrics of Devara Nama are written to praise and worship **Lord Vishnu** and are composed by the Haridasas, including notable figures like **Purandaradasa** and **Kanakadasa**.
 
• These devotional songs emphasize **Bhakti (devotion)** and moral values, aiming to connect common people with spirituality through their simplicity and relatable themes.
 
• The Haridasa Movement, which flourished between the **13th and 17th centuries**, was pivotal in popularizing Devara Nama across Karnataka, leaving a lasting impact on both music and spirituality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Haridasa Movement:**

 
 
• The Haridasa Movement was a **religious and cultural movement** in Karnataka aimed at spreading the principles of Bhakti (devotion) through music and literature.
 
• It flourished under the patronage of the Vijayanagara Empire and was instrumental in promoting the **Bhakti tradition**.
 
• Prominent Haridasas include **Purandaradasa** (known as the father of Carnatic music), **Kanakadasa**, and **Vijayadasa**.
 
• The movement focused on creating devotional compositions in **Kannada**, making spiritual teachings accessible to the common people.
 
 
 
• **Vachana:**
 
 
• Vachana is a form of **prose-poetry** written in Kannada, associated with the **Veerashaiva or Lingayat movement**.
 
• It focuses on spiritual and philosophical themes and was popularized by saints like **Basavanna**, **Allama Prabhu**, and **Akka Mahadevi**.
 
• Unlike Devara Nama, Vachanas are not set to music and are primarily reflective and meditative.
 
 
 
• **Janapada Geete:**
 
 
• Janapada Geete refers to **folk songs** of Karnataka that reflect the culture, traditions, and daily lives of rural communities.
 
• They are not specifically devotional and cover a variety of themes such as love, festivals, and harvests.
 
 
 
• **Bhajan:**
 
 
• Bhajans are **devotional songs** common across India and are usually dedicated to deities like Krishna, Rama, or Shiva.
 
• While they share similarities with Devara Nama, Bhajans are more **generic** and are not specific to Karnataka or the Kannada language.
 
 
 
• **Purandaradasa's Contribution:**
 
 
• Purandaradasa, a key figure in the Haridasa Movement, is revered as the **father of Carnatic music**.
 
• He composed **thousands of Devara Namas** that are still sung in Carnatic music concerts today.
 
• His works laid the foundation for the systematic teaching of Carnatic music through **structured lessons** like Sarali, Janta, and Alankara.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Haridasa Movement** not only influenced music but also contributed to **socio-religious reform**, promoting equality and devotion.
 
• The **Vijayanagara Empire**, under rulers like Krishnadevaraya, played a crucial role in supporting the Haridasa saints and their compositions.
 
• Devara Nama continues to be a cornerstone of **Carnatic music**, bridging classical traditions with spiritual themes.

In Indian classical music notation, a swara with a dot above the letter (e.g., S) represents the [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/efbb4cd1cdb04e3d55ec812b33b49b9c823e135e641878fdc8e5762164dc7a84.png] saptak.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Taar Saptak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **Indian Classical Music**, the term **Saptak** refers to a set of seven musical notes (Swaras): **Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, and Ni**.
 
• According to the **Bhatkhande Music Notation System**, which is widely used in **Hindustani Classical Music**, symbols are used to indicate different registers or octaves.
 
• A **dot placed above** a letter (e.g., Ṡ, Ṙ, Ġ) signifies the **Taar Saptak**, also known as the **Upper Octave**. These notes have a sound frequency that is exactly **double** that of the corresponding notes in the middle register.
 
• The **Taar Saptak** register is used to denote higher-pitched sounds and is essential for expanding the melodic range of a **Raga** during performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mandra Saptak** (Lower Octave):

 
 
• Represented by placing a **dot below** the swara letter (e.g., Ṣ, Ṛ, G̣). This indicates a deep, base register with half the frequency of the **Madhya Saptak**.
 
 
 
• **Madhya Saptak** (Middle Octave):
 
 
• This is the **normal register** where a musician mostly sings or plays. In notation, these notes are written **without any dots** above or below (e.g., S, R, G, M, P, D, N).
 
 
 
• **Shuddha Saptak**:
 
 
• This refers to a scale consisting entirely of **Shuddha (Natural)** swaras. In **Hindustani Classical Music**, the notes of **Bilawal Thaat** are considered the standard **Shuddha Saptak**.

question: Which term refers to a melodic framework in Indian classical music that consists of ascending (arohana) and descending (avarohana) notes?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Raga**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Raga** is a fundamental concept in **Indian classical music** and serves as the melodic framework for a musical composition.
 
• It consists of two main components: **ascending (Arohana)** notes and **descending (Avarohana)** notes, which create its unique structure and identity.
 
• A raga is not just a scale but a combination of notes that evoke specific emotions or **rasa** (aesthetic essence) in the listener.
 
• Each raga has its own rules, such as the choice of specific notes, their order, and the way they are emphasized, to create a unique musical expression.
 
• The concept of raga is deeply tied to Indian culture, spirituality, and nature, with many ragas associated with specific times of the day, seasons, or moods.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Swara:**

 
 
• A swara is a single musical note in Indian classical music.
 
• The basic swaras are **Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni**, which correspond to Western solfège notes: Do, Re, Mi, Fa, Sol, La, Ti.
 
• Swara forms the building block of a raga but does not define the melodic framework on its own.
 
 
 
• **Talam:**
 
 
• Talam refers to the rhythmic framework in Indian classical music.
 
• It governs the structure of beats and cycles and is independent of the melodic structure provided by the raga.
 
• Examples include **Adi Talam** and **Rupaka Talam**.
 
 
 
• **Alap:**
 
 
• Alap is the introductory section of a raga performance, where the artist explores the notes of the raga slowly and meditatively without rhythmic accompaniment.
 
• It is aimed at setting the mood and introducing the listener to the essence of the raga.
 
 
 
• **Raga Structure:**
 
 
• Each raga consists of **Pakad** (a distinct pattern of notes), **Vadi** (dominant note), and **Samvadi** (sub-dominant note).
 
• Some ragas have **Vikrit Swaras** (altered notes) that deviate from their natural pitch.
 
• Ragas are classified based on their **Thaat** (parent scale) in Hindustani music.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Significance:**
 
 
• Ragas are often associated with specific times of the day or seasons, such as **Raag Bhairav** for early morning or **Raag Malhar** for the monsoon season.
 
• The performance of a raga aims to transport the listener into a particular emotional or spiritual state.

question:
Which Hindustani classical gharana, founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan, is known for its melodic complexity and features exponents like

Kesarbai Kerkar and Kishori Amonkar?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Jaipur-Atrauli Gharana** was established by **Ustad Alladiya Khan** (1855−1946) in the late **19th century**. He was originally from **Atrauli** and later served in the courts of **Jaipur** and **Kolhapur**, merging these diverse musical influences.
 
• This gharana is globally recognized for its extreme **melodic complexity** and a technical singing style known as **Gund-Gunkari**, which involves intricate ornamentation and weaving of notes.
 
• A defining feature of this school is the use of **Vakra Taans** (oblique or convoluted melodic phrases). These patterns are non-linear and require immense breath control and **Raaga** knowledge to execute without losing the rhythmic cycle.
 
• The repertoire predominantly features **Aprachalit Raagas** (rare raagas) and **Jod Raagas** (compound raagas) such as **Lalita-Gauri**, **Jaitashree**, and **Sampoorna-Malkouns**, rather than common scales.
 
• Exponents like **Kesarbai Kerkar**, who was a **Padma Bhushan** recipient, and **Kishori Amonkar**, known for her innovative **Ras-Siddhant** approach, are the most celebrated figures of this tradition.
 
• The singing is characterized by a **steady medium tempo** (Madhya Laya), avoiding the very slow **Vilambit** used by other schools, ensuring a tight integration between **Swar** (note) and **Laya** (rhythm).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gwalior Gharana**

 
 
• Regarded as the **mother of all gharanas**, it was founded by **Ustad Hassu Khan** and **Haddu Khan**.
 
• Focuses on **lucidity**, simple **straight taans**, and the structural purity of the **Bandish**.
 
 
 
• **Agra Gharana**
 
 
• Founded by **Haji Sujan Khan** and later redefined by **Ustad Faiyaz Khan**, also known as **Aftab-e-Mausiqi**.
 
• Known for its **powerful resonance**, use of **Nom-Tom Alap**, and strong rhythmic play (**Layakari**).
 
 
 
• **Kirana Gharana**
 
 
• Established by **Ustad Abdul Karim Khan** and **Ustad Abdul Wahid Khan**, focusing heavily on **perfect intonation** (Swar).
 
• Famous for the **Barhat** technique, where the **Raaga** is expanded note-by-note with great emotional depth.

• The Natya-Shastra also discusses the role of the audience and the impact of the performance on the viewers.

question: Which Indian state is known for its traditional martial art, Gatka?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Punjab**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gatka** is a traditional **martial art** form that originated in the **Punjab** region of India and is deeply rooted in the history of the **Sikh community**.
 
• It is essentially a style of stick-fighting that employs wooden sticks, known as **Soti**, and leather shields, called **Phari**, to simulate sword combat.
 
• The practice was formally introduced and encouraged by **Guru Hargobind Ji**, the **Sixth Sikh Guru**, who advocated for the militarization of Sikhs for self-defense and justice.
 
• It reached its peak under the **Tenth Sikh Guru**, **Guru Gobind Singh Ji**, who mandated martial training for the **Khalsa** warriors in the late **17th century**.
 
• The art transitioned from a battlefield technique to a performance art and **competitive sport** during the British colonial period when the use of traditional weapons was restricted.
 
• Today, **Gatka** is an integral part of **Sikh festivals** and religious processions, especially during **Hola Mohalla** and **Vaisakhi**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Indigenous Sports Promotion**:

 
 
• The Government of India has officially recognized **Gatka** as a competitive sport, including it in the **Khelo India Youth Games** to preserve its cultural heritage.
 
• Other traditional martial arts promoted alongside it include **Kalaripayattu** from **Kerala**, **Thang-Ta** from **Manipur**, and **Mallakhamba** from **Madhya Pradesh** and **Maharashtra**.
 
 
 
• **Regional Martial Traditions**:
 
 
• **Haryana**: Predominantly famous for **Kushti** (traditional wrestling), making it a powerhouse for **Olympic** sports in India.
 
• **Rajasthan**: Known for **Shastar Vidya** and various Rajput warrior traditions involving swordsmanship and archery.
 
• **Gujarat**: While not known for a combat martial art like Gatka, it is famous for **Dandiya Raas**, which utilizes sticks for rhythmic folk dance.

question: Pandit Ravi Shankar popularised which instrument in particular all over the world?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sitar**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ravi Shankar **is renowned for popularizing the sitar, an Indian stringed instrument, globally. Shankar was a virtuoso of the sitar, an intricate instrument with a captivating resonance.
 
• Born on April 7, 1920, he commenced his performing career at the age of 14 as a dancer in his brother Uday's ensemble.
 
• Throughout the latter half of the 20th century, he ascended to become the foremost ambassador of North Indian classical music on the global stage.
 
• Shankar's artistic oeuvre encompasses a diverse range of endeavors, from composing pieces for orchestras to fusing clarinets with traditional Indian melodies, and even imparting sitar lessons to George Harrison, the guitarist of the Beatles.
 
• Additionally, he is the father of the acclaimed singer-songwriter Norah Jones.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **"sitar" **originates from the Persian word "sehtar," translating to "three-stringed." Believed to have evolved from long-necked lutes brought to India from Central Asia, the sitar reached its pinnacle during the 16th and 17th centuries before attaining its current form in the 18th century.
 
• **Tabla** comprises a pair of hand drums indigenous to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **The veena** encompasses various chordophone instruments native to the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Harmonium** resembles an organ and operates as a portable, hand-pumped reed organ, finding popularity across the Indian subcontinent.

question: Pandit Ram Narayan a famous instrumentalist, is known for playing which of the following instruments?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sarangi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandit Ram Narayan** is a renowned **instrumentalist**.
 
• He is known for playing the **Sarangi**, a traditional **Indian bowed string instrument**.
 
• **Narayan **is credited with **popularizing the sarangi** as a s**olo instrument** in **classical music**.
 
• He has made significant contributions to the development and recognition of the **sarangi internationally**.
 
• The awards received by **Pandit Ram Narayan**
 
 
• **Padma Vibhushan** (2005)
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Award** (1964)
 
• **Padma Bhushan** (1991)
 
• **Sangeet Natak Akademi Fellowship** (2009)
 
• **SNA Tagore Ratna** (2015)
 
• **Bharat Ratna Pandit Bhimsen Joshi Lifetime Achievement Award** (2014)
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ghatam**

 
 
• A percussion instrument originating from **South India**.
 
• **Made from clay**, usually with a **narrow mouth** at the top and a **wide base**.
 
• **Played by striking** the outer surface with the **fingers, palms, and sometimes with a stick**.
 
• Produces a **variety of tones **depending on where it is** struck** and the **force applied**.
 
• Often used in **Carnatic music concerts** and **accompanies dance performances**.
 
 
 
• **Veena**'
 
 
• A traditional **Indian string instrument**.
 
• Comes in various forms such as the **Saraswati veena**, **Rudra veena**, and **Vichitra veena**.
 
• Prominent in **Indian classical music**, particularly in **Carnatic and Hindustani traditions**.
 
• Often associated with the **Hindu goddess Saraswati**, the deity of **knowledge, arts, and music**.
 
 
 
• **Sarod**
 
 
• A fretless string instrument from the **Indian subcontinent**.
 
• Typically has **four to six main strings **and a number of **sympathetic strings**.
 
• Integral to **Hindustani classical music **and also used in some forms of **folk and fusion music**.
 
• Prominent performers include **Ali Akbar Khan**, **Amjad Ali Khan**, and **Buddhadev Das Gupta**.

__
 
• **Pandit Harashankar Bhattacharya** is a renowned **sitar maestro, **widely regarded as one of **India's foremost sitarists.**
 
• His musical journey has been marked by prestigious performances on** All India Radio (AIR)** and television as an **"A-TOP" artist.**

• Following his relocation to Kolkata, Bhattacharya assumed the role of the Government of West Bengal's senior sitarist in Information and Cultural Affairs.

• Primarily featured in Hindustani classical music, this genre is distinguished by intricate rhythmic structures, ornate melodies, and extensive improvisation.
 
• Measuring approximately 4 feet (1.2 meters) in length, the sitar typically features a pear-shaped gourd body and a lengthy, broad, hollow wooden neck.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pandavani** is a traditional folk ballad form from **Chhattisgarh** that narrates tales from the ancient Indian epic, the **Mahabharata**.
 
• The lead narrator, known as the **Ragi**, prominently uses the **Tambura** (also called **Tanpura**) as both a musical instrument and a versatile **theatrical prop**.
 
• The **Tambura** used in this folk form is often decorated with **peacock feathers** and **small bells**, giving it a distinct visual identity associated with the performer.
 
• During the performance, the artist symbolically uses the **Tambura** to represent different objects, such as the **Gada** (mace) of **Bhima**, a bow, or a sword, to enhance the storytelling through **gestures**.
 
• The instrument provides a continuous **drone sound**, helping the performer maintain the pitch while shifting between singing and high-energy narration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Performance Styles**:

 
 
• **Vedamati Style**: The performer remains **seated** on the floor throughout the recital, focusing more on the vocal delivery.
 
• **Kapalik Style**: The performer is **mobile**, dancing and enacting characters, where the **Tambura** becomes a dynamic tool for dramatization.
 
 
 
• **Renowned Exponents**:
 
 
• **Teejan Bai**: A legendary artist of the **Kapalik style** who brought international fame to **Pandavani** and received the **Padma Vibhushan**.
 
• **Punaram Nishad**: A celebrated figure known for his mastery over the **Vedamati style** of narration.
 
 
 
• **Accompanying Instruments**:
 
 
• While the **Tambura** is the central prop, the ensemble typically includes the **Harmonium**, **Tabla**, **Dholak**, and **Manjira** (cymbals) to provide rhythmic and melodic support.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chenda** is a traditional percussion instrument prominently used in **Kathakali**, a classical dance-drama form of Kerala, India.
 
• The **Chenda** is cylindrical in shape and is played using two sticks, producing a loud and rhythmic sound essential for setting the tempo in Kathakali performances.
 
• It is the primary instrument used to create the **rhythmic base** for Kathakali, providing synchronization between the dance movements and the accompanying music.
 
• The instrument plays a vital role in enhancing the dramatic expressions of the performers by accentuating their gestures and footwork.
 
• In Kathakali, the **Chenda** is not only a musical instrument but also a device to convey emotions and intensify the theatrical elements of the performance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Pakhawaj:**

 
 
• The **Pakhawaj** is a barrel-shaped drum used primarily in Hindustani classical music and dance forms like Dhrupad.
 
• It is not typically associated with Kathakali performances.
 
• The Pakhawaj produces a deep, resonant sound and is played using both hands.
 
 
 
• **Veena:**
 
 
• The **Veena** is a stringed instrument used in Carnatic music and is not a percussion instrument.
 
• It is primarily used for melodic accompaniment rather than providing rhythmic support.
 
• Its presence is unrelated to Kathakali performances.
 
 
 
• **Tabla:**
 
 
• The **Tabla** is a pair of drums used extensively in Hindustani classical music and Bollywood music.
 
• It does not play a significant role in Kathakali, as its tonal structure does not align with the dramatic and rhythmic requirements of Kathakali.
 
 
 
• **Chenda:**
 
 
• The **Chenda** is deeply rooted in Kerala’s cultural traditions and is used in temple rituals and classical art forms like Kathakali and Theyyam.
 
• It is made from jackfruit wood and has leather skins on both ends, which are struck to produce a loud sound.
 
• It is played in a standing position, adding to its dynamic nature in performances.
 
• Its role is pivotal in creating dramatic impact and maintaining synchronization in Kathakali.

__
 
• **Mario de Miranda** was a renowned Indian cartoonist and painter, famous for his unique style of illustrations and sketches.
 
• He was born on **2 May 1926**, in the village of **Loutolim** in the state of **Goa**, India.
 
• His works often depicted **Goan culture, traditions, and everyday life**, which became iconic representations of the region’s essence.
 
• He gained national and international fame for his cartoons, which were published in leading magazines and newspapers like **The Times of India**, **The Illustrated Weekly of India**, and **The Economic Times**.
 
• Mario de Miranda was honored with several prestigious awards, including the **Padma Shri** in **1988** and the **Padma Bhushan** in **2002**, for his immense contribution to art and culture.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About Mario de Miranda's Art Style:**

 
 
• Mario's art style was characterized by its **witty humor, intricate detailing, and vibrant portrayal of life**.
 
• His works spanned diverse themes, including **urban life, rural landscapes, and political satire**.
 
• His unique ability to capture the essence of Goa and its people made his art timeless and widely appreciated.
 
 
 
• **Goa's Cultural Influence on Mario:**
 
 
• Goa’s rich cultural heritage, particularly its Portuguese influence, heavily inspired Mario’s works.
 
• His cartoons often depicted the Goan way of life, including vibrant festivals, local architecture, and social dynamics.
 
 
 
• **Other Contributions:**
 
 
• Apart from cartoons, Mario created murals, illustrations for children’s books, and art for advertisements.
 
• He also worked internationally, contributing to publications like **Mad magazine** and **Lilliput** magazine.
 
 
 
• **Recognition and Legacy:**
 
 
• Mario de Miranda’s works are preserved in various museums and galleries, including the **Mario Gallery in Goa**.
 
• His art continues to inspire contemporary artists and cartoonists across the globe.

• In this art form,** the French naut open work and Herringbone stitch techniques are used.**
 
• Chikan saris and Kurtas are the perfect summer wear.
 
• The most popular origin story credits **Noor Jahan, Mughal empress**, and wife of Jahangir, with i**ntroducing Chikankari **to India.
 
• Chikan embroidery is mostly done on fabrics like** cotton, semi-Georgette, pure Georgette, crepe, chiffon, silk, and any other fabric which is light and which highlights the embroidery.**
 
• The fabric **cannot** be too** thick or hard, **else the embroidery needle won't pierce it.
 
 
 
• **Hence, option 4 is correct.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Crochet :**

 
 
• Crochet is a process of** creating textiles by using a crochet hook to interlock loops of yarn, thread, or strands of other materials.**
 
• The name is derived from the** French term crochet, meaning 'small hook'.**
 
• Hooks can be made from **a variety of materials, such as metal, wood, bamboo, or plastic.**
 
 
 
• **Needle lace :**
 
 
• It is a type of **lace created using a needle and thread to stitch up hundreds of small stitches** to form the lace itself.
 
• In its purest form, the only equipment and materials used are **a needle, thread, and scissors.**

• It played a vital role in the Indian independence movement, first sung in a political context by Rabindranath Tagore at the 1896 session of the Indian National Congress. 
 
 

 
• Bankim Chandra Chatterjee or Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay:

subject: GK
question: ‘Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri’ was originally written in which of the following languages?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Persian**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

**Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri (or Jahangirnama)**

__
 
• Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri or Jahangir-nama is the **autobiography of Mughal Emperor Nur-ud-din Muhammad Jahangir **(1569–1627).
 
• **It is written in Persian **and follows the tradition of his great-grandfather, Babur (1487–1530), who had written the Baburnama.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The autobiography is a unique piece of literature that shows his power of expression and observation. 
 
• **In it, he not only provided the history of his reign but also gave details viz. his perception of art, politics and also information about his family.**
 
• The Memoirs of the first twelve years, when completed, were bound and presented to imperial officers, the first person to get a copy was Prince Khurram, the emperor's son (later emperor Shahjahan).
 
• The Tuzuk-i-Jahangiri is the most important sourcebook for the reconstruction of the history of the Mughal empire in the reign of Jahangir.
 
• **Jahangir twice mentions a tower, tank, and pavilion used as a hunting palace about 29 km from Lahore.**
 
• Today the site is known as Shaikhupura, but Jahangir in 1606 refers to it as Jahangirpura and then in 1620 calls it Jahangirabad, both meaning the City of Jahangir, the latter a more Persianate form. 
 
• Although Jahangir's father Akbar prepared the scheme for conquering Bengal, the Mughal conquest of Bengal was completed in the reign of Jahangir and the credit is given to Subahdar Islam khan Chisti.
 
• Tuzuk is also a very important source for the history of the Mughal expansion in Bengal.

 Chhau

• Bhootada Kola is **performed** in **small local communities **in rural parts of Dakshina Kannada and Udupi districts.
 
• Bhootada Kola is not a tourist event and is not advertised much in mainstream media.

question: Which folk dance represents a mock fight between Goddess Durga and Mahishasura?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dandiya Raas.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Raas or Dandiya rass** is a** socio-religious folk danc**e, that originated in the **Gujarat region of India.**
 
• It is frequently done during the **Navaratri celebration.**
 
• The dance is done in **Rajasthan's Marwar.**
 
• Sanskrit terms **"Nava" (which means "Nine") and "Ratri" (which means nights) **are used to celebrate the **Hindu deity Shakti,** which means **Strength or Power.**
 
• With the help of Dandiya Raas, the** nine manifestations **of Shakti/Devi are worshipped.
 
• This traditional dance depicts a f**ictitious conflict between Mahishasura and Goddess Durga.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bhangra:**

 
 
• Bhangra is a traditional **folk dance of Punjab.**
 
• It takes place during the **harvesting season.**
 
• Bhangra is particularly connected to the** springtime Vaisakhi festival.**
 
 
 
• **Raslila:**
 
 
• The Raslila or Ras dance is a scene from the **popular Krishna tale** found in Hindu scriptures, in which** Krishna dances with Radha and Braj gopis.**
 
 
 
• **Kalbelia:**
 
 
• The Kalbelia are a snake-taming tribe from Rajasthan, India's Thar Desert.
 
• Men play the instruments and give the music, but only women perform it.

question: Which is one of the most famous dance forms of Assam performed by the 'Kulis' (people who work in the tea gardens) during autumn?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Jhumur dance.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jhumur is a traditional dance of the tea ethnical communities of Assam **and also in some corridors of **West Bengal.**
 
• It's generally performed in the crop season and carnivals.
 
• The main players of the **act are girls, but the music, lyrics, and instruments for the performance are maintained by the manly players.**
 
• Jhumur dance is substantially performed on carnivals like Karam puja and Tushu puja.
 
• Karam puja is one of the most important carnivals for the tea lines.
 
• It's a week-long festivity to worship Karam Raja.
 
• For an entire week, songs are sung, balls are danced, and people stay up late at night to celebrate and worship.

 [IMAGE: https://3.bp.blogspot.com/-zydoF8tG690/V-PBGP85G-I/AAAAAAAABuM/a4umezoU5FoigveGdL-IHosI1h08tSXHACLcB/s1600/2222.jpg] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahasu Dance:**

 
 
• Mahasu is one of the colourful forms of the Nati folk dance of Himachal Pradesh.
 
• The dance is called Mahasu presumably because it began in the region of the Mahasu Pahari-speaking area.
 
• In Himachal Pradesh, Mahasu Pahari is spoken in a veritably large region which includes further than ten lakh people.
 
• It's substantially spoken in Shimla and Solan.
 
 
 
• **Lambadi dance:**
 
 
• Lambadi dance is a folk dance of the Banjara tribe.
 
• It originated in the Anupu Village of Andhra Pradesh.
 
• A lot of folk dances have originated in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana. 
 
 
 
• **Karga dance:**
 
 
• Karaga folk dance is a traditional dance devoted to Draupadi.
 
• It is performed on a full moon night. It is also known as Droupthamma.
 
• Karaga is celebrated by the Tigala group in the Karnataka region.

question: Bhutia dance is performed in which of the following states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sikkim**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Bhutia dance:-**

 
 
• **It is an integral part of Bhutia culture, traditionally performed during festivals, celebrations, and community gatherings. **
 
• These vibrant dances showcase the rich heritage and storytelling traditions of the Bhutia people, an indigenous group inhabiting the Himalayan regions of India, Nepal, and Bhutan.
 
• **In India, it is performed in Sikkim.**
 
• Bhutia dances are characterized by their energetic movements, colorful costumes, and lively music. Some of the most popular Bhutia dances include:
 
 
• **Denzong-Neh-Na**: This lively dance is performed by both men and women and mimics the movements of birds in flight.
 
• **Ta-Shi-Yang-Ku**: This graceful dance is performed by women and depicts the movements of swans gliding across a lake.
 
• **Tashi Shabdo:** This energetic dance is performed by men and showcases their strength and agility.
 
 
 
• Bhutia dance costumes are elaborate and colorful, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of the Bhutia people. Men typically wear long robes and hats, while women wear colorful dresses and jewelry.
 
• The music for Bhutia dances is traditionally played on instruments such as drums, flutes, and cymbals. 
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **West Bengal:-**

 
 
• **It is a state in eastern India known for its rich cultural heritage, vibrant festivals, and stunning natural beauty. **
 
• The state's capital is Kolkata, formerly known as Calcutta, which is a major commercial and cultural hub.
 
• West Bengal is famous for its exquisite handicrafts, delicious cuisine, and renowned literary figures.
 
• The state is also home to the Sundarbans, the world's largest mangrove forest, which is a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Odisha:-**
 
 
• **It is a state in eastern India known for its ancient temples, breathtaking beaches, and vibrant tribal culture. **
 
• The state's capital is Bhubaneswar, which is known as the "Temple City of India" for its numerous ancient temples.
 
• Odisha is also famous for its rich handloom tradition, exquisite handicrafts, and delicious cuisine.
 
• The state is home to the Lingaraj Temple, one of the largest temples in India, and the Konark Sun Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage Site.
 
 
 
• **Nagaland:-**
 
 
• **It is a state in northeastern India known for its lush green hills, colorful festivals, and unique tribal culture. **
 
• The state's capital is Kohima, which is known as the "Land of the Nagas". Nagaland is famous for its rich biodiversity, vibrant festivals, and traditional crafts.
 
• The state is home to the Naga people, who are divided into numerous tribes, each with its own distinct culture, language, and traditions.

question: Dr.Teejan Bai, a Padma Shri, Padma Bhushan and Padma Vibhushan awardee is globally recognised for her contribution to which of the following art forms?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pandavani.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Teejan Bai:-**

 
 
• She was born on August 8, 1956, in the village of Ghughara, Chandrapur district of Chhattisgarh, India.
 
• **She hails from the Gond tribal community, and her family has a rich tradition of Pandavani, a traditional storytelling art form that narrates tales from the epic Mahabharata.**
 
• Teejan Bai's contributions to Pandavani have been recognized with numerous prestigious awards, including Padma Shri in 1987, Padma Bhushan in 2003, Padma Vibhushan, the 2nd highest civilian award in India, in 2019, and Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 1995.
 
 
 
• **Pandwani means Pandavwani **– that is Panda Katha, a story of Mahabharata. Pandwani is a folk ballad form performed predominantly in Chhattisgarh.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gendi:-**

 
 
• **It is a lively and energetic dance performed during festivals and celebrations.**
 
• It is characterized by its acrobatic movements, where dancers balance themselves on two long bamboo poles, performing intricate steps and twirls.
 
 
 
• **Raut Nacha:-**
 
 
• **It is a dramatic and narrative dance that depicts the story of Lord Krishna and his battles against the evil forces of King Kansa. **
 
• The dance is performed by men dressed as cowherds, wielding sticks and shields, enacting the scenes of Krishna's bravery and triumph.
 
 
 
• **Jhirliti:-**
 
 
• **It is a unique and playful dance performed by children during festivals and celebrations. **
 
• It is characterized by its whimsical and impromptu nature, where children dress up in colorful rags and masks, dancing in circles and performing playful antics.
 
• The dance is accompanied by the sounds of clapping, singing, and makeshift instruments, creating a joyful and lighthearted atmosphere.

question: Thullal dance originated in which of the following states?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Thullal, **a solo satiric dance form, **originated in Kerala, **India, during the **18th century,** credited to **Kunchan Nambiar,** one of the renowned **Malayalam poets **known as the **Prachina Kavithrayam**.
 
• This art form combines dance and drama, with the performer singing and narrating stories, which requires considerable skill.
 
• Thullal often portrays aspects of the literary, artistic, and cultural milieu of **medieval Kerala**, with episodes from Indian epics presented through straightforward Malayalam poetry.
 
• There are three primary forms of thullal: Ottan Thullal, Parayan Thullal, and Sheethankan Thullal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Some **traditional dance forms **from **Kerala**:
 
• **Kathakali: **Known for its elaborate makeup and expressive movements, Kathakali is a classical dance-drama that depicts stories from Hindu mythology through captivating performances.
 
• **Mohiniyattam:** Celebrated for its graceful movements and subtle expressions, Mohiniyattam is a traditional dance form performed mainly by women, showcasing stories of love and devotion.
 
• **Thullal: **Originating in the 18th century, Thullal is a solo satirical dance form introduced by Kunchan Nambiar, featuring storytelling through song and dance, often reflecting Kerala's literary and cultural life.
 
• **Koodiyattam: **Recognized as one of the oldest classical theater forms in the world, Koodiyattam combines dance, music, and drama to present stories from Hindu epics with intricate choreography and vibrant costumes.

question: Which dance from Assam involves a group of dancers performing in circles or rows, often accompanied by drums and pipes, to celebrate the Bihu festival?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bihu**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Bihu** is a traditional dance form of Assam, performed during the **Bihu festival**, which is one of the most significant cultural celebrations in the region.
 
• The dance is characterized by its **lively movements**, performed in circles or rows, and is accompanied by traditional instruments like **drums (dhol), pipes (pepa), and cymbals (toka).**
 
• The Bihu festival marks the **Assamese New Year** and is celebrated to express gratitude for a good harvest and to welcome the spring season.
 
• This dance involves **vigorous hand and foot movements**, reflecting the joy and energy of the festival, and is performed by both men and women, wearing traditional Assamese attire.
 
• Bihu dance is a symbol of Assamese culture and heritage and has gained recognition both nationally and internationally for its **vibrant and energetic performances.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Bagurumba:**

 
 
• Bagurumba is a folk dance of the **Bodo community** in Assam.
 
• It is also known as the **butterfly dance** due to its graceful movements resembling a butterfly's flight.
 
• Performed by Bodo women, this dance is often associated with nature and is typically performed during the **Bwisagu festival**.
 
 
 
• **Dhol Cholom:**
 
 
• Dhol Cholom is a traditional dance from **Manipur**, performed during the festival of **Holi**.
 
• This dance involves vigorous drumming on the dhol and synchronized movements by performers, showcasing their **strength and rhythm.**
 
• It is not associated with the Bihu festival or Assamese culture.
 
 
 
• **Hojagiri:**
 
 
• Hojagiri is a traditional dance of the **Reang (Bru) tribe** of Tripura.
 
• This dance is performed by women balancing earthen pots on their heads and showcasing intricate footwork and movements.
 
• It is distinct from the Bihu dance and is associated with the **Hojagiri festival**.
 
 
 
• **Bihu Festival:**
 
 
• The Bihu festival is celebrated in three forms: **Bohag Bihu** (spring), **Magh Bihu** (harvest), and **Kati Bihu** (sowing).
 
• It is a time of **feasting, dancing, and singing**, reflecting the cultural and agricultural heritage of Assam.
 
• The traditional attire includes **mekhela chador** for women and dhoti-gamosa for men.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• Bihu dance is performed during **Bohag Bihu**, which is celebrated in April and marks the beginning of the Assamese New Year.
 
• The dance is an integral part of the festivities, symbolizing joy, prosperity, and the vibrant spirit of the Assamese people.
 
• It has been recognized as a **representation of India’s rich cultural diversity** on various platforms, including international cultural festivals.
 
• Assamese musical instruments like the **pepa** (a wind instrument made from buffalo horn) and the **dhol** play a pivotal role in the performance, adding to its energy and rhythm.

question: Which traditional dance from Uttar Pradesh involves women carrying lighted oil lamps on their heads?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Charkula**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Charkula** is a spectacular folk dance that originated in the **Braj region** of **Western Uttar Pradesh**, an area deeply associated with the legends of **Lord Krishna**.
 
• The dance is traditionally performed by women to celebrate the birth of **Radha**, the consort of **Lord Krishna**, specifically on the third day after **Holi** (known as **Dooj**).
 
• Performers balance a heavy, multi-tiered circular wooden pyramid called a **Charkula** on their heads; this structure typically holds exactly **108 lighted oil lamps** (diyas) arranged in tiers.
 
• The wooden structure can weigh between **40 to 50 kilograms**, and dancers must maintain perfect balance while moving to the rhythmic beats of **Nagada** (drums) and **Rasiya** folk songs.
 
• Legend suggests that **Radha’s grandmother** ran out of her house with a chariot wheel on her head to announce **Radha’s birth**, which eventually evolved into this unique lamp-balancing dance form.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Raslila**:

 
 
• A major dance-drama form from the **Braj region** of **Uttar Pradesh**, depicting the divine love and childhood pranks of **Lord Krishna** and the **Gopis**.
 
• It is an integral part of festivals like **Janmashtami** and is performed in sacred towns like **Mathura** and **Vrindavan**.
 
 
 
• **Giddha**:
 
 
• A high-energy, traditional folk dance from the state of **Punjab**, performed exclusively by **women** during festive or social occasions like **Teeyan**.
 
• It is characterized by the singing of **Boliyan** (couplets) and rhythmic clapping, reflecting the grace and vibrant spirit of Punjabi culture.
 
 
 
• **Bhangra**:
 
 
• One of the most popular folk dances of **Punjab**, traditionally performed by men to celebrate the **Vaisakhi** harvest festival.
 
• It involves athletic movements and is performed to the powerful beat of the **Dhol** drum.

solution:
__
 
• The **Purna Kumbh Mela **takes place every **twelve years** at one of the four places by rotation, **Prayag, Haridwar, Ujjain and Nashik.**
 
• **Kumbh Mela -**__ 
 
 
• The Kumbh Mela is a major Hindu festival and pilgrimage.
 
• The mela is held every three years, and switches between four different locations – **Haridwar (river Ganga**), **Prayag (Triveni sangam of Yamuna, Ganga and Saraswati)**, **Ujjain (river Kshipra)**, and **Nasik (river Godavari)**
 
• The mela returns to each location after a span of **12 years**.
 
• The Kumbh Mela is related to the Hindu mythological story of ***“Samudra Manthan”*** or the churning of nectar.
 
• The **“kumbh”** actually means ***pot***, signifying the pot holding the Amrita (nectar) churned out during Samudra Manthan.
 
• As per the story, after Samudra Manthan, the Asuras ran behind devas to get the nectar of immortality.
 
• During the chase some of the nectar fell on the four locations and hence these four locations are worshiped and revered.
 
• Hindus believe bathing in the holy water at the four locations during Kumbh washes away their sins and bless them with divine power.
