__
 
• **Jamshedi Navroz is a festival of Zoroastrian origin that marks the day of the vernal equinox in March every year and is celebrated by Parsis in India.**

 
 
• The Parsi New Year is a regional holiday celebrated on the first day of the Zoroastrian calendar’s first month, Farvardin.
 
• It is also known as Navroz, which is derived from ‘Nav’ and ‘Roz’, meaning new and day respectively in Persian.
 
 
 
• The festival falls every year on Spring Equinox around 21st March.
 
 
• But the Parsi community in India follows the Shahenshahi calendar and thus celebrates their new year later in July or August.
 
• In 2021, the Parsi New Year will be observed on 16th August (Monday) in India.

• Places to Observe Parsi New Year’s Day in India:
 
 
• **Gujarat, Maharashtra**
 
 
 
• On this day, Parsis clean the house and decorate with flowers and rangoli to make it look beautiful and welcoming for visitors.
 
• Dressed up in** traditional attire, **they visit the** Fire Temple after breakfast and perform a prayer called Jashan** to express gratitude to the Lord,** pray for prosperity and seek His forgiveness.**
 
• Milk, water, fruits, flowers, and sandalwood are put into the sacred fire as offerings.
 
• **Frawardigan :**
 
 
• Frawardigan is **a ten-day period at the end of the Zoroastrian religious** year during which** the souls of the dead are commemorated.**
 
• The name frawardigan is a Zoroastrian Middle Persian allusion to the fravashis, which – among other aspects – also include the souls of the dead.
 
 
 
• **Khordad Sal :**
 
 
• Khordad Sal is **the birth anniversary of Zoroaster.**
 
• Zoroastrians all over the world, especially the Parsis of India,** celebrate the day in great glamour.**
 
• Parties and ghambars are held.
 
• Special prayers and jashan are also held throughout the entire day.

• Each festival historically commemorates a **distinct paddy crop **agriculture cycle.

__
 
• **Onam,** the vibrant cultural festival celebrated in **South India**, holds deep roots in the legend of **King Mahabali.**
 
• According to local folklore, Kerala was once under the rule of the **benevolent Asura (demon) king**, Mahabali, also affectionately known as Maveli or Onathappan.
 
• Despite his demon status, Mahabali was revered for his unparalleled generosity and compassion. His reign was hailed as a golden era marked by joy, harmony, and abundance.
 
• Each year, during the** ten-day Onam festivities,** the people of Kerala eagerly anticipate the symbolic return of their beloved king.
 
• The poignant folk song **"Maveli nadu vaneedum kalam"** poignantly recounts Mahabali's selfless sacrifice and resonates deeply with the spirit of Onam.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Gudi Padwa,** also referred to as the Marathi New Year or Hindu New Year, is a festive occasion primarily celebrated by Marathi and Konkani Hindus. It is observed in regions such as Maharashtra, Goa, and Daman. The term "Gudi" symbolizes a flag, while "Padwa" denotes the first day of the lunar fortnight.
 
• **Ugadi,** alternatively known as Yugadi, is a significant Hindu festival marking the commencement of the New Year. It is predominantly celebrated in the states of Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, and Karnataka in India. The term "Ugadi" originates from the Sanskrit words "yuga" (age) and "adi" (beginning), symbolizing the onset of a new age or era.
 
• **Pongal** holds immense importance among Tamil people in Tamil Nadu, Sri Lanka, and the global Tamil diaspora. Celebrated over three or four days, each day of Pongal is marked by distinct rituals. The four consecutive days are Bhogi, Surya Pongal, Mattu Pongal, and Kanum Pongal. This festival venerates Surya, the solar deity in Hinduism, and aligns with the occasion of Makar Sankranti.

__
 
• **The Chad Sukra festival** is celebrated by the **Jaintia tribe of Meghalaya, **also known as the **Pnar people, every year in April.**
 
• The festival honors the start of the sowing season and is also a way to ask for protection from natural calamities that could harm crops.
 
• The festival dates back to the **Jaintia Kingdom**, when the king would move his court from **Sutnga to Jaintiapur,** and people from all over the kingdom would perform for him and his ministers at the start of spring.
 
• The word Chad Sukra literally means "dance with a joyful heart, with health and vitality".
 
• During the festival, farmers offer prayers to mother earth and thank her for her blessings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In addition to rituals and prayers, the Chad Sukra festival features traditional dances, including the **"Laho" dance.**
 
• In this dance, two young men flank a girl, linking arms with her, and they dance together in synchronized steps.
 
• Women participating in the festival adorn themselves in traditional attire such as ryndia stem, thoh saru, khyrwang, sapjat, kein shrooh/kyrshah, while men wear iuslein pyniein, iuspong, ryndia tlem, among others.
 
• Furthermore, women embellish their attire with ornaments like paila, khoila (earrings), and khadu (bracelets), adding to the festive atmosphere of the occasion.

• **Vaishakha**
 
 
• Vaishakha is the second month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar and follows Chaitra.
 
• It typically overlaps with April and May in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• Vaishakha is associated with several festivals, including **Akshaya Tritiya** and Buddha Purnima.
 
 
 
• **Magha**
 
 
• Magha is the eleventh month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar.
 
• It corresponds to January-February in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The month is significant for its religious observances such as **Magha Purnima** and the Kumbh Mela held every twelve years.
 
 
 
• **Kartika**
 
 
• Kartika is the eighth month of the Hindu lunisolar calendar.
 
• It typically overlaps with October and November in the Gregorian calendar.
 
• The month is considered highly auspicious, with festivals such as **Kartik Purnima** and Diwali being observed during this period.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Ugadi**
 
 
• Ugadi is celebrated as the beginning of a new year and is a time for introspection, renewal, and hope.
 
• The festival reflects the cultural and agricultural significance of the region, marking the end of the harvest season and the onset of the spring season.

question: In which Indian state is Onam celebrated?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Onam** is an annual harvest festival celebrated predominantly in the Indian state of **Kerala**, marking the homecoming of King Mahabali.
 
• It is observed during the **Malayalam month of Chingam**, which usually falls in **August–September**.
 
• Onam is a celebration that includes **traditional feasts** (called Onasadya), **Pookkalam** (floral decorations), **Vallam Kali** (boat races), **Pulikali** (tiger dances), and **Kathakali performances**.
 
• The festival is deeply rooted in Kerala’s culture and is celebrated by people of all religions, showcasing unity and harmony.
 
• Onam has been officially recognized as the **state festival of Kerala** due to its historical, cultural, and social significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Historical Background of Onam:**

 
 
• According to legend, Onam is celebrated to honor the **benevolent King Mahabali**, who ruled Kerala and was known for his generosity, fairness, and prosperity.
 
• It is believed that the **Vamana avatar** of Lord Vishnu sent King Mahabali to the netherworld, but granted him permission to visit his people once a year, which is celebrated as Onam.
 
 
 
• **Onasadya:**
 
 
• Onasadya is a grand feast served on a banana leaf and consists of approximately **26 traditional dishes**, including rice, sambar, avial, thoran, and payasam.
 
• This feast is an integral part of the celebration and reflects Kerala’s culinary heritage.
 
 
 
• **Vallam Kali (Boat Race):**
 
 
• Vallam Kali is a traditional snake boat race held during Onam, with the **Nehru Trophy Boat Race** being the most famous.
 
• It showcases Kerala’s maritime traditions and involves synchronized rowing by hundreds of participants.
 
 
 
• **Pookkalam:**
 
 
• Pookkalam refers to the intricate floral designs made on the ground using colorful flowers to welcome King Mahabali.
 
• These designs symbolize prosperity and are created by families and communities during the festival.
 
 
 
• **Unity in Diversity:**
 
 
• Onam is celebrated by people of all religions and communities in Kerala, highlighting the state’s **diverse and inclusive culture**.
 
• It serves as a platform for cultural expression and communal harmony.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Recognition as State Festival:** Onam is officially recognized as Kerala’s state festival due to its cultural, historical, and social relevance.
 
• **Economic Impact:** The festival boosts the economy of Kerala through tourism, local markets, and cultural events.
 
• **Tourism Attraction:** Onam attracts tourists globally who come to experience Kerala’s traditional art forms, feasts, and celebrations.
 
• **Government Involvement:** The Kerala government organizes events and competitions during Onam, including fairs, cultural programs, and exhibitions.
 
• **Global Observance:** Malayali communities worldwide celebrate Onam, showcasing Kerala’s cultural heritage on a global stage.

question: What is the primary focus of the Sohrai festival celebrated in Jharkhand?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Worshiping cattle**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sohrai festival** is primarily celebrated in the state of **Jharkhand**, India, and is an important tribal harvest festival.
 
• The festival is centered around **worshiping cattle**, as they play a significant role in agricultural activities and rural life.
 
• **Cattle** are considered sacred and vital for farming, as they assist in plowing fields and transporting goods.
 
• During Sohrai, cattle are **cleaned, decorated, and worshipped** to express gratitude for their contribution to agricultural productivity.
 
• The celebration involves **traditional rituals, folk songs, and Sohrai art**, which include wall paintings created using natural pigments and inspired by tribal beliefs.
 
• The festival also marks the beginning of the harvest season, signifying prosperity and abundance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sohrai Festival:**

 
 
• The Sohrai festival is celebrated by **tribal communities like the Santhal, Oraon, and Munda** in Jharkhand, along with neighboring states such as Bihar and West Bengal.
 
• It generally takes place during the **Diwali season** (October-November) and coincides with the **autumn harvest**.
 
• The rituals involve **smearing cattle with oil and turmeric**, followed by painting traditional patterns on the walls of homes using materials like clay and natural dyes.
 
• The festival strengthens the bond between humans and animals and highlights the **importance of sustainable agriculture**.
 
 
 
• **Sohrai Art:**
 
 
• Sohrai art is a key cultural element of the festival. It involves **tribal wall paintings** made with natural pigments derived from soil, coal, and flowers.
 
• The paintings often depict themes of **nature, animals, and fertility**, showcasing the close connection of tribal communities with the environment.
 
• These artworks are typically created by women and reflect their **creativity and cultural heritage**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Cattle in Agriculture:**
 
 
• Cattle are vital for **plowing fields, transporting goods, and producing manure**, which enriches the soil for farming.
 
• In rural India, especially in tribal regions, cattle are regarded as **symbols of wealth and livelihood**.
 
• Worshiping cattle during Sohrai is seen as a gesture of **gratitude and respect** for their indispensable role in daily life.
 
 
 
• **Other Festivals Related to Cattle Worship:**
 
 
• Similar festivals are celebrated across India, such as **Pongal** in Tamil Nadu and **Makar Sankranti** in other states, where cattle are revered for their contribution to agriculture.
 
• In Tamil Nadu, the third day of Pongal, called **Mattu Pongal**, is dedicated to cattle worship.
 
• These festivals emphasize the significance of **harmonious coexistence** between humans and animals in agrarian societies.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tribal Traditions:** The festival reflects the **rich cultural heritage** and beliefs of tribal communities, emphasizing their deep connection with nature and agriculture.
 
• **Environmental Sustainability:** Practices such as using natural pigments in Sohrai art and respecting animals highlight the tribal commitment to **sustainable living**.
 
• **Regional Variations:** Although Sohrai is celebrated in Jharkhand, similar festivals across India show regional differences in rituals and practices while maintaining the central theme of **gratitude towards nature and animals**.
 
• **Economic Significance:** The festival also contributes to **local economies**, as it involves the purchase of decorations, art materials, and festive goods.

• The event takes place in **slushy paddy fields** filled with mud and water, where a pair of buffaloes are driven by a **jockey** over a distance of approximately 100 to 160 meters.
 
• Historically, the tradition is believed to be over **800 years old** and is deeply associated with the **farming community** of the **Tulu Nadu** region.
 
• The festival is dedicated to **Lord Kadri Manjunatha**, an incarnation of **Lord Shiva**, as a gesture of gratitude for a bountiful **harvest** and to keep the cattle free from diseases.
 
• The racing season typically begins in **November** and continues until **March**, featuring various competition categories such as **Kane Halage** and **Hagga Haaki**.

question: Which harvest festival in Tripura involves traditional tribal dances and rituals after jhum cultivation?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Garia Puja** is a major harvest festival celebrated in the northeastern state of **Tripura**, primarily by the **Tripuri** and **Jamatia** tribal communities.
 
• The festival is observed on the seventh day of the Hindu month of **Baishakh** (usually falling in **April**) to honor **Lord Garia**, the deity of livestock, wealth, and prosperity.
 
• It marks the successful conclusion of the **Jhum cultivation** cycle (shifting cultivation) and serves as a prayer for a prosperous new agricultural year.
 
• The ritualistic worship involves a symbolic **bamboo pole** decorated with garlands and thread, representing the deity, alongside offerings of fowls, eggs, and rice beer.
 
• A significant highlight is the **Garia dance**, where performers mimic the actions of agricultural labor and household chores through rhythmic movements and traditional music.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Moatsu**

 
 
• Celebrated by the **Ao Naga** tribe of **Nagaland** in the first week of **May**.
 
• It signifies the completion of the **sowing season** and involves community singing and the sharing of rice beer.
 
 
 
• **Losar**
 
 
• Known as the **Tibetan New Year**, it is widely celebrated in **Arunachal Pradesh** (by the **Monpa** tribe), **Ladakh**, and **Sikkim**.
 
• The festivities involve religious rituals at **monasteries** and traditional dances to ward off evil spirits.
 
 
 
• **Chapchar Kut**
 
 
• This is the most important festival of **Mizoram**, celebrated during **March**.
 
• It occurs after the clearing of forests for **Jhum** (burning of trees) and features the world-renowned **Cheraw** or bamboo dance.

question: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with respect to the Lyuva Khutla festival of the Mara tribe?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Festival Host - Chaypi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Lyuva Khutla** is the most significant and largest cultural festival of the **Mara people**, who primarily inhabit the **Mara Autonomous District Council** in the state of **Mizoram**.
 
• The festival is celebrated annually to mark the successful completion of **Jhum clearing** (slash-and-burn agriculture) and to offer thanks to the almighty for a successful season.
 
• The village of **Chaypi**, situated in the **Siaha district**, is historically recognized as a major host and epicenter for these grand celebrations, showcasing the tribe's rich heritage. ***Hence, Festival Host - Chaypi is correct.***
 
• **Bihu** is the traditional folk dance of **Assam**, and **Dalkhai** is the most popular folk dance of **Western Odisha**, neither of which belongs to the Mara tribe. ***Hence, Dances - Bihu & Dalkhai is incorrect.***
 
• The **Mekhela Chador** is the traditional indigenous dress of **Assamese women**, whereas the Mara people wear distinct traditional ethnic garments such as the **Viachhai**. ***Hence, Attire - Mekhela Chador is incorrect.***
 
• While modern festivities may include sports, the core of the **Lyuva Khutla** revolves around traditional rituals, folk songs, and community feasts rather than specific modern board games like **Ludo**. ***Hence, Modern Games - Ludo is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Lyuva Khutla**:

 
 
• Etymology: The term is derived from 'Lyuva' meaning a **newly cleared forest** for cultivation and 'Khutla' meaning **festival**.
 
• Cultural Significance: It features the famous **Pakhupila** (Butterfly Dance), which involves intricate footwork and rhythmic movements.
 
 
 
• **Mara Tribe**:
 
 
• Location: They are one of the major ethnic groups in **Mizoram**, concentrated in the southernmost part of the state.
 
• Governance: They are governed by the **Mara Autonomous District Council**, established under the **Sixth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution** in **1972**.
 
• History: Historically known as the **Lakher**, the community possesses a unique linguistic and cultural identity distinct from other **Mizo** sub-tribes.

question: The "Vallamkali" boat races of Kerala feature which unique type of boat, known for its length and speed?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chundan Vallam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The "Vallamkali" or boat races of Kerala are an integral part of the state's culture and tradition, primarily conducted during the festival of **Onam**.
 
• **Chundan Vallam**, also known as the **Snake Boat**, is the unique type of boat featured in these races. These boats are famous for their extraordinary **length, speed, and sleek design**.
 
• Chundan Vallam boats are characterized by their impressive length, often measuring **100 to 138 feet**, and can hold around **100 to 150 rowers**.
 
• These boats are traditionally crafted from the wood of the **Anjili tree (Artocarpus hirsutus)**, a durable and water-resistant material.
 
• The races are highly competitive and are accompanied by traditional songs known as **Vanchipattu**, which boost the morale of the rowers and add to the festive atmosphere.
 
• Chundan Vallam holds a historical significance as these boats were originally designed as **war boats** by the local rulers of Kerala.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Other Types of Vallam (Boats):**

 
 
• **Odi Vallam**: A smaller racing boat used in local races but not as prominent as Chundan Vallam.
 
• **Iruttukuthi Vallam**: Known for its speed, it is smaller in size compared to Chundan Vallam.
 
• **Churulan Vallam**: A smaller and round-shaped boat used for racing in some regions of Kerala.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Vallamkali:**
 
 
• The boat races are deeply rooted in Kerala's history, serving as a symbol of unity and teamwork among the participants.
 
• It is not just a sporting event but also a **spiritual offering** to the deities, often conducted at temple festivals.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Chundan Vallam:**
 
 
• The prow of the boat is raised high, resembling the hood of a snake, hence the name **Snake Boat**.
 
• It is manned by a synchronized team of rowers, steered by a **chief oarsman**, and accompanied by a group of singers.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Historical Context:**

 
 
• The Chundan Vallam was historically used as a war vessel to transport soldiers and goods, showcasing its robust design and utility.
 
 
 
• **Nehru Trophy Boat Race:**
 
 
• Named after India's first Prime Minister, **Jawaharlal Nehru**, who visited Kerala in 1952 and was fascinated by the Snake Boat races.
 
• This annual race is among the most prestigious Vallamkali events.

question: Which of the following best describes the Rajini Gerba ritual?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Purificatory animal-sacrifice ritual**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Rajini Gerba ritual** is a traditional practice observed in certain tribal communities in India, particularly in regions like Gujarat and Rajasthan.
 
• This ritual involves a **purificatory sacrifice of animals**, symbolizing the cleansing of individuals or communities from impurities or negative energies.
 
• The practice is deeply rooted in the tribal belief system, which emphasizes the role of sacrificial rituals in maintaining harmony between the community and the spiritual realm.
 
• The **animal sacrifice** in Rajini Gerba often holds symbolic significance, representing offerings to deities or spirits revered by the community.
 
• This ritual is primarily conducted during auspicious occasions or periods of perceived spiritual imbalance, aiming to restore peace and balance within the tribe.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Harvest Thanksgiving Dance:**

 
 
• This is a common tradition in agrarian societies where communities perform dances to express gratitude for a successful harvest.
 
• Unlike Rajini Gerba, this ritual does not involve animal sacrifice but focuses on communal celebration and gratitude.
 
• Examples include the **Bihu dance in Assam** and the **Pongal festival in Tamil Nadu**.
 
 
 
• **Temple Renovation Ceremony:**
 
 
• Temple renovation ceremonies are often performed in Hindu traditions to consecrate and restore temples.
 
• These ceremonies involve rituals such as **Kumbhabhishekam**, which include water, fire, and chanting of mantras.
 
• While sacred, these ceremonies differ from purificatory sacrifice as they focus on architectural and spiritual restoration rather than cleansing through sacrifice.
 
 
 
• **Community Storytelling Events:**
 
 
• These events are a form of oral tradition where communities gather to share folklore, myths, and historical narratives.
 
• Storytelling plays a crucial role in preserving cultural heritage but lacks the ritualistic and sacrificial components of Rajini Gerba.
 
• Examples include the **Panchatantra tales** and **Jataka stories** in Indian tradition.
 
 
 
• **Purificatory Rituals:**
 
 
• **Purificatory animal-sacrifice rituals** such as Rajini Gerba are part of tribal customs, signifying the removal of impurities and the restoration of spiritual balance.
 
• Animal sacrifice is often seen as an offering to deities and spirits, ensuring protection and blessings for the tribe.
 
• These rituals are deeply symbolic and align with the belief systems of tribal communities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of Animal Sacrifice:**

 
 
• In tribal rituals like Rajini Gerba, animal sacrifice serves as a spiritual offering to appease deities and ensure communal well-being.
 
• It symbolizes the relationship between humans and the divine, emphasizing gratitude and respect for spiritual forces.
 
 
 
• **Regional Variations:**
 
 
• Similar sacrificial rituals are observed in other tribal communities across India, with variations in the type of animals used and the ceremonial procedures.
 
• For instance, certain tribes in the northeastern states of India perform rituals involving chicken or pigs as sacrifices.
 
 
 
• **Cultural Context:**
 
 
• Rituals like Rajini Gerba reflect the unique cultural and spiritual heritage of tribal communities.
 
• They are often passed down through generations, preserving the identity and traditions of the tribe.

question: What is the primary objective of the Angami Sekrenyi festival?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Cleanse body and soul**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Sekrenyi** festival is the premier annual event of the **Angami Naga** tribe of **Nagaland**, which serves as a major cultural landmark for the community.
 
• The primary objective of the festival is **Phousanyi**, a term that signifies **purification**. It is observed to **cleanse the body and soul** of all past transgressions and misfortunes, seeking spiritual renewal.
 
• The celebration lasts for **ten days** and begins on the 25th day of the month of **Kezei** (which usually falls in February), marking the start of the **Angami lunar year**.
 
• A central theme of the festival is to bring **unity** and **sanctification** to the community, ensuring that the villagers enter the new agricultural cycle with a pure spirit and a healthy body.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Angami Naga Community**:

 
 
• The Angamis are one of the 17 major recognized tribes of **Nagaland**, primarily settled in the **Kohima** and **Chumoukedima** districts.
 
• They are famously known for their mastery in **terrace cultivation** and the preservation of rich oral traditions and folk music.
 
 
 
• **Ritualistic Highlights**:
 
 
• **Kizie Ritual**: This involves the symbolic sprinkling of **rice water** (Zhumho) from a leaf, intended to ward off **unlucky spirits** and illness.
 
• **Themlhu Day**: On the most sacred day, the village men perform a **ritual bath** at the village well before dawn. The water is treated as **holy**, and this act is believed to wash away all spiritual impurities.
 
• The festival features vibrant **traditional attire**, the preparation of local pork delicacies, and the communal sharing of **rice beer**, fostering social bonds.
 
 
 
• **Regional Significance**:
 
 
• While Sekrenyi is tribal-specific, Nagaland also hosts the famous **Hornbill Festival** in December, which showcases the collective heritage of all Naga tribes at the **Kisama Heritage Village**.

question: Siddheshvara Mahadeva temple in Bengal depicts the architecture of which dynasty?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pala dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Siddheshvara Mahadeva temple**, located in Barakar, Burdwan District, West Bengal, stands as an exemplary representation of the early **Pala style of architecture.**
 
• This distinctive style, prevalent from the 9th to the 11th centuries in Bengal and Bihar, derives its name from the Pala dynasty that reigned over the region during that era.
 
• Constructed in the 9th century, the Siddheshvara Mahadeva temple is a Hindu religious edifice characterized by its unique architectural features.
 
• Notably, it boasts a towering, curving shikhara (spire) adorned with a sizable amalaka (circular stone disk).
 
• This architectural style shares similarities with contemporary temples found in Odisha, showcasing the cultural exchange and artistic influences prevalent during that period.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Pala dynasty, **a ruling dynasty in Bihar and Bengal, India, held sway from the 8th to the 12th century. Its inception traces back to Gopala, a local chieftain who ascended to power in the mid-8th century amidst a period of turmoil and disorder.
 
• Gopala's successor, Dharmapala, reigned from around 770 to 810 and significantly expanded the kingdom, even briefly controlling Kannauj.
 
• Under the reign of Devapala (approximately 810–850), Pala dominance was sustained through military campaigns that extended into northern regions, the Deccan, and the peninsula.
 
• However, subsequent to Devapala's era, the dynasty witnessed a decline in power. Mahendrapala, the Gurjara-Pratihara emperor of Kannauj during the late 9th and early 10th centuries, even managed to penetrate northern Bengal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The Chalukya dynasty, **a prominent Hindu dynasty, held sway over significant territories in southern and central India from the 6th to the 12th centuries. Throughout this era, they governed as three interrelated yet distinct dynasties.
 
• **The Shunga dynasty** emerged as the seventh ruling dynasty of Magadha, exercising control over much of the northern Indian subcontinent from approximately 187 to 73 BCE.
 
• **The Hussain Shahi dynasty,** a familial lineage, assumed authority over the late medieval Sunni Muslim Sultanate of Bengal, reigning from 1494 to 1538.

question: Ker and Garia Puja are traditional tribal festivals of which state?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Tripura**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ker and Garia Puja** are traditional tribal festivals celebrated in Tripura, a northeastern state of India.
 
• **Ker Puja** is dedicated to Ker, the guardian deity of Vastu Devata. It occurs approximately two weeks after the Kharchi Puja in August. The term "Ker" signifies "austerity" and in the Kokborok language, the indigenous tribal language, it denotes "boundary" or "specific area".
 
• **Garia Puja**, on the other hand, is the most significant festival in Tripura. It spans seven days, commencing on the final day of the Chaitra month and concluding on the seventh day of the Vaisakha month. The last day of the festival is observed as a regional holiday. During Garia Puja, rituals are performed by a priest known as Ochai.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Tripura,** pronounced is a state located in Northeast India. It is the third-smallest state in the country, covering an area of 10,491 square kilometers (4,051 square miles).
 
• Despite its small size, it ranks as the seventh-least populous state, with a population of 3.67 million people.
 
• The state shares its borders with Assam and Mizoram to the east, and with Bangladesh to the north, south, and west.
 
• Tripura is administratively divided into 8 districts and 23 sub-divisions, with Agartala serving as both the capital and the largest city in the state.
 
• Tripura boasts a diverse demographic composition, with 19 distinct tribal communities coexisting alongside a predominant Bengali population. The official languages of the state are Bengali, English, and Kokborok.

question: Which Goddess is associated with the Gangaur Festival celebrated in Central and Western India?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Goddess Parvati**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Goddess Parvati** is associated with the Gangaur Festival celebrated in Central and Western India.
 
• **Gangaur** is a vibrant and significant festival celebrated by the people of Rajasthan, as well as in other Indian states like Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, and Uttar Pradesh.
 
• It is dedicated to the worship of Goddess Gauri (Parvati), the consort of Lord Shiva, and is observed with great zeal and devotion during the Hindu month of Chaitra, which typically falls in March or April.
 
• The festival symbolizes various aspects including the arrival of spring, the harvest season, marital fidelity, conjugal happiness, and fertility.
 
• Women play a central role in the celebrations, offering prayers to Goddess Gauri for blessings related to marriage, marital bliss, and the well-being of their husbands. Unmarried women seek the blessings of the goddess for a suitable life partner, while married women pray for the health, longevity, and prosperity of their husbands.
 
• Gangaur is characterized by colorful processions, traditional rituals, and cultural performances that showcase the rich heritage and traditions of the region. It serves as a time for communities to come together, celebrate, and express gratitude for the blessings bestowed upon them.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Parvati** is a revered Hindu goddess known for her association with the Himalayas, fertility, beauty, marriage, and the arts. She is considered one of the principal deities in Hinduism.
 
• **Saraswati** is another prominent Hindu goddess, symbolizing knowledge, music, and the arts. She is revered as the embodiment of wisdom and creativity.
 
• **Lakshmi,** often depicted as a goddess with lotus flowers, is worshipped as the deity of wealth, good fortune, happiness, youth, and beauty. She is highly esteemed in Hindu culture and is believed to bring prosperity to her devotees.
 
• **Kali **is a significant Hindu goddess associated with various aspects including time, change, creation, power, destruction, and death in the Shaktism tradition. She is often depicted as fierce and fearsome, representing the raw power of nature and the cycle of life and death.

• **Talvin Singh **is an English musician, producer, and composer known for his expertise in playing the tabla.
 
• He gained recognition for pioneering a unique fusion of Indian classical music with drum and bass, contributing to the emergence of the electronica subgenre known as Asian Underground.
 
• Singh's collaborations with artists like Siouxsie and the Banshees and Björk in the early 1990s propelled him into the spotlight.
 
• His debut album, "Ok," released in 1999, earned him the prestigious Mercury Music Prize.
 
• In 2010, Singh received an award at the UK Asian Music Awards for his "Commitment to Scene." In recognition of his contributions to music, he was honored with an OBE in the 2014 Birthday Honours.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **A tabla** is a pair of hand drums originating from the Indian subcontinent. Since the 18th century, it has held a central role as the principal percussion instrument in Hindustani classical music.
 
• It is versatile, being played solo, accompanying other instruments and vocals, and as part of larger ensembles.
 
• The tabla is prevalent in popular and folk music performances across India, Bangladesh, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Nepal, and Sri Lanka.
 
• It holds significance in the devotional practices of Hinduism and Sikhism, often used during bhajan and kirtan singing.
 
• Sufi musicians commonly use the tabla in qawwali performances, and it is a prominent feature in dance forms like Kathak. As a rhythmic instrument, the tabla plays a crucial role in various musical traditions.

__
 
• **Losar **is a vibrant new year festival observed in **Arunachal Pradesh and Ladakh**, deeply rooted in Buddhist traditions.
 
• Occurring on the first day of the Tibetan lunar calendar, Losar heralds the arrival of spring and symbolizes the onset of new beginnings.
 
• Central to the festivities are rituals aimed at dispelling malevolent forces and invoking auspicious energies. Across regions like Tawang in Arunachal Pradesh, Losar unfolds over a 15-day period marked by fervent celebrations.
 
• Communities come together to adorn their homes, engage in religious observances, and prepare elaborate offerings for divine entities. In the spirit of hospitality, people welcome both kinfolk and strangers alike.
 
• Amidst the jubilant atmosphere, traditional delicacies like "kapse," a special type of cake, and "chang," a fermented alcoholic beverage, are savored with gusto, adding to the festive cheer. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Arunachal Pradesh**, often referred to as the 'Dawn-Lit Mountain Province,' is a state nestled in the northeastern region of India. 
 
• Established on February 20, 1987, it emerged from the North-East Frontier Agency (NEFA) territory. The capital and largest town of Arunachal Pradesh is Itanagar. 
 
• This state shares its borders with the Indian states of Assam and Nagaland to the south, while its international boundaries extend to Bhutan in the west and Myanmar in the east. 
 
• Notably, Arunachal Pradesh also shares a disputed border of 1,129 km with China's Tibet Autonomous Region to the north, demarcated by the McMahon Line. 
 
• Although China claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of the Tibet Autonomous Region, its occupation of certain regions in 1962 was subsequently reversed.

question: The Beating Retreat ceremony is held at which of the following places?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vijay Chowk**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Beating Retreat ceremony** takes place at **Vijay Chowk in Delhi**, India, serving as the culmination of **Republic Day celebrations.**
 
• This annual event occurs on **January 29** and is orchestrated by the Indian Army.
 
• Commencing with the "Shankhnaad" tune by the massed band, the ceremony features a repertoire of melodies such as "Veer Bharat," "Sangam Dur," "Deshon ka Sartaj Bharat," "Bhagirathi," and "Arjuna" performed by the Pipes and Drums band.
 
• The tradition of the Beating Retreat ceremony harkens back to the historical practice of soldiers withdrawing from battle at dusk.
 
• It serves as a symbol of national pride and military prowess, showcasing the rich musical heritage of India's armed forces.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **The term "Beating Retreat"** has its origins in the **17th century,** when it was utilized to signify the conclusion of a day's military activities or patrolling. Bugles were sounded at sunset to signal the troops to return to their camps.
 
• This tradition was initially embraced by** the British Army and later adopted by the Indian Army **following independence.
 
• The inaugural Beating Retreat ceremony in India took place in 1955 during the state visit of** Queen Elizabeth II and Prince Philip.**
 
• Major GA Roberts conceptualized the event, which was commissioned by then-Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• Since its inception, the ceremony has evolved into an annual affair that serves as a platform to showcase India's rich musical and cultural heritage.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eid ul Fitr** is celebrated after the month of Ramzan (Ramadan).
 
• It is one of the most significant festivals in the Islamic calendar, marking the end of a month-long dawn-to-sunset fasting during Ramadan.
 
• The festival is also known as the "Festival of Breaking the Fast" and it is a joyous occasion for Muslims worldwide.
 
• On Eid ul Fitr, Muslims express gratitude to Allah for the strength and patience shown during Ramadan.
 
• The day begins with a special prayer called the "Salat al-Eid," which is performed in congregation.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Ramzan (Ramadan)** is the ninth month of the Islamic lunar calendar, observed by Muslims worldwide as a month of fasting, prayer, reflection, and community.
 
• Fasting during Ramadan is one of the Five Pillars of Islam, which are the foundational acts of worship and the core beliefs of the Muslim faith.
 
• Muslims fast from dawn (Fajr) until sunset (Maghrib), abstaining from food, drink, and other physical needs to purify the soul and practice self-discipline.
 
• Eid ul Fitr is a time for Muslims to give Zakat al-Fitr (charity in the form of food) to the needy, ensuring that all Muslims can enjoy the festivities.
 
• The celebration of Eid ul Fitr varies around the world, but common practices include communal prayers, feasting, visiting friends and family, and exchanging gifts.

question: In 2010, considering its outstanding value and vulnerability, UNESCO recognised 'Mudiyettu', an age-old ritual-drama of ______, as an ‘intangible cultural heritage of humanity’.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Kerala**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2010, considering its outstanding value and vulnerability, **UNESCO** recognised** 'Mudiyettu', **an age-old ritual-drama of Kerala, as an** ‘intangible cultural heritage of humanity’.**
 
• Mudiyettu is a traditional ritual performance deeply rooted in the Goddess Kali cult, primarily practiced by the Marar and Kuruppu communities. The name "Mudiyettu" is derived from the Malayalam words "Mudi" meaning hair and "Ettu" meaning wear.
 
• This performance involves seven key characters: Goddess Bhadrakali, Darika, Lord Shiva, Sage Narada, Dhanavendran, Koyimbadan, and Kooli. Each character adorns vibrantly decorated headgears, costumes, and makeup, enhancing the visual spectacle.
 
• The performance unfolds to the rhythmic beats of traditional percussion instruments. Mudiyettu is traditionally performed in the districts of Ernakulam, Thrissur, Kottayam, and Idukki, which were once part of the old Princely States of Travancore and Cochin in Kerala.
 
• This cultural tradition serves as a vibrant expression of local beliefs and folklore, captivating audiences with its colorful pageantry and spiritual significance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Kerala,** situated on the Malabar Coast of India, was established on November 1, 1956, through the enactment of the States Reorganisation Act.
 
• This formation amalgamated Malayalam-speaking regions from the former entities of Cochin, Malabar, South Canara, and Travancore. Encompassing an area of 38,863 square kilometers (15,005 square miles), Kerala ranks as the 21st largest state in India by land area.
 
• It shares borders with Karnataka to the north and northeast, Tamil Nadu to the east and south, and the Lakshadweep Sea to the west.
 
• As of the 2011 census, Kerala boasts a population of 33 million, making it the 13th most populous state in India. Administratively, Kerala is divided into 14 districts, with Thiruvananthapuram serving as its capital.
 
• Malayalam stands as the predominant language, serving as both the most commonly spoken tongue and the official language of the state.

 Har Gobind Khorana

 Subramanyan Chandrasekhar
 
 
 
• In 1983, he bagged the Nobel Prize in Physics for theoretical studies of the physical processes of importance to the structure and evolution of the stars.
 
• He shared the award with another physicist William Alfred Fowler.
 
• His theory suggested that the star further collapses into a compact star known as a white dwarf.
 
 
 
 

 Venkatraman Ramakrishnan

• He shared the award with Thomas A Steitz and Ada E Yonath.

• **Pandit Birju Maharaj **was the youngest recipient of the **Padma Vibhushan Award** in **dance in 1986**.

• Bob Dylan, an iconic American musician, received the Nobel Prize in Literature in 2016 for **“having created new poetic expressions within the great American song tradition.”**
 
• This marked the first time a musician was awarded the Nobel Prize in Literature, sparking a global debate about the definition of literature.
 
• Born as Robert Allen Zimmerman, Dylan’s influence on music and culture is profound, with his works blending poetry, music, and political commentary.
 
• Some of his most famous songs include **“Blowin’ in the Wind”** and **“The Times They Are A-Changin’,”** which became anthems for the civil rights and anti-war movements.

• The Nobel Prize in Literature is awarded annually to individuals who have produced outstanding work in the field of literature.

__
 
• **Jon Fosse**, a renowned Norwegian author, was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Literature in 2023**. The Nobel committee recognized his contributions to literature, particularly his innovative plays and prose.
 
• Fosse’s work is known for its **minimalist style**, which focuses on the essence of human emotions and relationships. His writing has a distinctive rhythm that captures the nuances of everyday life.
 
• He has written **plays, novels, poetry, essays, and children's books**, making him one of Norway's most versatile and celebrated writers. His works have been translated into over **40 languages**.
 
• The Nobel Prize acknowledged his ability to **explore the universal themes of existence**, such as love, loss, faith, and identity, often employing a sparse and poetic language.
 
• Jon Fosse is often compared to Samuel Beckett and Henrik Ibsen for his profound influence on contemporary theater and literature.
 
• The 2025 Nobel Prize in Literature has been awarded to the famous Hungarian author **László Krasznahorkai**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **Jon Fosse’s Contributions:**

 
 
• Fosse’s literary career spans over four decades, and he is considered a master of **existential drama**. His works often delve into human vulnerability and the complexities of relationships.
 
• His celebrated play, **"Someone Is Going to Come,"** and his novel, **"Trilogy,"** showcase his ability to blend simplicity with profound emotional depth.
 
• He has been awarded numerous prestigious honors, including the **International Ibsen Award** in 2010 and the **Nordic Council Literature Prize** in 2015.
 
 
 
• **About the Nobel Prize in Literature:**
 
 
• The Nobel Prize in Literature is awarded annually by the **Swedish Academy** to an author who has produced "the most outstanding work in an idealistic direction."
 
• It was established in **1901** as part of Alfred Nobel's will, with the intent to recognize exceptional contributions to the field of literature.
 
• Winners receive a **gold medal, a diploma, and a monetary award**.

• **Per Petterson:** Best known for his novel **"Out Stealing Horses,"** Petterson is a highly regarded Norwegian writer but has not received the Nobel Prize.
 
• **Erlend Loe:** A Norwegian author noted for his humorous and satirical works, such as **"Naïve. Super,"** but he has not been awarded the Nobel Prize.

• **Minimalist Literature:** Jon Fosse’s works are considered minimalist, emphasizing clarity, simplicity, and emotional resonance. This style often strips away excess to focus on core human experiences.
 
• **Global Impact:** Fosse’s plays are staged worldwide, and his novels are widely read, making him a significant figure in contemporary global literature.
 
• **Norwegian Literary Tradition:** Norway has a rich literary heritage, including figures like Henrik Ibsen and Knut Hamsun, who have also achieved international acclaim.

question: Which Nobel Laureate in Literature refused the prize in 1964, only for it to still be recorded in his name?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jean-Paul Sartre**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Jean-Paul Sartre**, a prominent figure in **20th-century French philosophy**, was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Literature** in **1964**.
 
• He was a leading proponent of **existentialism** and **Marxism**, exerting a significant influence on sociology, critical theory, and literary studies.
 
• Sartre became the first person to voluntarily decline the Nobel Prize, stating that a writer should not allow themselves to be transformed into an **institution**, even if it takes place in the most honorable form.
 
• He had previously declined other honors, including the **Legion of Honour** in **1945**, to maintain his **intellectual independence** and objective stance.
 
• Despite his public refusal and a letter sent to the **Swedish Academy** to withdraw his name, the committee announced him as the winner, and his name remains permanently recorded in the official list of **Nobel Laureates** for **1964**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gabriel Garcia Marquez**:

 
 
• A Colombian novelist and journalist who received the prize in **1982**.
 
• He is best known for his masterpiece **One Hundred Years of Solitude** and for popularizing the literary style known as **magical realism**.
 
 
 
• **Bob Dylan**:
 
 
• An American singer-songwriter who was awarded the Nobel Prize in **2016**.
 
• He was recognized for creating new poetic expressions within the great **American song tradition**, becoming the first musician to receive the honor.
 
 
 
• **Samuel Beckett**:
 
 
• An Irish avant-garde novelist and playwright who won the award in **1969**.
 
• A key figure in the **Theatre of the Absurd**, his most famous work is the play **Waiting for Godot**.

• She primarily focused on the struggles and aspirations of women within the **traditional Bengali middle-class** social structure during the **20th century**.
 
• In addition to the Jnanpith, she was awarded the **Padma Shri** by the Government of India in **1976** and the **Sahitya Akademi Fellowship** in **1994**.

• She was a leading **Punjabi** writer and poet who received the **Jnanpith Award** in **1981** for her collection **Kagaz Te Kanwas**.
 
• She was the first woman to win the **Sahitya Akademi Award** in **1956** for her poem **Sunehade**.
 
 
 
• **Mahasveta Devi**:
 
 
• A renowned **Bengali** author and social activist who was honored with the **Jnanpith Award** in **1996**.
 
• Her famous works include **Hajar Churashir Maa** and **Aranyer Adhikar**, often focusing on the rights of **tribal communities**.
 
 
 
• **Qurratulain Hyder**:
 
 
• An influential figure in **Urdu literature**, she won the **Jnanpith Award** in **1989**.
 
• Her most notable work is the historical novel **Aag Ka Darya** (River of Fire).

__
 
• **Jeremy Lalrinnunga** became the first Indian athlete to win a **gold medal at the Youth Olympics** by achieving this feat during the **2018 Summer Youth Olympics** held in **Buenos Aires, Argentina**.

• This victory marked a historic moment for **India**, as it was the first-ever gold medal won by an Indian in the history of the Youth Olympics.
 
• Jeremy Lalrinnunga hails from **Mizoram**, India, and is known for his exceptional talent in weightlifting, having trained at the **Army Sports Institute in Pune**.

• His Youth Olympics gold medal win was a precursor to his future successes in the senior weightlifting circuit.
 
 
 
• **Youth Olympics:**

• The event aims to develop young athletes and promote the Olympic values of **excellence, friendship, and respect**.
 
• The **2018 Summer Youth Olympics** was the third edition of the event and was hosted in **Buenos Aires, Argentina**, from **6 to 18 October 2018**.
 
• India participated in various sports and achieved a significant medal tally, including the historic gold by Jeremy Lalrinnunga.
 
 
 
• **Weightlifting:**
 
 
• Weightlifting is a sport that tests an athlete's strength through two main lifts: the **snatch** and the **clean and jerk**.
 
• Competitions are held across various weight categories, with athletes aiming to lift the maximum weight in each category.
 
• India has a rich history in weightlifting, with athletes like **Karnam Malleswari** and **Mirabai Chanu** bringing international laurels in the sport.
 
• Weightlifting requires rigorous training, discipline, and proper technique to excel at the global level.
 
 
 
• **Other Indian Youth Olympics Achievements:**
 
 
• In addition to Jeremy Lalrinnunga's gold, Indian athletes won several medals in the 2018 Youth Olympics, including **Manu Bhaker** (shooting) and **Suraj Panwar** (athletics).
 
• The performance of Indian athletes at the Youth Olympics reflects the growing support and investment in youth sports in India.
 
• Such achievements highlight the importance of initiatives like **Khelo India** in nurturing young talent and preparing them for international competitions.

• The **2008 Commonwealth Youth Games** were primarily hosted in **Pune, Maharashtra**, India. It was the third edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games.
 
• The event took place from **12th to 18th October 2008**, and it showcased the participation of young athletes from various Commonwealth nations.
 
• The Games saw the participation of around **1,300 athletes** and officials from 71 Commonwealth countries competing in various disciplines.
 
• **Shree Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex**, located in Balewadi, Pune, was the main venue for the Games. The facility was renovated and modernized to international standards for this purpose.
 
• The event featured **9 sports disciplines**, including athletics, swimming, badminton, boxing, table tennis, shooting, tennis, wrestling, and weightlifting, providing a platform for young athletes to showcase their talent.
 
• The Games were significant for promoting **youth sports** and fostering international camaraderie among the Commonwealth nations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Background and Significance of the Commonwealth Youth Games:**

 
 
• The **Commonwealth Youth Games** aim to provide young athletes (aged 14–18) a platform to compete at an international level and prepare for larger multi-sport events like the Commonwealth Games or the Olympics.
 
• The first edition of the Commonwealth Youth Games was held in **Edinburgh, Scotland, in 2000**, followed by the second edition in **Bendigo, Australia, in 2004**.
 
• The Games also play a crucial role in promoting the values of the Commonwealth, including **friendship, equality, and inclusivity**.
 
 
 
• **Shree Shiv Chhatrapati Sports Complex:**
 
 
• This sports complex, situated in **Balewadi, Pune**, served as the main venue for the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games.
 
• The complex underwent a major renovation to meet international standards, including facilities for multiple sports, advanced infrastructure, and seating arrangements for spectators.
 
• It continues to host various national and international sporting events, making it a significant sports hub in India.
 
 
 
• **Participants and Sports:**
 
 
• The 2008 edition saw participation from **71 Commonwealth countries**, with over **1,300 young athletes** competing.
 
• The Games featured **9 disciplines**: athletics, badminton, boxing, swimming, shooting, table tennis, tennis, wrestling, and weightlifting.
 
• The event was a stepping stone for many athletes who later went on to achieve success in senior-level competitions.
 
 
 
• **India’s Role:**
 
 
• Hosting the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games was a matter of pride for India, showcasing its ability to organize international multi-sport events.
 
• The successful hosting of the event also served as a precursor to India hosting the **2010 Commonwealth Games** in New Delhi.
 
• India performed exceptionally well in the Games, clinching **33 gold medals** and securing the **top position** in the medal tally.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of the 2008 Commonwealth Youth Games:**

 
 
• The Games left a lasting legacy in terms of **sports infrastructure** in Pune, with facilities that continue to benefit athletes and sports enthusiasts.
 
• The event boosted **India’s reputation** as a capable host for international sporting events.
 
• It also inspired increased participation and interest in sports among Indian youth, contributing to the country’s overall sports development.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Other Editions:**
 
 
• The 2008 Games were notable for their **efficient organization** and the enthusiastic participation of athletes and spectators alike.
 
• While the earlier editions (2000 in Edinburgh and 2004 in Bendigo) set the foundation, the Pune Games raised the bar in terms of **scale and impact**.

question: The Ashok Chakra Class-III was renamed as the ______ in 1967.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shaurya Chakra**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Ashok Chakra Class-III was renamed as the Shaurya Chakra in 1967.**

 
 
• The medal was originally established on** 4 January 1952 as the "Ashoka Chakra, Class I"**.
 
• As the first step of a three-class sequence of** non-combatant bravery decorations.**
 
• In 1967, these decorations were removed from the "class-based" system and renamed** as the Ashoka Chakra, and Shaurya Chakra. **
 
• The Ashoka Chakra is India's** highest peacetime military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the battlefield.**
 
• Flt.** Lt. Suhas Biswas** was the** first Indian Air Force officer **to be awarded the Ashoka Chakra.
 
• A recipient can be awarded the Kirti Chakra or Shaurya Chakra in addition for separate acts of gallantry.
 
 
 
• **Hence, option 1 is correct.** 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Kirti Chakra :**

 
 
• Kirti Chakra was known as** Ashok Chakra**,** Class II before 1967.**
 
• The Kirti Chakra is an **Indian military decoration awarded for valour, courageous action or self-sacrifice away from the field of battle**.
 
• It may be awarded to **civilians** as well as **military personnel, including posthumous awards**.
 
• It is the peacetime equivalent of the Maha Vir Chakra.
 
 
 
• **Mahavir Chakra :**
 
 
• The Maha Vir Chakra is **the second-highest military decoration in India, after the Param Vir Chakra.**
 
• It is awarded for acts of **conspicuous gallantry in the presence of the enemy, whether on land, at sea or in the air**.
 
• It replaced the British Distinguished Service Order.
 
• The medal may be awarded posthumously.
 
 
 
• **Vir Chakra :**
 
 
• Vir Chakra is an **Indian gallantry award presented for acts of gallantry in the presence of the enemy on the battlefield.**
 
• It replaced the** British Distinguished Service Cross**, Military Cross and Distinguished Flying Cross.
 
• Award of the decoration carries with it the right to use Vr.C. as a postnominal abbreviation.

question: Padma Bhushan awardee Kumudini Lakhia is renowned for which of the following dance forms?
solution:
The Correct Answer is __**Kathak**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **Year 2024** list includes **5 Padma Vibhushan**, **17 Padma Bhushan** and **110 Padma Shri awards,**Among the 2024 award winners, **30 are also women**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kathak****​**

 
 
• It is a classical Indian dance form originating from the northern parts of India.
 
• It is known for its quick footwork, intricate spins, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• Kathak is traditionally performed by both men and women, and it often tells stories from Hindu mythology or depicts scenes from everyday life
 
• Roshan Kumari, Shovana Narayan, Maya Rao and** Kumudini Lakhia** are eminent kathak artists.
 
 
 
• ​Kumudini Lakhia
 
 
• ​Kumudini Lakhia, born on May 17, 1930, is an famous Indian Kathak dancer and choreographer based in Ahmedabad, Gujarat.
 
• She played a crucial role in reshaping the traditional solo form of Kathak, especially during the 1960s.
 
• Her famous choreographies include "Dhabkar", "Yugal", and "Atah Kim".
 
• She also contributed as a choreographer in the Hindi film "Umrao Jaan" (1981). ​
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Odissi:-

 
 
• It is a classical Indian dance form originating from the state of Odisha in eastern India.
 
• It is known for its graceful and lyrical movements, intricate footwork, and expressive facial expressions.
 
• Odissi is traditionally performed by women, and it often tells stories from Hindu mythology or depicts scenes from everyday life.
 
• **Sujata Mohapatra, Madhavi Mudgal, Kelucharan Mohapatra, Surendra Nath Jena, Shobana Sahajananan** are eminent kathak artists.
 
 
 
• Kuchipudi:-
 
 
• It is a classical Indian dance form originating from the state of Andhra Pradesh in southern India. It is known for its energetic and vigorous movements, rhythmic footwork, and expressive hand gestures.
 
• Kuchipudi is traditionally performed by men, and it often tells stories from Hindu epics, such as the Ramayana and the Mahabharata.
 
• **Mallika Sarabhai, V. Satyanarayana Sarma, Deepa Shashindran** are eminent kathak artists.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam**
 
 
• Bharatanatyam originated in Tamil Nadu.
 
• Bharatanatyam is the oldest Indian classical dance and it originated hundreds of years ago in the Indian state of Tamil Nadu.
 
• This dance form expresses the religious themes and spiritual ideas of South India.
 
• The ancient Tamil epic Silappatikaram contains the description of Bharatanatyam.
 
• **​****Rukmini Devi, Padma Subrahmanyam, Vyjayanthimala, Sheema Kermani, Padmini** are eminent kathak artists.
 
• The Sangeet Natak Akademi currently confers classical status on eight Indian classical dance styles:** Bharatanatyam** (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North, West and Central India), Kathakali (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odissa), Manipuri (Manipur), Mohiniyattam (Kerala), and Sattriya (Assam).

• **Rabindranath Tagore** was also known as **Gurudev, was a Bengali polymath- poet, writer, composer, philosopher, and painter.**
 
 
• **He was the first non-European and the first Indian to receive the Nobel Prize for Literature (1913)**.
 
• He was the author of **‘Geetanjali’**.
 
• Tagore was awarded the **knighthood by King George V in 1915, but he repudiated it in 1919 as a protest against the Amritsar (Jallianwala Bagh) Massacre. He is sometimes referred to as “the Bard of Bengal”**.
 
• He was the founder of **Visvabharati University**.
 
• **He is the only person who wrote the National anthem for two countries- ‘Jana Gana Mana’ originally written in Bengali for India in 1911 and first sung at the Calcutta Session of Congress and ‘Amar Sonar Bangla’ for Bangladesh in the year 1905**.

question: ‘An Enquiry into the Nature and Cause of the Wealth of Nations’ is an influential work by economist ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Adam Smith**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **‘An Enquiry into the Nature and Cause of the Wealth of Nations’ is an influential work by economist Adam Smith.**

 
 
• classical capitalism was expressed in An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776).
 
• By the Scottish economist and philosopher Adam Smith, which recommended** leaving economic decisions to the free play of self-regulating market forces.**
 
• Adam Smith's purpose in writing The Wealth of Nations was to critique and offer an alternative to** the mercantilist economic system, which he believed would eventually stifle countries' productivity.**
 
• Adam Smith was **a Scottish economist, philosopher as well as a moral philosopher, a pioneer of political economy**.
 
 
• **Books :**
 
 
• **The Theory of Moral Sentiments (1759), An Inquiry into the Nature and Causes of the Wealth of Nations (1776).**
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
• **Hence, option 1 is correct. **

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] Additional Information__**

 
• **Millicent Fawcett :**

 
 
• Millicent Garrett Fawcett was** an English politician, writer, and feminist**.
 
• She campaigned fo**r women's suffrage through legislative change** and led Britain's largest women's rights association,** the National Union of Women's Suffrage Societies, from 1897 to 1919.**
 
• **Books :**
 
 
• **Women's suffrage, What I Remember, Janet Doncaster.**
 
 
 
 
 
• **Alfred Marshall:**
 
 
• Alfred Marshall was **an English economist, who was one of the most influential economists of his time**.
 
• His book, Principles of Economics, was the** dominant economic textbook in England for many years**.
 
• It brings the ideas of **supply and demand, marginal utility, and costs of production into a coherent whole.**
 
• **Books :**
 
 
• **Money, Credit & commerce, Element of Economics, Industry, and Trade.**
 
 
 
 
 
• **John Maynard Keynes** :
 
 
• John Maynard Keynes was **an English economist,** whose ideas fundamentally changed the theory and** practice of macroeconomics and the economic policies of governments.**
 
• **Book :**
 
 
• **The General Theory of Employment, Interest, and Money, The Collected writings, The Essential Keynes.**

• Structured akin to the Mahabharata, the novel is divided into sections and chapters that mirror the organization of the epic.
 
• Each segment skillfully alludes to themes and events from its counterpart in the Mahabharata, lending depth and complexity to the narrative.

question: Who wrote the novel 'A Suitable Boy'?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Vikram Seth**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Vikram Seth** is the author of the novel **'A Suitable Boy'**, published in 1993.
 
• The book is one of the longest novels ever published in a single volume, with over 1,300 pages.
 
• 'A Suitable Boy' is set in post-independence India (1950s) and revolves around the lives of four families, focusing on the search for a suitable match for Lata Mehra, the protagonist.
 
• The novel explores themes such as family dynamics, love, politics, and religious tensions in India.
 
• Vikram Seth is a celebrated Indian author and poet, known for works like 'The Golden Gate' (1986) and 'An Equal Music' (1999).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Salman Rushdie**

 
 
• Salman Rushdie is a renowned Indian-British author known for his contributions to magical realism.
 
• His most famous work is **'Midnight's Children'**, which won the Booker Prize in 1981 and depicts post-independence India through the lens of magical realism.
 
• Other notable works by Rushdie include 'The Satanic Verses,' 'The Moor's Last Sigh,' and 'Shalimar the Clown.'
 
 
 
• **Chetan Bhagat**
 
 
• Chetan Bhagat is a contemporary Indian author known for his best-selling novels, typically based on modern Indian youth and their struggles.
 
• Some of his famous works include **'Five Point Someone,' '2 States,' and 'The 3 Mistakes of My Life.'**
 
• His books have been adapted into popular Bollywood movies such as '3 Idiots,' 'Kai Po Che!,' and '2 States.'
 
 
 
• **Manu Joseph**
 
 
• Manu Joseph is an Indian journalist and author known for his satirical and insightful writings.
 
• His famous novels include **'Serious Men'** (winner of The Hindu Literary Prize) and 'The Illicit Happiness of Other People.'
 
• 'Serious Men' was adapted into a Netflix film in 2020, further cementing his reputation as a prominent contemporary writer.

question: Which Nigerian author won the Women's Prize for Fiction in 2007 for "Half of a Yellow Sun"?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie** is a renowned Nigerian author known for her impactful works exploring themes of identity, feminism, and post-colonialism.
 
• She won the **Women's Prize for Fiction in 2007** for her novel "**Half of a Yellow Sun**," which is set during the Nigerian Civil War (also known as the Biafran War).
 
• "Half of a Yellow Sun" is recognized for its vivid portrayal of the war's impact on individuals and families, offering a deeply human perspective on a historical event.
 
• The Women's Prize for Fiction is a prestigious literary award recognizing outstanding fiction written by women, and Adichie's win brought significant international attention to African literature.
 
• In addition to this accolade, Chimamanda Ngozi Adichie has been celebrated for other works, including "Purple Hibiscus," "Americanah," and her famous TED Talk-turned-book, "We Should All Be Feminists."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Buchi Emecheta**:
 
 
• Buchi Emecheta was a Nigerian author known for her works focusing on African women's experiences and themes of gender, migration, and identity.
 
• Her notable works include "The Joys of Motherhood," "Second-Class Citizen," and "The Bride Price."
 
• Emecheta's writing often highlights the struggles of African women in traditional and modern settings.
 
 
 
• **Lola Shoneyin**:
 
 
• Lola Shoneyin is a Nigerian poet and novelist best known for her novel "**The Secret Lives of Baba Segi’s Wives**."
 
• Her work explores polygamy, family dynamics, and societal expectations in Nigeria.
 
• Shoneyin is also the founder of the Aké Arts and Book Festival, a prominent literary event in Africa.
 
 
 
• **Sefi Atta**:
 
 
• Sefi Atta is a Nigerian author and playwright celebrated for her novel "**Everything Good Will Come**."
 
• Her works delve into themes of women's empowerment, societal challenges, and the cultural complexities of Nigeria.
 
• Atta's writing is widely acclaimed for its witty and insightful portrayal of Nigerian society.
 
 
 
• **Main Theme: The Nigerian Civil War and Literature**:
 
 
• "Half of a Yellow Sun" is set during the Nigerian Civil War (1967–1970), a conflict that arose from the attempted secession of the southeastern region of Nigeria as the Republic of Biafra.
 
• The novel provides a historical narrative interwoven with personal stories, exploring the war's devastating effects on people’s lives and relationships.
 
• This theme has been a significant focus in Nigerian literature, bringing global attention to the country's history and culture.

question: Which Chinese-American author's novel "The Joy Luck Club" became internationally acclaimed and adapted into a film in 1993?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amy Tan**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Amy Tan, a renowned **Chinese-American author**, wrote the acclaimed novel **"The Joy Luck Club"**, published in **1989**. The book garnered critical and commercial success worldwide.
 
• "The Joy Luck Club" explores the lives and relationships of **Chinese immigrant mothers** and their **Chinese-American daughters**, portraying themes of cultural identity, generational conflict, and familial bonds.
 
• The novel was adapted into a film in **1993**, directed by **Wayne Wang**. The movie received widespread praise and was one of the first mainstream Hollywood films to feature a predominantly Asian cast.
 
• Amy Tan's writing often reflects her personal experiences as the daughter of Chinese immigrants, addressing the challenges of balancing traditional values with contemporary American culture.
 
• The novel's success established Amy Tan as one of the leading voices in **Asian-American literature**, contributing significantly to the representation of Asian-American stories in mainstream media.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About "The Joy Luck Club":**

 
 
• The novel is structured as a series of interconnected stories, offering perspectives from eight characters—four mothers and their daughters. Each story delves into the characters' struggles with their cultural heritage and personal aspirations.
 
• The title refers to a **mahjong club** formed by the immigrant mothers to maintain their cultural ties and share their experiences in America.
 
• The themes of the book include **cultural identity**, **mother-daughter relationships**, and the complexities of assimilation into a new culture.
 
 
 
• **Amy Tan's Other Works:**
 
 
• After the success of "The Joy Luck Club," Amy Tan wrote other acclaimed novels such as **"The Kitchen God's Wife"** (1991), **"The Hundred Secret Senses"** (1995), and **"The Bonesetter's Daughter"** (2001).
 
• Her works often explore themes of **family, identity, and cultural heritage**, drawing heavily from her own experiences and background.
 
 
 
• **Adaptation of "The Joy Luck Club":**
 
 
• The 1993 film adaptation was groundbreaking for its **representation of Asian-American characters** in Hollywood, paving the way for future projects like **"Crazy Rich Asians"** (2018).
 
• The screenplay was co-written by **Amy Tan** and **Ronald Bass**, ensuring the film remained faithful to the novel's themes and narratives.
 
 
 
• **Other Authors from the Options:**
 
 
• **Celeste Ng:** Author of **"Little Fires Everywhere"** and **"Everything I Never Told You"**. Her works explore family dynamics and social issues but are unrelated to "The Joy Luck Club."
 
• **Maxine Hong Kingston:** Known for **"The Woman Warrior"** and **"China Men"**, Kingston's works focus on Chinese-American identity but are distinct from Amy Tan's storytelling style.
 
• **Lisa See:** Famous for novels like **"Snow Flower and the Secret Fan"** and **"The Tea Girl of Hummingbird Lane"**, Lisa See also explores Chinese culture and history in her works.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Amy Tan's Influence:** Her novels have been translated into **more than 30 languages**, and she has received numerous awards for her contributions to literature.
 
• **The Joy Luck Club's Legacy:** The novel has been included in **school curriculums** and is celebrated as a significant work in American literature, particularly in the context of immigrant narratives.
 
• **Representation in Media:** The 1993 film adaptation helped increase the visibility of **Asian-American culture** in mainstream media, marking a milestone for diversity in Hollywood.

question: Who is the first English language writer to become a Jnanpith laureate?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Amitav Ghosh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Amitav Ghosh** became the first English-language writer to be honored with the **Jnanpith Award**. This prestigious recognition was conferred upon him in **2018** for his outstanding contribution to literature.
 
• The **Jnanpith Award** is India's highest literary honor, established in **1961** by the Bharatiya Jnanpith organization.
 
• **Amitav Ghosh** is renowned for his novels that often blend historical elements with social and cultural narratives. His works include **"The Shadow Lines," "The Glass Palace," "Sea of Poppies,"** and **"The Hungry Tide."**
 
• Ghosh's writing style incorporates rich storytelling, detailed research, and themes like migration, colonialism, and environmental concerns.
 
• Before **Amitav Ghosh**, the Jnanpith Award was traditionally given to writers who wrote in Indian languages, making his recognition a landmark in the award's history.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About the Jnanpith Award:**

 
 
• The Jnanpith Award is presented annually to an author for their contribution to literature written in any of the recognized languages of India, per the **Eighth Schedule of the Indian Constitution.**
 
• The award consists of a **cash prize, a citation, and a bronze replica of Saraswati (the goddess of wisdom).**
 
• Authors such as **Girish Karnad, Ashapurna Devi, and G. Sankara Kurup** have previously received this honor for their exceptional literary contributions.
 
 
 
• **Amitav Ghosh's Literary Achievements:**
