question: Which of the following is NOT a part of India's first indigenous anti-nuclear medical kit?
solution:
**Saline Solution** is not a part of India's first indigenous anti-nuclear medical kit.

Institute of Nuclear Medicine and Allied Sciences (INMAS) has developed India’s first indigenous anti-nuclear medical kit.

The kit may ensure protection from serious injuries and faster healing of wounds resulting from nuclear warfare or radioactive leakage.

**Content of the kit:-**

 
• **Prussian blue tablets** - provides 100 per cent absorption from the gut and other portals of entry to the human body and are highly effective in incorporating Radio Cesium (Cs-137) and Radio Thallium.
 
• Ethylenediaminetetraacetic acid (EDTA) injection - traps uranium in the guts and blood of victims during a nuclear accident or warfare.
 
• Ca-EDTA Respiratory Fluid - inhalation formula for chelation, or grabbing, of heavy metals and radioactive elements deposited in lungs through inhalation at nuclear accident sites. When injected into the veins, it “grabs” heavy metals and minerals and removes them from the body.
 
• Anti-gamma ray skin ointment - protects and heals the radiation damage on the skin.
 
• Amifostine injection - conventional radiopharmaceutical that limits damage from gamma radiation.
 
• Radioactive urine/biofluid collector - can safely dispose of the urine of a person affected by radiation.

question: Researchers of Kerala-based Amrita University in collaboration with the Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority have developed a real-time _______. This system can help save lives and prevent loss to property by issuing advance alerts.
solution:
__
 
• Researchers of **Kerala-based Amrita University** in collaboration with the **Sikkim State Disaster Management Authority **have developed a real-time **Landslide warning system****.**
 
• The system gives advance warnings of landslides so that people can be safely evacuated before disaster strikes.
 
• After successfully deploying India’s first such system in Kerala’s Western Ghats, it will now be deployed in Sikkim to guard against rainfall-induced landslides in the Sikkim-Darjeeling belt. 
 
• The system collects real-time, continuous data from the sensors, performs basic analysis at the Field Management Center (FMC) located on the site in Sikkim and relays it to the Data Management Center (DMC) at Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham in Kerala’s Kollam district.
 
• The project is jointly funded by the **Ministry of Earth Sciences**, Government of India, and **Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham**.
 
• **Extra:-__**
 
• In 2008, Amrita set up **India's first landslide laboratory** which can create small landslides under controlled conditions and act as the feedback system for field deployment.
 
• **Amrita Vishwa Vidyapeetham **has been ranked 8th among the Indian universities by NIRF in 2019.

question: In June _________, the Reserve Bank of India published a ‘Consultative Document on Regulation of Microfinance’.
solution:
The correct answer is __**2021**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** issued a consultative document concerning microfinance regulation on **June 14, 2021, **which is accessible as a PDF.
 
• The document provides an overview of the **microfinance sector in India**, detailing its evolution over the past two decades.
 
• It comprises chapters **covering Introduction, Developments in the microfinance sector, and Customer protection **concerns in the microfinance sector.
 
• One of the primary objectives of the document is to streamline the regulatory frameworks governing various regulated lenders operating within the microfinance domain.
 
• By removing most rules, except for one, the document aims to create a level playing field.
 
• Notably, it grants **Microfinance Institutions (MFIs)** the authority to determine the interest rates they levy on borrowers, albeit with the stipulation that these rates remain non-usurious.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** serves as India's **central bank and regulatory authority** overseeing the Indian banking system.
 
• Operated under the ownership of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, the RBI plays a pivotal role in controlling, issuing, and managing the supply of the Indian rupee.
 
• Additionally, it supervises the nation's primary payment systems and actively works to foster economic development. In collaboration with the Indian Banks' Association, the RBI established the National Payments Corporation of India, tasked with promoting and regulating payment and settlement systems across the country.
 
• Furthermore, the RBI created the Deposit Insurance and Credit Guarantee Corporation as a specialized division, aimed at providing deposit insurance and credit guarantee facilities to all Indian banks.

question: Which of the following is NOT among the list of Indian biosphere reserves designated as a "UNESCO World Network Site" in 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Dibru-Saikhowa Biosphere Reserve** is located in Assam, India, and is renowned for its rich biodiversity and wetland ecosystems.
 
• It is not part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves as of 2024, unlike other biosphere reserves such as Nilgiri, Panna, and Great Nicobar.
 
• The reserve comprises grasslands, wetlands, and forests, and is a habitat for several endangered species, including the Bengal tiger, river dolphins, and migratory birds.
 
• Dibru-Saikhowa is primarily recognized for its regional importance in conserving flora and fauna but has not yet achieved UNESCO designation.
 
• The reserve is known for its unique ecosystem, including the presence of semi-evergreen forests, deciduous forests, and swamp forests.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve**

 
 
• Located at the intersection of Tamil Nadu, Kerala, and Karnataka, the Nilgiri Biosphere Reserve is one of India's first biosphere reserves and was designated as part of UNESCO's World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2000.
 
• It hosts a wide variety of flora and fauna, including several endangered species such as the lion-tailed macaque and Nilgiri tahr.
 
• The reserve is part of the Western Ghats, recognized as a UNESCO World Heritage Site for its ecological significance.
 
 
 
• **Panna Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• Panna Biosphere Reserve is located in Madhya Pradesh and was designated as a UNESCO World Network Site in 2020.
 
• It is famous for its tiger population and is part of the Panna Tiger Reserve, which successfully revived its tiger population after facing near extinction.
 
• The reserve also encompasses diverse ecosystems, including deciduous forests, grasslands, and riverine areas.
 
 
 
• **Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve**
 
 
• Situated in the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, the Great Nicobar Biosphere Reserve was designated as part of the UNESCO World Network of Biosphere Reserves in 2013.
 
• It is known for its tropical rainforest ecosystems and is home to unique species such as the Nicobar pigeon and saltwater crocodile.
 
• The reserve also includes indigenous communities like the Nicobarese and Shompen tribes, who coexist with the rich biodiversity.

question: e-NAM is primarily aimed at which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**National digital market**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **e-NAM** stands for **National Agriculture Market**, which is a pan-India electronic trading portal to connect existing Agricultural Produce Market Committees (APMCs) to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.
 
• The primary objective of e-NAM is to establish a **National digital market** for agricultural produce, enabling farmers to sell their produce across the nation and not be restricted to local markets.
 
• e-NAM integrates markets through a virtual platform, reducing intermediation costs, ensuring better price discovery, and improving market transparency.
 
• Launched by the Government of India on **14th April 2016**, it aims to provide remunerative prices to farmers by improving their bargaining power.
 
• As of **October 2023**, over **1000 APMC mandis** from various states and union territories have been integrated with the e-NAM platform.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Functions and Features of e-NAM:**

 
 
• It facilitates **online trading** of agricultural commodities and integrates APMC markets across the country.
 
• Provides a single window service for all APMC-related information and services, including commodity arrivals, quality assessment, and real-time price discovery.
 
• Farmers can directly connect with buyers, avoiding intermediaries, and ensuring better returns.
 
• It supports various languages and is accessible through mobile and desktop platforms, making it user-friendly for farmers.
 
 
 
• **Benefits of e-NAM:**
 
 
• Enhances **price discovery** through a transparent auction mechanism based on the quality of produce.
 
• Reduces transaction costs and eliminates the need for physical presence at the market by allowing e-bidding.
 
• Promotes **uniformity** in agricultural marketing by streamlining processes and removing information asymmetry between buyers and sellers.
 
• Encourages interstate trade of agricultural produce, leading to better market integration at the national level.
 
 
 
• **Other Agricultural Initiatives by the Indian Government:**
 
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY):** Launched in 2016, it provides a comprehensive risk cover for crops, ensuring financial support to farmers in case of crop failure.
 
• **Soil Health Card Scheme:** Introduced in 2015, this scheme aims to provide farmers with information on soil health and recommendations for nutrient management.
 
• **Kisan Credit Card (KCC):** It provides short-term credit to farmers for agricultural and allied activities at subsidized rates.
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Krishi Sinchayee Yojana (PMKSY):** Launched to improve irrigation efficiency and ensure water accessibility for every farm in India.
 
 
 
• **Important Reports:**
 
 
• According to the **Economic Survey 2020-21**, the implementation of e-NAM has significantly improved market access for farmers and reduced wastage of produce.
 
• The **World Bank Report** on agriculture highlights the role of digital platforms like e-NAM in reducing barriers to market access for small and marginal farmers.

question: On 6th July 2025, Prime Minister Narendra Modi paid tribute to which leader known for founding the Bharatiya Jana Sangh and sacrificing his life for India's unity and integrity?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee** was the founder of the **Bharatiya Jana Sangh**, which later evolved into the **Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP)**, one of India's largest political parties.
 
• He was a firm advocate of **India's unity and integrity** and opposed the special status granted to Jammu and Kashmir under Article 370.
 
• Dr. Mookerjee sacrificed his life while protesting against the special autonomy of Jammu and Kashmir, which he believed was harmful to India's unity. His motto was, "**Ek Vidhan, Ek Nishan, Ek Pradhan**" (One Constitution, One Flag, One Leader).
 
• He was a respected politician, educationist, and intellectual. He served as the **Minister for Industry and Supply** in the first cabinet of independent India under Prime Minister Jawaharlal Nehru.
 
• On 6th July 2025, **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** paid tribute to Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee for his contributions to the nation and his role in laying the foundation for modern Indian politics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee:**

 
 
• He was born on **6th July 1901** in **Kolkata, West Bengal**, and passed away on **23rd June 1953** under mysterious circumstances while in custody in Jammu and Kashmir.
 
• He was instrumental in establishing the **Bharatiya Jana Sangh** in **1951** to promote nationalism and counter the policies of the Congress party.
 
• Dr. Mookerjee was a key figure in the **Bengal Partition movement**, which ensured that a part of Bengal remained with India during the partition in 1947.
 
• He held the position of **Vice-Chancellor of Calcutta University** at the age of 33, making significant contributions to education and academic excellence.
 
 
 
• **Article 370:**
 
 
• Article 370 of the Indian Constitution granted special status to Jammu and Kashmir, allowing it to have its own constitution and autonomy over internal matters, except defense, communications, and foreign affairs.
 
• Dr. Mookerjee strongly opposed Article 370, emphasizing the importance of **national integration** and equal status for all states within the Indian Union.
 
• His protest against the special status led to his arrest and eventual death, which remains a subject of controversy and speculation.
 
• In **2019**, Article 370 was abrogated by the Government of India, fulfilling one of Dr. Mookerjee's key ideologies.
 
 
 
• **Other leaders mentioned in the options:**
 
 
• **Pandit Deendayal Upadhyaya:** He was an Indian politician and philosopher known for his concept of **Integral Humanism**, which became the guiding philosophy of the BJP.
 
• **Bal Gangadhar Tilak:** A prominent freedom fighter and social reformer, he was known as the **Father of Indian Unrest** and played a significant role in India's independence movement.
 
• **Lala Lajpat Rai:** He was a key leader in the Indian independence movement and earned the title **Punjab Kesari**. He actively protested against colonial rule, including the Simon Commission.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Legacy of Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee:**

 
 
• His contributions laid the foundation for the **nationalist political movement** in India, which continues to influence Indian politics today.
 
• He is remembered for his unwavering commitment to **national unity** and his efforts to integrate Jammu and Kashmir fully with India.
 
• His death sparked debates on the treatment of political dissenters and the importance of transparency in governance.
 
 
 
• **Tributes:**
 
 
• Institutions such as **Syama Prasad Mookerjee Port Trust** and several educational institutions have been named after him.
 
• Prime Minister Narendra Modi and the BJP often highlight his contributions as part of their political discourse and policies.
 
• Annual tributes are paid on his birth and death anniversaries to honor his legacy.

question: Which of the following is now explicitly considered a 'document' under the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam?
solution:
The correct answer is __**A server log file**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam, 2023**, which replaced the **Indian Evidence Act of 1872**, has significantly expanded the legal definition of a **document** to encompass the digital age.
 
• Under **Section 2(1)(d)** of the Act, a **document** is defined as any matter expressed, described, or inscribed upon any substance by means of letters, figures, or marks, intended for recording that matter.
 
• The Act explicitly includes **electronic and digital records** within this definition, specifically mentioning **server logs**, **emails**, **documents on computers**, **laptop or smartphone messages**, and **websites**.
 
• By including a **server log file**, the law recognizes automated digital footprints as valid evidence, allowing for better prosecution of **cyber-crimes** and technology-related disputes.
 
• This shift ensures that **electronic records** are treated with the same legal weight as traditional paper-based evidence, provided their **integrity** is maintained.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023**:

 
 
• The Act received the **President's assent** on **December 25, 2023**, and came into effect on **July 1, 2024**.
 
• It introduces provisions for the **admissibility of electronic evidence** as primary evidence under **Section 61**, provided the storage remains in its original digital form.
 
• **Section 63** of the BSA outlines the requirements for a **certificate** to authenticate electronic records, replacing the older **Section 65B** of the previous Act.
 
• Other digital formats recognized include **locational evidence**, **voice mail messages**, and data retrieved from **cloud storage** or **digital devices**.
 
 
 
• **Excluded Concepts**:
 
 
• **Verbal agreements** are considered oral evidence rather than documentary evidence unless reduced to writing or a digital record.
 
• **Spontaneous thoughts** are intangible and do not meet the criteria of being recorded on a substance or medium to qualify as a document.

question: On 8th March 2025, the nation observed the Jayanti of which social reformer and founder of the Matua Sect, known for leading the Chandal movement against untouchability?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shree Harichand Thakur**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shree Harichand Thakur** was a prominent **social reformer and spiritual leader** who founded the **Matua Sect**, a religious and social movement aimed at uplifting the downtrodden and marginalized communities.
 
• He is known for initiating and leading the **Chandal movement**, which was directed against the practice of **untouchability** and social discrimination faced by the oppressed communities, particularly the Chandals (a Dalit community).
 
• Shree Harichand Thakur emphasized the principles of **equality, social justice, and humanity**. His teachings were focused on eradicating caste-based discrimination and promoting dignity for all human beings.
 
• His followers, known as **Matuas**, played a significant role in spreading his message across Bengal and other parts of India. The Matua Sect continues to be a major spiritual and social movement, especially among the Dalit communities.
 
• The **8th of March 2025** marked the observance of his **Jayanti** (birth anniversary), showcasing his contribution to the fight against social inequality and untouchability.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Matua Sect:**

 
 
• The Matua Sect was founded by **Shree Harichand Thakur** in the **19th century** in Bengal.
 
• It is a socio-religious reform movement aimed at uplifting the **economically and socially weaker sections**, particularly the Dalits and marginalized communities.
 
• The movement emphasizes **spirituality, equality, and social reform**, rejecting caste-based discrimination.
 
 
 
• **Chandal Movement:**
 
 
• It was a significant social reform movement led by Shree Harichand Thakur against the practice of **untouchability**.
 
• The movement aimed to abolish the stigmatization of the Chandal community and ensure their **social dignity and rights**.
 
• The Chandal movement is considered a key milestone in the history of India's social reform movements.
 
 
 
• **Teachings of Shree Harichand Thakur:**
 
 
• He emphasized the principles of **truthfulness, simplicity, and equality**.
 
• His teachings encouraged people to reject caste-based discrimination and practice **universal brotherhood**.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Shree Harichand Thakur's efforts led to significant social changes in Bengal and laid the foundation for **Dalit empowerment**.
 
• His followers continue to celebrate his teachings and principles through various cultural and religious practices.
 
• In modern times, the Matua Sect has also gained political significance in regions with a significant Dalit population.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Shree Narayan Guru:** A social reformer from Kerala, known for his work in promoting equality and abolishing caste-based discrimination in the region. He was not associated with the Matua Sect.
 
• **Shree Jyotirao Phule:** A social reformer from Maharashtra, known for his efforts in women's education and the upliftment of oppressed communities. He was not connected to the Matua Sect.
 
• **Shree Guru Ravidas:** A Bhakti movement saint and poet from North India, known for his spiritual teachings advocating equality and social justice. He was not associated with the Chandal movement or the Matua Sect.

question: Which of the following offenses has been newly and clearly defined under the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Mob lynching**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), 2023**, which replaced the colonial-era **Indian Penal Code (IPC) of 1860**, has introduced **Mob lynching** as a specifically defined offense for the first time in Indian criminal law.
 
• Under **Section 103(2)** of the BNS, mob lynching is defined as an act of murder committed by a group of **five or more persons** acting in concert on grounds of **race, caste, community, sex, place of birth, language, personal belief**, or any other similar ground.
 
• The statute mandates severe punishments for those convicted of this offense, including **life imprisonment** or the **death penalty**, alongside a mandatory fine.
 
• While the **IPC** previously prosecuted such acts under general provisions like **Section 302 (Murder)** read with **Section 149 (Unlawful Assembly)**, it lacked a dedicated definition that recognized the specific socio-political nature of lynching.
 
• This legislative change follows various directives from the **Supreme Court of India**, notably in the **Tehseen S. Poonawalla v. Union of India (2018)** case, which urged the government to enact a special law against lynching.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Evolution of Legal Definitions in BNS**:

 
 
• **Organized Crime**: Newly defined under **Section 111**, it covers activities like **kidnapping, robbery, and land grabbing** carried out by criminal syndicates.
 
• **Terrorist Act**: Defined under **Section 113**, bringing specific elements of the **Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA)** into the general penal code.
 
• **Defamation**: Retained under **Section 356**, but notably introduces **community service** as a non-custodial punishment option.
 
• **Sedition**: The term has been removed and replaced by **Section 152**, which penalizes acts endangering the **sovereignty, unity, and integrity of India**.
 
• **Snatching**: Now a specific offense under **Section 304**, distinct from ordinary theft.

question: Who is the Secretary-General of the United Nations as on July 2020?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Antonio Guterres**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Antonio Guterres** is the **9th Secretary-General** of **the United Nations**.
 
• He took office on **1 January 2017**.

question: Who has been appointed as the Chief Justice of India with effect from May 14, 2025?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Shri Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Shri Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai** has been appointed as the **Chief Justice of India (CJI)** with effect from **May 14, 2025**. He is set to be the **53rd Chief Justice of India**.
 
• Justice Gavai was appointed as a judge of the **Supreme Court of India** on **May 24, 2019**. His tenure in the judiciary has been marked by significant contributions and judgments.
 
• He will succeed the current CJI as per the seniority norms traditionally followed in the appointment process of Chief Justices in India.
 
• Shri Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai hails from the state of **Maharashtra**, and he is known for his expertise in constitutional, civil, and criminal law matters.
 
• His appointment reflects the continuation of the seniority convention in the Indian judiciary, ensuring a smooth transition in the office of the Chief Justice of India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Role of the Chief Justice of India (CJI):**

 
 
• The **CJI** is the head of the **judiciary system of India** and the **Supreme Court**, which is the highest judicial forum and final court of appeal under the Constitution of India.
 
• The CJI plays a pivotal role in ensuring the independence and integrity of the judiciary.
 
• The CJI is also responsible for the allocation of cases and appointment of constitutional benches to deal with significant legal issues.
 
 
 
• **Appointment Process:**
 
 
• The appointment of the CJI is based on the convention of seniority, where the senior-most judge of the Supreme Court is appointed as the CJI.
 
• The **President of India** appoints the CJI under Article 124(2) of the **Indian Constitution**.
 
• The recommendation for appointment is made by the outgoing CJI.
 
 
 
• **Notable Judgments by Justice Bhushan Ramkrishna Gavai:**
 
 
• Justice Gavai has delivered judgments on various key issues, including constitutional law, human rights, and environmental law.
 
• He has contributed significantly to cases relating to **administrative law** and **judicial review** of executive actions.
 
 
 
• **Important Facts About the Supreme Court:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court of India was established on **January 28, 1950**, after the adoption of the Constitution of India.
 
• The Supreme Court comprises the **CJI** and a maximum of **34 judges** (as per the current sanctioned strength).
 
• It functions as the **guardian of the Constitution** and is vested with the power of **judicial review**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The tenure of a Chief Justice of India is not fixed but depends on the retirement age of **65 years**, as prescribed under the Constitution.
 
• Justice Gavai will hold office as the CJI for a short period, as his retirement is due on **November 24, 2025**.
 
• The Supreme Court plays a crucial role in maintaining the balance of power between the legislature, executive, and judiciary, as enshrined in the Constitution of India.

question: Who was appointed as the Defence Secretary of India in November 2024?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Giridhar Aramane**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Giridhar Aramane** was appointed as the **Defence Secretary of India** in **November 2022**. His tenure began after the retirement of his predecessor, **Ajay Kumar**.
 
• Prior to his appointment as Defence Secretary, **Giridhar Aramane** served as the **Secretary in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways**, where he oversaw significant infrastructure projects across the nation.
 
• He belongs to the **1988 batch of the Indian Administrative Service (IAS)** from the **Andhra Pradesh cadre** and has held several key administrative positions during his career.
 
• As Defence Secretary, he is responsible for overseeing **India's defence policies**, managing the **Ministry of Defence**, and coordinating with the **armed forces** to ensure the country’s security and strategic interests.
 
• He holds a **Master’s degree in Economics** and a **Bachelor’s degree in Civil Engineering**, which reflects his strong academic background and technical expertise.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Roles and Responsibilities of the Defence Secretary:**

 
 
• The Defence Secretary is the administrative head of the **Ministry of Defence (MoD)** in India.
 
• He/she plays a vital role in formulating and executing **defence policies** in consultation with the armed forces and government officials.
 
• The Defence Secretary oversees the functioning of various departments within the MoD, including the **Department of Defence**, **Defence Production**, and **Research and Development**.
 
• He/she is also responsible for ensuring proper coordination between the armed forces and civilian authorities on matters of national security.
 
 
 
• **Previous Defence Secretaries:**
 
 
• **Ajay Kumar** served as the Defence Secretary before Giridhar Aramane and contributed to several defence modernization programs.
 
• Other notable Defence Secretaries include **Vijay Singh** and **Shekhar Dutt**, who played critical roles in shaping India’s defence policies.
 
 
 
• **Ministry of Defence:**
 
 
• The Ministry of Defence is responsible for the **defence of India** and ensures the sovereignty, security, and integrity of the nation.
 
• It oversees organizations such as the **Indian Army**, **Indian Navy**, **Indian Air Force**, and **DRDO (Defence Research and Development Organisation)**.
 
• The ministry also manages defence production units and ensures indigenous manufacturing of defence equipment under the **Make in India initiative**.
 
 
 
• **Giridhar Aramane's Achievements:**
 
 
• During his tenure in the Ministry of Road Transport and Highways, he played a key role in implementing the **Bharatmala Pariyojana**, a flagship infrastructure project.
 
• He has also worked on initiatives that promote **self-reliance in defence manufacturing**, aligning with the government’s **Atmanirbhar Bharat** vision.
 
• His extensive experience in governance and policy-making makes him a highly capable administrator for the role of Defence Secretary.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Selection Process:**

 
 
• The **Defence Secretary** is appointed by the **Appointments Committee of the Cabinet (ACC)**, headed by the Prime Minister of India.
 
• The post is usually held by a **senior IAS officer** with significant experience in administration and policymaking.
 
• The tenure of the Defence Secretary is typically **two years**, but it may be extended based on performance and government requirements.
 
 
 
• **India’s Defence Policies:**
 
 
• India’s defence policies focus on **modernizing the armed forces**, enhancing indigenous defence production, and strengthening strategic partnerships with other countries.
 
• The government has launched initiatives like **Defence Acquisition Procedure (DAP) 2020** to streamline procurement and promote **Make in India** in the defence sector.
 
• India is also focusing on enhancing its **cybersecurity capabilities** to counter emerging threats in the digital domain.

question: What is a key factor considered in the World Happiness Report's ranking?
solution:
The correct answer is __**GDP per capita**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Happiness Report ranks countries based on various indicators that reflect the well-being of their citizens, one of the most important being **GDP per capita**.
 
• **GDP per capita** measures the average income of a country's citizens and serves as a strong indicator of economic prosperity and living standards.
 
• This metric is closely linked to the ability of individuals to access basic necessities, healthcare, education, and other resources contributing to happiness.
 
• The World Happiness Report utilizes GDP per capita as a key variable to gauge material well-being, which directly impacts overall life satisfaction.
 
• Countries with higher GDP per capita often rank higher due to better infrastructure, higher standards of living, and improved social services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Military Strength**

 
 
• While military strength is important for national security, it is **not a direct determinant of happiness**.
 
• Countries with strong military capabilities might not necessarily have high happiness levels as national defense does not inherently affect individual well-being or quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Internet Speed**
 
 
• Internet speed, though important for connectivity and communication, is not a core factor in the World Happiness Report.
 
• While faster internet can improve efficiency and access to resources, it does not directly measure a population's happiness or satisfaction with life.
 
 
 
• **Forest Cover**
 
 
• Forest cover contributes to environmental sustainability and has indirect effects on happiness through improved air quality and mental health benefits.
 
• However, it is not a primary metric used in the World Happiness Report rankings.
 
 
 
• **World Happiness Report**
 
 
• The World Happiness Report is published annually by the United Nations Sustainable Development Solutions Network.
 
• It ranks countries based on six main factors: **GDP per capita, social support, healthy life expectancy, freedom to make life choices, generosity, and perceptions of corruption**.
 
• The report emphasizes both economic and non-economic factors in determining happiness, providing a holistic measure of a country's well-being.

question: Which of these is a pillar assessed by the Index of Economic Freedom?

The correct answer is __**Government Spending**__.

__
 
• The **Index of Economic Freedom** is a tool developed by The Heritage Foundation and The Wall Street Journal to measure economic freedom in 12 key areas, including government spending.
 
• **Government Spending** is a critical pillar, assessing the level of government expenditure as a percentage of GDP and its impact on economic freedom.
 
• Excessive government spending can lead to fiscal deficits, inflation, and higher tax burdens, which restrict economic freedom, while controlled spending facilitates efficient resource allocation.
 
• This pillar evaluates how efficiently governments manage public resources and avoid the crowding-out effect, which occurs when government spending inhibits private sector growth.
 
• The Index covers 184 countries, and the government spending score impacts a country's overall ranking in economic freedom.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Social Welfare Programs:**
 
 
• Social welfare programs are government initiatives designed to provide support to disadvantaged groups, including health care, unemployment benefits, and housing assistance.
 
• While important for social equity, these programs are not directly assessed in the Index of Economic Freedom.
 
• Excessive welfare spending can sometimes impact the government spending score in the Index, as it increases fiscal burdens.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Regulations:**
 
 
• Environmental regulations are rules and standards aimed at protecting the environment from overexploitation and pollution.
 
• While these regulations are crucial for sustainable development, they are not a direct pillar in the Index of Economic Freedom.
 
• However, excessive regulations can affect the "Regulatory Efficiency" pillar of the Index, which measures the ease of doing business.
 
 
 
• **Artistic Freedom:**
 
 
• Artistic freedom refers to the freedom of individuals and groups to express themselves creatively without censorship or restriction.
 
• This concept is vital for cultural and societal development but is not included in the Index of Economic Freedom's assessment criteria.

question: The Global Liveability Index 2025, a form of Global Cities Index, is published by which organization?
solution:
The correct answer is __**EIU**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU)** publishes the **Global Liveability Index**, which evaluates cities worldwide based on their liveability conditions.
 
• The index ranks cities on factors such as **stability, healthcare, culture, environment, education, and infrastructure**.
 
• The **Global Liveability Index** is a prominent measure used by businesses, governments, and individuals to assess the quality of living in urban areas.
 
• It is updated annually, providing insights into which cities offer the best and worst living conditions globally.
 
• The data is sourced through surveys, expert opinions, and assessments, ensuring a comprehensive and reliable analysis of urban living standards.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **About the Economist Intelligence Unit (EIU):**

 
 
• The EIU is the research and analysis division of **The Economist Group**, which is headquartered in **London, UK**.
 
• It provides forecasting and advisory services through research and analysis on various topics, including global economic trends, politics, and industries.
 
• Founded in **1946**, it is recognized globally for its in-depth and reliable data analysis.
 
• In addition to the **Global Liveability Index**, the EIU also publishes other significant reports, such as the **Democracy Index** and **Worldwide Cost of Living Survey**.
 
 
 
• **Other Organizations Mentioned:**
 
 
• **PwC:** PricewaterhouseCoopers focuses on **professional services** like auditing, consulting, and tax advisory. It does not publish global indices like the Global Liveability Index.
 
• **KPMG:** A multinational professional services network, KPMG specializes in **audit, tax, and advisory services**. It is not involved in publishing indices like the Global Liveability Index.
 
• **World Economic Forum (WEF):** The WEF publishes significant reports such as the **Global Competitiveness Report** and the **Global Gender Gap Report**. It does not publish the Global Liveability Index.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for the Global Liveability Index:**
 
 
• **Stability:** Considers crime rates, conflict, and civil unrest in the city.
 
• **Healthcare:** Assesses the availability and quality of private and public healthcare services.
 
• **Culture and Environment:** Examines cultural availability, climate, corruption levels, and social freedoms.
 
• **Education:** Rates the availability and quality of primary, secondary, and tertiary education.
 
• **Infrastructure:** Evaluates public transport, housing, energy, and water provision, as well as roads and telecommunication systems.
 
 
 
• **Notable Cities in the Index:**
 
 
• **Vienna, Austria:** Regularly ranks as one of the most liveable cities due to its excellent healthcare, cultural offerings, and infrastructure.
 
• **Melbourne, Australia:** Frequently appears in the top ranks for its stability, healthcare, and educational resources.
 
• **Damascus, Syria:** Often ranks at the bottom of the index due to ongoing conflict and poor infrastructure.

question: The Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI) 2025 evaluates countries based on their performance in:

options.text: GHG Emissions, Renewable Energy, Energy Use, Climate Policy
Carbon Sequestration, Water Conservation, Biodiversity, Pollution Control
Disaster Preparedness, Adaptation Strategies, Mitigation Funding, Policy Implementation
Green Buildings, Sustainable Transport, Waste Management, Circular Economy

solution:
The correct answer is __**GHG Emissions, Renewable Energy, Energy Use, Climate Policy**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI)** is an annual publication that evaluates and compares the climate protection performance of 60 countries and the European Union, collectively responsible for over 90% of global greenhouse gas emissions.
 
• The CCPI focuses on four major parameters: **GHG Emissions, Renewable Energy, Energy Use, and Climate Policy**, providing a comprehensive overview of how nations are addressing climate change.
 
• **GHG Emissions:** This category assesses the total greenhouse gas emissions of a country, including emissions from fossil fuel combustion and industrial processes. It is a critical factor in evaluating climate mitigation efforts.
 
• **Renewable Energy:** The index evaluates the share of renewable energy in a country's energy mix and the progress made toward transitioning to sustainable energy sources.
 
• **Energy Use:** This parameter measures the energy consumption of a country per capita and its efficiency in utilizing energy resources to minimize environmental impact.
 
• **Climate Policy:** The index reviews the effectiveness of national and international policies implemented by governments to combat climate change, including commitments made under international frameworks like the Paris Agreement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Climate Change Performance Index (CCPI):**

 
 
• The CCPI has been published annually by Germanwatch, the NewClimate Institute, and the Climate Action Network (CAN) since **2005**.
 
• The index serves as a tool to enhance transparency in international climate politics and encourages countries to step up their climate protection efforts.
 
• Countries are scored on a scale from 0 (poor performance) to 100 (excellent performance) based on their contributions to global climate mitigation.
 
 
 
• **Paris Agreement:**
 
 
• The Paris Agreement, adopted in **2015**, is a landmark international treaty that aims to limit global warming to below **2°C** above pre-industrial levels.
 
• It encourages countries to submit Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) outlining their climate action plans.
 
 
 
• **Renewable Energy:**
 
 
• Renewable energy sources include solar, wind, hydroelectric, geothermal, and biomass energy, which are crucial for reducing reliance on fossil fuels.
 
• Countries like **Germany** and **Sweden** are leading in renewable energy adoption, serving as examples for others.
 
 
 
• **Global Greenhouse Gas Emissions:**
 
 
• Major contributors to global GHG emissions include energy production, transportation, agriculture, and industrial activities.
 
• Countries like **China**, **India**, and the **United States** are among the top emitters, making their climate policies crucial for global efforts.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **CCPI Scoring:**

 
 
• Each country is assigned a score based on its performance in the four categories, with rankings ranging from **high performers** to **low performers**.
 
• The rankings aim to highlight leaders and laggards in climate action, pushing governments to adopt better policies.
 
 
 
• **Role of Policies:**
 
 
• Effective climate policies are essential for achieving the goals set under international agreements like the Paris Agreement.
 
• Countries with strong policies often invest in renewable energy, energy efficiency, and carbon pricing mechanisms.
 
 
 
• **Significance of CCPI:**
 
 
• The index serves as a benchmark to evaluate the global progress toward climate mitigation and helps identify areas of improvement.
 
• It fosters international cooperation by sharing best practices and promoting accountability among nations.

• It specializes in developing global business leaders through its MBA and executive education programs.
 
• The IMD World Competitiveness Ranking is one of its flagship publications and is widely used by policymakers, businesses, and researchers globally.
 
 
 
• **Criteria for World Competitiveness Ranking:**
 
 
• The ranking is based on four main factors: **Economic Performance**, **Government Efficiency**, **Business Efficiency**, and **Infrastructure**.
 
• Each of these factors is further divided into sub-factors that include metrics like **GDP growth, productivity, employment, business regulations, and technology adoption**.
 
• The data is collected from both statistical sources and responses to surveys conducted among business executives worldwide.
 
 
 
• **Other Global Rankings:**
 
 
• The **World Economic Forum** publishes the **Global Competitiveness Report**, which is different from the IMD World Competitiveness Ranking.
 
• The **World Bank** releases reports such as the **Ease of Doing Business Index**, which evaluates business regulations across countries.
 
• The **International Monetary Fund (IMF)** focuses on financial stability and publishes reports like the **World Economic Outlook**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **IMD World Competitiveness Yearbook:**

 
 
• IMD publishes the **World Competitiveness Yearbook** annually, which contains detailed insights into the competitiveness rankings.
 
• The yearbook includes profiles of each country, highlighting key indicators and trends.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Competitiveness Rankings:**
 
 
• Countries with higher rankings tend to attract more foreign investments due to their favorable business environments.
 
• Lower-ranked countries often focus on reforms to improve their rankings, leading to better economic policies and infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Key Difference:**
 
 
• While both IMD and the World Economic Forum publish competitiveness rankings, IMD’s approach is more focused on **quantitative data and executive opinions**.
 
• The World Economic Forum's Global Competitiveness Report, on the other hand, places greater emphasis on **qualitative metrics** and long-term development goals.

• They eat the** primary consumers,** which are herbivores.
 
• These organisms are **heterotrophs**, more particularly, **omnivores and carnivores.**

• Decomposers are creatures that perform **decomposition** or the **breakdown of dead or decaying organisms.**

question: Detritivores in the soil break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**fragmentation**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

 
• Decomposition of detritus (dead remains of plants and animals) is the process in which decomposers **break down complex organic matter into inorganic substances like carbon dioxide, water, and nutrients**.
 
• The important steps in the process of decomposition are **fragmentation, leaching, catabolism, humification**, and **mineralization**.
 
 
• Detritivores (like earthworms) break down detritus into smaller particles. This process is called **fragmentation**.
 
• By the process of **leaching**, water-soluble inorganic nutrients go down into the soil horizon and get precipitated as unavailable salts.
 
• In the **catabolism** process, Bacterial and fungal enzymes degrade detritus into simpler inorganic substances.
 
• **Humification** leads to the accumulation of a dark-colored amorphous substance called **humus** that is highly resistant to microbial action and undergoes decomposition at an extremely slow rate.
 
• The **humus** is further degraded by some microbes and the release of inorganic nutrients occurs by the process known as **mineralization**.

question: In an ecosystem, vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**stratification**__

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• The process of identification and enumeration of plant and animal species of an ecosystem gives its species composition.
 
• The vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is called >stratification.
 
• For example, trees occupy the top vertical strata or layer of a forest, shrubs the second, and herbs and grasses occupy the bottom layers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Species composition**

 
 
• It differs from one ecosystem to another depending upon geography, topography, and climate.
 
• Each ecosystem has a biotic community composed of a particular grouping of species.
 
• Maximum species composition occurs in tropical rainforests and coral reefs.
 
• The minimum occurs in deserts and arctic regions.
 
 
 
• **Stratifications**
 
 
• Stratification is the occurrence of vertical zonation in the ecosystem & indicates the presence of favorable environmental conditions, for e.g., trees occupy top vertical strata or layer of a forest, shrubs, and herbs & grasses occupy the bottom layers. >Stratification helps in the accommodation of a large number & types of plants in the same area.
 
• It also provides a number of microhabitat & niches for various types of animals.
 
• It is absent or poor where environmental conditions are unfavorable, e.g. desert ecosystems have very few trees & shrubs.
 
 
 
• **Standing crop**
 
 
• A standing crop is an amount of living biomass in an ecosystem. It indicates the productivity & luxuriance of growth.
 
• It is expressed in the form of the number or biomass of organisms per unit area.
 
• A terrestrial ecosystem with a high standing crop possesses a forest while the one with a low standing crop occurs in grassland followed by the arid ecosystem.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Epilimnetic, metalimnetic, and hypolimnetic water strata** are characteristic layers in the thermal stratification of a lake.
 
• In a stratified lake, the **epilimnion** is the uppermost layer where the water is warm and well-mixed.
 
• The **metalimnion** (or thermocline) is the middle layer where temperature changes rapidly with depth.
 
• The **hypolimnion** is the deepest layer, consisting of cooler, denser water that is typically more stable and less mixed.
 
• This stratification is crucial for understanding lake ecology, including temperature distribution, oxygen levels, and nutrient cycling.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The process of stratification typically occurs in temperate regions during the summer when the surface water is heated by the sun.
 
• During the fall, the surface water cools, and the entire lake can mix in a process called **turnover**, which helps distribute oxygen and nutrients throughout the lake.
 
• Understanding these layers helps in managing lake ecosystems, particularly in relation to fisheries, water quality, and habitat conservation.
 
• Human activities such as pollution and water extraction can disrupt natural stratification, leading to ecological imbalances.

question: Eutrophication can be defined as:

options.text: the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an grassland ecosystem
the gradual decrease in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake
the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in desert areas
the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake

solution:
The correct answer is __**the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Eutrophication** is the gradual increase in the concentration of phosphorus, nitrogen, and other plant nutrients in an aging aquatic ecosystem such as a lake.
 
• This process leads to an increase in the growth of algae and aquatic plants, which can deplete the oxygen levels in the water and harm aquatic life.
 
• Eutrophication is typically caused by runoff from agriculture, wastewater, and other nutrient sources entering the water body.
 
• It can result in harmful algal blooms, fish kills, and loss of biodiversity in aquatic ecosystems.
 
• Management practices such as reducing nutrient runoff and improving wastewater treatment can help mitigate eutrophication.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Eutrophication** can also occur naturally over long periods, but human activities have accelerated the process significantly.
 
• In severe cases, eutrophication can create "dead zones" where oxygen levels are too low to support most marine life.
 
• Preventative measures include promoting sustainable agricultural practices, using phosphate-free detergents, and protecting wetlands that can filter nutrients.
 
• Public awareness and education on the impacts of nutrient pollution are crucial in addressing eutrophication.

question:
Consider the following statements about the LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) initiative:

1. It was launched by India during COP26.

2. It emphasizes government regulations over citizen participation.

3. It promotes sustainable habits such as reusing, reducing, and recycling.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 and 3 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The LiFE (Lifestyle for Environment) initiative was **launched by India during COP26 (26th UN Climate Change Conference of the Parties) held in Glasgow in 2021**.
 
• It is a global movement that aims to encourage individuals and communities to adopt environmentally conscious lifestyles to mitigate climate change and promote sustainability.
 
• The initiative does not prioritize government regulations but rather emphasizes **individual and community participation** to achieve its goals.
 
• It promotes sustainable habits such as the **3Rs: Reuse, Reduce, and Recycle**, and encourages the responsible use of resources.
 
• The LiFE initiative aligns with India’s commitments under the Paris Agreement and the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Explanation of Statement 1:** 
 
 
• The LiFE initiative was indeed launched by India at COP26 in Glasgow, highlighting its commitment to addressing climate change through collective action.
 
• It calls for a shift from a "use-and-dispose" economy to a "circular economy" that emphasizes resource efficiency and sustainability.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Statement 2:** 
 
 
• This statement is incorrect as the LiFE initiative prioritizes **citizen participation** over government regulations to achieve its objectives.
 
• It empowers individuals to take climate-friendly actions and make sustainable choices in their daily lives rather than solely relying on policy measures.
 
 
 
• **Explanation of Statement 3:** 
 
 
• The promotion of sustainable habits such as reducing waste, reusing materials, and recycling resources is a core component of the LiFE initiative.
 
• These actions align with the principles of environmental sustainability and are integral to achieving the goals of the initiative.
 
 
 
• **About the LiFE Initiative:**
 
 
• LiFE seeks to inspire individuals to take simple, yet impactful actions that collectively contribute to global environmental protection.
 
• The initiative encourages the adoption of behaviors such as conserving water, reducing food wastage, minimizing energy consumption, and opting for public transport or carpooling over personal vehicles.
 
• It also involves public awareness campaigns and educational programs to foster a culture of environmental responsibility.

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__**

__
 
• **Deep-sea hydrothermal ecosystems exist at depths exceeding 1,000 meters on the ocean floor.**
 
• These ecosystems feature **hydrothermal vents, fissures in the Earth's crust, emitting hot, mineral-rich fluids **into the surrounding seawater.
 
• Vents are formed by **tectonic and volcanic processes**, releasing heated water containing high mineral concentrations.
 
• Life in these extreme environments includes bacteria, archaea, and specialized organisms **adapted to high pressure, darkness, and temperature fluctuations.**
 
• Unique microbial communities thrive around vents, utilizing **chemosynthesis **to produce organic matter from inorganic compounds.
 
• Hydrothermal vent ecosystems support diverse life forms such as **tube worms, clams, shrimp, and octopuses.**
 
• They contribute to global **biogeochemical **cycles and offer insights into the origins of life on Earth and potential extraterrestrial habitats.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• An **ecosystem is the basic ecological unit **in which living organisms interact among themselves and with their surrounding physical environment.
 
• **Except for the deep sea hydro-thermal ecosystem**, the sun (sunlight) is the only source of energy for all ecosystems on earth.
 
• Out of the total incident solar radiation, **only 50% of it is photosynthetically active radiation (PAR).**
 
• **Plants capture only 2-10 per cent of the PAR **and this small amount of energy sustains the entire living world.

question: Which of these is a secondary pollutant that is included in Air Quality Index (AQI) calculations?
solution:
The correct answer is __**O₃**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Ozone (O₃)** is a secondary pollutant formed by the reaction of primary pollutants such as nitrogen oxides (NOₓ) and volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in the presence of sunlight.
 
• It is one of the key pollutants included in the **Air Quality Index (AQI)** calculations because of its significant impact on air quality and human health.
 
• O₃ can cause respiratory problems, reduce lung function, and aggravate asthma and other lung diseases, making it a critical pollutant to monitor.
 
• The formation of ground-level ozone is heavily influenced by weather conditions and is typically higher during sunny and hot weather.
 
• In AQI standards, ozone is monitored as an 8-hour average, and its levels are categorized into different ranges to inform the public about air quality.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **SO₂ (Sulfur Dioxide):**
 
 
• SO₂ is a primary pollutant released directly into the atmosphere from sources such as fossil fuel combustion and industrial processes.
 
• It contributes to acid rain formation and is harmful to human health, particularly the respiratory system.
 
• Although included in AQI, it is not classified as a secondary pollutant.
 
 
 
• **NO₂ (Nitrogen Dioxide):**
 
 
• NO₂ is a primary pollutant emitted from vehicles, industrial activities, and power generation.
 
• It is a precursor to secondary pollutants like ozone and particulate matter but is itself a primary pollutant.
 
• Exposure to NO₂ can lead to respiratory issues and reduced lung function.
 
 
 
• **PM10 (Particulate Matter 10):**
 
 
• PM10 refers to particulate matter with a diameter of 10 micrometers or smaller, which can be inhaled and cause health problems.
 
• It is a primary pollutant generated from sources like construction activities, road dust, and combustion processes.
 
• PM10 is a significant component of AQI but is not a secondary pollutant.

question: In July 2018, an experiment aboard the International Space Station cooled a cloud of atoms of which chemical element to one ten-millionth of one Kelvin above absolute zero, forming a Bose-Einstein Condensate in space?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Rubidium**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In 2018, scientists at the **Cold Atom Lab **confirmed the production of **Bose–Einstein condensates (BECs)** from **rubidium atoms,** achieving temperatures as low as 100 nanoKelvin, just a fraction above absolute zero.
 
• This remarkable feat surpassed the typical temperature of space, which hovers around 3 Kelvin. However, the researchers aimed for even lower temperatures, aspiring to surpass previous Earth-based BEC experiments.
 
• Bose–Einstein condensates are a fascinating state of matter in condensed matter physics, emerging when a gas of bosons, a type of subatomic particle, is cooled to extremely low temperatures near absolute zero.
 
• At such chilly conditions, a significant portion of bosons occupy the lowest quantum state, revealing intriguing quantum mechanical phenomena at a macroscopic scale, such as wavefunction interference.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• In June 2020, the **Cold Atom Laboratory's experiment** aboard the International Space Station (ISS) marked a significant milestone.
 
• Successfully generating a BEC of rubidium atoms in microgravity, the experiment observed these atoms for over a second while in free-fall.
 
• This breakthrough, initially a proof of concept, yielded intriguing results, with approximately half of the atoms forming a magnetically insensitive halo-like cloud surrounding the main body of the BEC.

question: In 1957, who redefined a model that predicted the shape of individual molecules based on the extent of electron-pair electrostatic repulsion?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nyholm and Gillespie**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Ronald Gillespie and Ronald Nyholm **significantly enhanced the **valence shell electron pair repulsion (VSEPR) model** in **1957,** refining its level of detail and its ability to discern between various molecular geometries.
 
• The **VSEPR theory** represents a **foundational concept in chemistry,** offering a straightforward explanation for the shapes of molecules.
 
• It posits a direct relationship between molecular geometry and the count of valence electrons, further providing predictions for precise molecular structures, including bond angles.
 
• The theory was initially proposed by **Nevil Sidgwick and Herbert Powell** in 1940, yet its roots trace back to Ryutaro Tsuchida of Japan, who originally suggested the notion of a correlation between molecular geometry and the number of valence electron pairs in 1939.
 
• However, it was the contributions of Gillespie and Nyholm that significantly expanded and refined the VSEPR model, solidifying its position as a fundamental tool in the study of molecular structures.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The VSEPR model**, or the Valence Shell Electron Pair Repulsion model, offers predictions for** the geometry of the majority of polyatomic molecules and ions.**
 
• It achieves this by solely considering the count of electron pairs surrounding the central atom, while disregarding all other valence electrons.
 
• According to the model, **lone pairs of electrons localize** on the central atom, while each bonded pair is shared between two atoms.
 
• The lone pair electrons in a molecule occupy a larger spatial region compared to the bonding pairs of electrons.
 
• Also referred to as the Gillespie-Nyholm theory, the VSEPR theory is named after its principal developers, Ronald Gillespie and Ronald Nyholm.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Galileo Galilei** is incorrectly paired with the **wave theory of light**.
 
• Galileo Galilei was an Italian astronomer, physicist, and engineer, sometimes described as a polymath. He is known for his contributions to observational astronomy, including the telescopic confirmation of the phases of Venus, the discovery of the four largest satellites of Jupiter, and the observation and analysis of sunspots.
 
• The wave theory of light is primarily attributed to **Christiaan Huygens** in the 17th century and was later expanded by other scientists, including Thomas Young and Augustin-Jean Fresnel.
 
• Galileo's contributions were more focused on mechanics, motion, and astronomy rather than the wave theory of light.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Heinrich Rudolf Hertz** is correctly credited with the generation of electromagnetic waves. He was the first to conclusively prove the existence of electromagnetic waves by generating them in his laboratory.
 
• **Albert Einstein** is correctly known for explaining the photoelectric effect, for which he received the Nobel Prize in Physics in 1921.
 
• **Michael Faraday** is accurately associated with the laws of electromagnetic induction, which describe how a magnetic field can interact with an electric circuit to produce an electromotive force (EMF).
 
• The correct pairing for the wave theory of light would be **Christiaan Huygens** or **Thomas Young**.

question: What is the main purpose of developing ISRO's MiniSAR (Miniaturized Synthetic Aperture Radar) at X-Band?

options.text: To replace the PSLV upper stage with a lighter radar system
To monitor atmospheric pressure changes over remote
To provide high-resolution X-Band radar imagery using compact airborne systems
To offer real-time video transmission during crewed missions

solution:
The correct answer is __**To provide high-resolution X-Band radar imagery using compact airborne systems.**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **MiniSAR (Miniaturized Synthetic Aperture Radar)** is developed by ISRO to provide high-resolution radar imagery at X-Band frequencies.
 
• This technology is designed specifically for compact airborne systems, enabling precision imaging capabilities for remote sensing and Earth observation.
 
• The X-Band radar operates at frequencies between 8–12 GHz, allowing for detailed surface mapping, even in adverse weather conditions like clouds and rain.
 
• MiniSAR is pivotal in monitoring Earth's surface for geological, environmental, and agricultural applications, enhancing spatial resolution in radar imaging systems.
 
• Its compact design ensures adaptability to small platforms such as drones or lightweight aircraft, making it cost-effective and versatile for various missions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 1: To replace the PSLV upper stage with a lighter radar system**

 
 
• This option is incorrect, as MiniSAR is not related to the propulsion stages of the PSLV (Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle).
 
• PSLV stages are designed for launching satellites into orbit, and radar systems like MiniSAR focus on Earth observation and imaging.
 
• Radar systems are payloads, not components of rocket stages, and serve entirely different purposes compared to PSLV stages.
 
 
 
• **Option 2: To monitor atmospheric pressure changes over remote areas**
 
 
• This option is incorrect because atmospheric pressure monitoring is typically performed using barometers or other meteorological instruments, not radar systems like MiniSAR.
 
• Radar systems are used for imaging and surface mapping, not atmospheric measurements.
 
• MiniSAR's primary focus is on high-resolution imaging rather than atmospheric studies.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: To offer real-time video transmission during crewed missions**
 
 
• This option is incorrect, as MiniSAR is not designed for video transmission but for radar imaging.
 
• Real-time video transmission during crewed missions is typically handled by communication systems, not synthetic aperture radar.
 
• MiniSAR's utility lies in remote sensing and Earth observation rather than real-time video applications.

• India Post Payments Bank (IPPB) introduced a **QR (Quick Response) card** to facilitate cashless and cardless transactions for its customers.
 
• The IPPB QR card uses a **secure, Aadhaar-enabled payment system** that eliminates the need for remembering account numbers or PINs.
 
• This technology enables customers to perform transactions **without the need for a physical debit card** or an internet connection.
 
• The QR code on the card is scanned at IPPB access points, and the transaction is authenticated using the customer’s biometric data, such as a fingerprint.
 
• The QR card is part of IPPB's efforts to promote **financial inclusion** by providing easy and secure banking services to rural and underserved populations.

• Although NFC is a popular technology for cashless transactions, it requires special-enabled devices and is not used by India Post Payments Bank for withdrawals.

• It offers services such as savings and current accounts, remittances, and financial products like insurance and mutual funds.
 
• IPPB's innovative QR card is a step toward making banking accessible to all, especially in rural and remote areas.

question: At which Lagrange point does the Aditya-L1 spacecraft orbit?
solution:
The correct answer is __**L1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The Aditya-L1 spacecraft is India's first dedicated solar mission and it orbits around the **Lagrange Point 1 (L1)**, located approximately 1.5 million kilometers from Earth.
 
• The L1 point is a unique location between the Earth and the Sun where the gravitational forces of both bodies and the centrifugal force of the spacecraft balance, allowing it to stay in a stable orbit.
 
• This position provides an uninterrupted view of the Sun, making it ideal for monitoring solar activities such as solar flares and coronal mass ejections.
 
• Aditya-L1 carries seven scientific payloads designed to study various aspects of the Sun, including its photosphere, chromosphere, and outermost layer, the corona.
 
• The mission aims to enhance our understanding of solar dynamics, space weather, and their impact on the Earth's environment and technological systems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **L2**

 
 
• Lagrange Point 2 (L2) is another stable position in the Earth-Sun system, located on the far side of Earth, opposite the Sun, approximately 1.5 million kilometers away.
 
• L2 is commonly used for space observatories such as the James Webb Space Telescope because it provides a stable environment with minimal interference from Earth's radiation and thermal effects.
 
• At this point, the spacecraft can maintain a fixed position relative to the Earth and Sun, making it ideal for deep-space observations.
 
 
 
• **GEO (Geostationary Earth Orbit)**
 
 
• A geostationary orbit is a circular orbit approximately 35,786 kilometers above Earth's equator.
 
• Satellites in GEO appear stationary from the Earth's surface because their orbital period matches Earth's rotation period.
 
• GEO is commonly used for communication, weather monitoring, and broadcasting satellites such as GSAT and INSAT.
 
 
 
• **SSO (Sun-Synchronous Orbit)**
 
 
• A Sun-Synchronous Orbit is a near-polar orbit in which a satellite passes over the same region of Earth at the same local solar time every day.
 
• Satellites in this orbit are used for Earth observation, remote sensing, and environmental monitoring due to consistent lighting conditions.
 
• Examples include satellites like India's Cartosat series for high-resolution imaging.

NISAR satellite carries dual-frequency radar bands ______ and ______.

The correct answer is __**L & S**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **NISAR (NASA-ISRO Synthetic Aperture Radar)** is a collaborative project between **NASA** (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) and **ISRO** (Indian Space Research Organisation).
 
• The satellite is equipped with **dual-frequency radar bands**, specifically the **L-band** and **S-band**, making it the first satellite to use these frequencies together.
 
• The **L-band radar** operates at a frequency of 1-2 GHz and is particularly effective in penetrating dense vegetation and monitoring changes in the Earth's surface.
 
• The **S-band radar** operates at a frequency range of 2-4 GHz and is used for applications like soil moisture mapping and vegetation monitoring.
 
• The purpose of these radar bands is to facilitate **high-resolution imaging** for a variety of applications, including disaster monitoring, agriculture, forestry, and climate change studies.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NISAR Mission Overview:**

 
 
• The satellite is expected to be launched in **early 2024** from **India’s Satish Dhawan Space Centre** using the **GSLV Mk II** launch vehicle.
 
• The primary objective of NISAR is to provide data on **ecosystem disturbances, ice-sheet collapse, and natural disasters like earthquakes, tsunamis, and landslides**.
 
• The satellite aims to **monitor global environmental changes** and their impact on Earth’s surface.
 
 
 
• **L-Band Radar:**
 
 
• The L-band radar penetrates through vegetation, snow, and ice, enabling it to monitor **subsurface features** and detect subtle changes over time.
 
• This band is highly effective for monitoring large-scale changes such as **deforestation, glacial movement, and soil erosion**.
 
 
 
• **S-Band Radar:**
 
 
• The S-band radar is utilized for detailed surface-level observations, including **soil moisture and land cover changes**.
 
• It is particularly useful for monitoring **agriculture, vegetation dynamics, and coastal areas**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of NISAR:**
 
 
• The satellite will be the **world’s most advanced radar imaging satellite** for Earth observation, offering data that is **crucial for scientific research** and disaster management.
 
• Its mission life is expected to be **at least three years**, with comprehensive global coverage.
 
• It will provide **unprecedented temporal and spatial resolution**, enabling researchers to better understand the planet.
 
 
 
• **Collaboration Between NASA and ISRO:**
 
 
• NASA is providing the L-band radar, while ISRO is supplying the S-band radar, along with the spacecraft and launch services.
 
• This partnership highlights the **strength of international collaboration** in advancing Earth observation capabilities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Dual-Frequency Advantage:** Combining L-band and S-band radar frequencies allows for a **multi-dimensional view of Earth's surface**, improving data accuracy and reliability.
 
• **Applications:** The satellite will be instrumental in **agriculture monitoring, coastal erosion studies, urban development planning, and disaster response.**
 
• **Technological Milestone:** NISAR represents a significant step forward in radar imaging technology, setting a new benchmark for **Earth observation satellites**.
 
• **Global Reach:** The data from NISAR will be freely available to researchers worldwide, fostering global collaboration in understanding and mitigating environmental challenges.
