question: In which of the following years was the National Food Security Act enacted in India ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2013**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **__Important Points__**

__
 
• **National Food Security Act** was enacted to provide food and nutritional security in the human life cycle approach, by ensuring access to an adequate quantity of quality food at affordable prices to people to live a life with dignity and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

 
• **Salient features of the National Food Security Act 2013**.

 
 
• Public Distribution System (PDS) is now governed by provisions of the National Food Security Act, 2013 (NFSA).
 
• Coverage under PDS is de-linked from the erstwhile 'poverty estimates'.
 
• The Act provides coverage for nearly 2/3rd of the country's total population, basis Census 2011 population estimates.
 
• 75% of the Rural and 50% of the Urban population is entitled to receive highly subsidized foodgrains under two categories of beneficiaries – Antodaya Anna Yojana (AAY) households and Priority Households (PHH).
 
• State/UT-wise coverage is determined by the erstwhile Planning Commission (now NITI Ayog) on the basis of the 2011-12 Household Consumption Expenditure survey of NSSO.
 
• The Act entitles 35 kg of foodgrains per AAY Household per month, whereas 5 Kg of foodgrain per PHH Person per month.
 
• Identification of beneficiaries/households under NFSA is done by the respective State/UT Government, which is required to frame its own criteria.
 
• Highly subsidized Central Issue Prices of Re.1, Rs.2, and Rs.3 for Coarse-grains, Wheat, and Rice respectively, kept unchanged till June 2019.
 
• No reduction in foodgrains allocation to any State/UT under NFSA. Allocation gaps if any, are covered with Tide-Over allocation.
 
• The eldest woman of the beneficiary household (18 years or above) is considered as 'Head of Family' for the purpose of issuing ration cards.
 
• Grievance redressal mechanism, through State Food Commissions, DGROs, Vigilance Committees at different levels are provisioned for Women Empowerment.
 
• Provisions for disclosure of records relating to PDS operations, placing of beneficiaries' list in public domain/portals, for enhanced transparency.
 
• Assistance to States/UTs for meeting expenditure on intra-State transportation & handling of foodgrains and FPS Dealers' margin.

__
 
• The Prime Minister's Employment Generation Programme (**PMEGP**) was launched in the year **2008**.
 
• **PMEGP** is a credit-linked subsidy program aimed at generating self-employment opportunities through the establishment of micro-enterprises in the non-farm sector by helping traditional artisans and unemployed youth.
 
• The scheme is implemented by the **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** at the national level and by the State KVIC Directorates, State Khadi and Village Industries Boards (KVIBs), and District Industries Centers (DICs) at the state level.

• The **Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC)** is a statutory body created by an Act of Parliament, and it functions under the Ministry of Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises.
 
• The scheme was formulated by merging two schemes, namely the **Prime Minister's Rojgar Yojana (PMRY)** and the **Rural Employment Generation Programme (REGP)**, to enhance the effectiveness of employment generation in rural and urban areas.
 
• Beneficiaries under the scheme can avail of financial assistance in the form of margin money subsidy, which is adjusted against the loan amount provided by the banks.
 
• The scheme has specific eligibility criteria, including age, educational qualification, and project cost limits, to ensure that genuine and deserving candidates benefit from it.
 
• Entrepreneurs who set up projects under PMEGP also receive training and handholding support to ensure the sustainability and success of their enterprises.

question: Who are the main beneficiaries of the PM-Kisan Maandhan Yojana?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Marginal farmers**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The PM-Kisan Maandhan Yojana is a pension scheme introduced by the Government of India to provide social security to **marginal farmers and small farmers.**
 
• It was launched on **12 September 2019** in Jharkhand by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, aiming to ensure financial stability for farmers in their old age.
 
• The scheme provides a **monthly pension of Rs. 3000** after the age of 60 to farmers who enroll and contribute during their working years.
 
• Farmers within the **age group of 18 to 40 years** with cultivable land of up to 2 hectares are eligible to apply for the scheme.
 
• The contributions to the pension fund vary between Rs. 55 and Rs. 200 per month, depending on the age of entry, and the government matches the contribution.
 
• The scheme is managed by the Life Insurance Corporation (LIC) of India, which ensures the disbursement of pensions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Fishermen**

 
 
• While fishermen are not the primary beneficiaries of PM-Kisan Maandhan Yojana, they are supported under other schemes such as the **Pradhan Mantri Matsya Sampada Yojana (PMMSY)**.
 
• PMMSY aims to enhance fish production, create employment, and improve infrastructure for fishermen and aquaculture farmers.
 
• It supports the development of cold storage chains, fish markets, and modernized fishing techniques.
 
 
 
• **Women SHGs (Self-Help Groups)**
 
 
• Women SHGs are not the target group for PM-Kisan Maandhan Yojana; however, they are beneficiaries under schemes like **Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission (DAY-NRLM)**.
 
• DAY-NRLM promotes women's empowerment by providing financial assistance, skill development, and livelihood opportunities through SHGs.
 
• It focuses on poverty alleviation by enabling SHG members to access credit, market linkages, and entrepreneurship opportunities.
 
 
 
• **Retired Civil Servants**
 
 
• Retired civil servants are not eligible for the PM-Kisan Maandhan Yojana as they typically receive pensions through government pension schemes.
 
• They are supported under the **National Pension System (NPS)**, which ensures old-age income security for government employees and other subscribers.

subject: GK
question: The GOBARdhan scheme focuses on converting which of the following into valuable resources like compost and biogas?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Agricultural waste and cattle dung**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The GOBARdhan (Galvanizing Organic Bio-Agro Resources Dhan) scheme was launched by the Government of India as part of the Swachh Bharat Mission-Gramin (SBM-G) initiative.
 
• It aims to promote the management and conversion of organic waste such as agricultural waste, cattle dung, and other biodegradable materials into biogas, compost, and other useful resources.
 
• The scheme supports rural areas by creating opportunities for farmers and households to generate energy and organic manure while addressing waste management issues.
 
• Biogas produced under the scheme can be used for cooking, electricity generation, or as a fuel, contributing to renewable energy development.
 
• It also helps reduce greenhouse gas emissions and improves sanitation in rural areas by providing a systematic waste management framework.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial effluents and hazardous waste**

 
 
• These are waste materials generated by industries, including chemicals, heavy metals, and other toxic substances.
 
• Industrial effluents are typically managed through specialized treatment plants to reduce environmental pollution.
 
• Hazardous waste disposal requires strict regulations and safe handling procedures due to its potential to harm human health and ecosystems.
 
• The GOBARdhan scheme does not focus on industrial effluents and hazardous waste but rather on organic and biodegradable waste.
 
 
 
• **Plastic waste and e-waste**
 
 
• Plastic waste includes discarded plastic materials, which pose significant environmental challenges due to their non-biodegradable nature.
 
• E-waste refers to electronic waste such as old computers, mobile phones, and other electronic devices.
 
• The management of plastic waste involves recycling and reducing plastic usage, while e-waste management focuses on recovering valuable materials and safe disposal.
 
• These types of waste are not covered under the GOBARdhan scheme, as it specifically targets organic waste management.
 
 
 
• **Marine waste and fish**
 
 
• Marine waste includes debris and pollutants found in oceans and seas, such as plastics, fishing nets, and other materials.
 
• Fish waste can be utilized in specific industries for producing fishmeal and fertilizers, but it is not the focus of the GOBARdhan scheme.
 
• The scheme is designed to cater primarily to rural areas and agricultural communities, addressing biodegradable waste rather than marine waste.
 
 
 
• **Key Theme: Waste Management through Organic Resources**
 
 
• The GOBARdhan scheme is part of India's broader initiative to promote sustainable waste management practices.
 
• It aligns with the goals of the Swachh Bharat Mission and emphasizes the importance of utilizing organic waste for energy and fertilizer production.
 
• By addressing rural waste management challenges, the scheme contributes to environmental sustainability, renewable energy, and rural economic development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The National Health Mission (NHM) is a flagship health program by the Government of India launched in 2013 to achieve universal access to equitable, affordable, and quality healthcare services.
 
• One of its core objectives is the **reduction in child mortality** and maternal mortality rates by improving the quality of healthcare services provided at various levels.
 
• The NHM focuses on **Reproductive, Maternal, Newborn, Child, and Adolescent Health (RMNCH+A)** as a strategic approach to address key health challenges, including child mortality.
 
• Various initiatives under NHM, such as the Janani Suraksha Yojana (JSY) and Integrated Child Development Services (ICDS), aim to ensure safe deliveries and proper nutrition for children, contributing to reduced child mortality rates.
 
• NHM has significantly contributed to improving India's Infant Mortality Rate (IMR) and Under-5 Mortality Rate (U5MR) through better healthcare infrastructure and community-level interventions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Industrial Growth**

 
 
• Industrial growth refers to the expansion of industries in terms of production, employment, and technological advancements.
 
• It is primarily driven by economic policies, investments, technological innovations, and infrastructure development.
 
• While industrial growth is critical for economic development, it is not directly related to the objectives of the NHM, which focuses on healthcare and public health services.
 
 
 
• **Space Exploration**
 
 
• Space exploration is the scientific investigation of outer space using advanced technologies such as satellites, probes, and telescopes.
 
• In India, space exploration is led by ISRO (Indian Space Research Organisation), contributing significantly to global space missions and advancements in satellite technology.
 
• This area of interest is unrelated to the NHM, which focuses on improving health outcomes rather than scientific research or space missions.
 
 
 
• **Wildlife Protection**
 
 
• Wildlife protection involves conserving ecosystems, preserving biodiversity, and safeguarding endangered species.
 
• In India, wildlife protection is governed by laws such as the Wildlife Protection Act, 1972, and initiatives like Project Tiger and Project Elephant.
 
• While wildlife protection is a significant environmental concern, it does not align with the healthcare-centric objectives of the NHM.

subject: GK
question:
Consider the following statements about Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme:

(1) The NBS scheme provides fixed per-kg subsidy rates for N, P, K, and S in non-urea fertilizers.

(2) Freight assistance is also provided.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Both 1 and 2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) scheme** was introduced by the Government of India in **April 2010** to regulate subsidies for fertilizers other than urea. It promotes balanced fertilizer usage across the country.
 
• **Statement 1:** The NBS scheme provides fixed per-kg subsidy rates for nutrients such as **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and sulfur (S)**. These subsidies are announced by the government annually based on the international and domestic prices of fertilizers. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• **Statement 2:** Freight assistance is also provided under the scheme to ensure the availability of fertilizers across the country, especially in remote regions. This ensures equitable distribution and accessibility for farmers. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Under the NBS scheme, fertilizer companies are compensated to sell fertilizers to farmers at subsidized rates, ensuring affordability for farmers while promoting agricultural productivity.
 
• The scheme applies to all **phosphatic and potassic fertilizers** such as DAP (Di-Ammonium Phosphate), MOP (Muriate of Potash), and complex fertilizers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Purpose of the NBS Scheme:**

 
 
• To encourage the balanced use of fertilizers by subsidizing nutrients rather than specific fertilizers.
 
• To ensure an adequate supply of fertilizers to farmers at reasonable prices.
 
• To reduce the financial burden on farmers and promote sustainable agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Fertilizer Subsidy Structure:**
 
 
• The subsidy is calculated based on the nutrient content of fertilizers, such as the per-kg subsidy for **nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), potassium (K), and sulfur (S).**
 
• For example, if the per-kg subsidy on nitrogen is announced as Rs. 20, then a fertilizer with 10 kg of nitrogen content will receive a subsidy of Rs. 200 per bag.
 
 
 
• **Challenges with the NBS Scheme:**
 
 
• The scheme focuses on non-urea fertilizers, whereas urea continues to be heavily subsidized, leading to an imbalance in fertilizer usage.
 
• Farmers often overuse urea due to its lower cost, resulting in soil degradation and declining nutrient efficiency.
 
• The government incurs a significant financial burden annually due to the fertilizer subsidy.
 
 
 
• **Steps Taken to Improve the Scheme:**
 
 
• Promoting the use of organic fertilizers and bio-fertilizers to reduce dependency on chemical fertilizers.
 
• Encouraging farmers to adopt integrated nutrient management (INM) practices to improve soil health and productivity.
 
• Digitizing the subsidy disbursement process to ensure transparency and reduce leakages.
 
 
 
• **Important Data:**
 
 
• India is the second-largest consumer of fertilizers in the world, with a significant portion of the subsidy budget allocated to the fertilizer sector.
 
• The government allocated approximately **Rs. 1.75 lakh crore** for fertilizer subsidies in the **Union Budget 2023-24**.
 
• Urea accounts for the majority of fertilizer consumption in India, followed by DAP and MOP.

subject: GK
question:
Consider the following statements regarding the Urea Subsidy Scheme:

Statement 1: Urea is sold to farmers at a fixed Maximum Retail Price (MRP).

Statement 2: The subsidy is directly transferred to the bank accounts of farmers.

Which of the above is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Statement 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Urea** is the only fertilizer in India that remains under statutory price control. The **Government of India** fixes a uniform **Maximum Retail Price (MRP)** for urea across the country, ensuring it remains affordable for the farming community. The current MRP is approximately **Rs 242 per 45 kg bag** (excluding taxes and neem coating charges). ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• Under the **Direct Benefit Transfer (DBT)** system for fertilizers, the subsidy is not paid directly to the farmers' bank accounts. Instead, the **Government of India** pays the subsidy amount directly to the **fertilizer companies** (manufacturers or importers) after the actual sale is made to the farmer through a **Point of Sale (PoS)** device. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Urea Subsidy** is the difference between the **cost of production** (for domestic units) or the **Import Parity Price (IPP)** (for imported urea) and the fixed **MRP** paid by the farmers. This entire fiscal burden is borne by the **Central Government**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Neem Coated Urea (NCU):**

 
 
• In **2015**, the government made it mandatory for all domestic producers to produce **100% Neem Coated Urea**.
 
• This initiative was launched to prevent the **illegal diversion** of highly subsidized urea for industrial uses and to improve **Nitrogen Use Efficiency (NUE)**.
 
 
 
• **Nutrient Based Subsidy (NBS) Scheme:**
 
 
• Unlike urea, Phosphatic and Potassic (P&K) fertilizers like **DAP** and **MOP** are governed by the **NBS Scheme** launched in **April 2010**.
 
• Under **NBS**, a fixed amount of subsidy is provided based on the nutrient content (Nitrogen, Phosphorus, Potash, and Sulphur) rather than a fixed retail price.
 
 
 
• **New Urea Policy (NUP) 2015:**
 
 
• The **NUP 2015** was implemented to maximize indigenous production, promote **energy efficiency** in urea plants, and rationalize the total subsidy burden.

question: What is the primary focus of the National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)?

options.text: Promoting cultivation of a tropical oil-rich crop

solution:
The correct answer is __**Promoting cultivation of a tropical oil-rich crop**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Mission on Edible Oils-Oil Palm (NMEO-OP)** is a **Centrally Sponsored Scheme** launched by the Government of India in **August 2021** to transform the edible oil sector.
 
• The primary objective of this mission is to significantly increase the domestic production of **Crude Palm Oil (CPO)** by promoting the cultivation of **Oil Palm**, which is a highly productive **tropical oil-rich crop**.
 
• The mission targets expanding the area under oil palm cultivation to **10 lakh hectares** by **2025-26** and further to **16.7 lakh hectares** by **2029-30**, focusing heavily on the **North-Eastern states** and the **Andaman and Nicobar Islands**.
 
• With a total financial outlay of **Rs. 11,040 crore**, the initiative aims to reduce India's heavy reliance on edible oil imports, which currently account for nearly **60%** of the total domestic consumption.
 
• The scheme provides **financial assistance** to farmers for planting material and maintenance, while also establishing a **Viability Price** mechanism to protect farmers from the volatility of international CPO prices.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Oil Palm Characteristics:**

 
 
• It is a perennial **tropical crop** that yields much higher quantities of oil per unit of land compared to traditional oilseeds like **mustard**, **groundnut**, or **soybean**.
 
• A single hectare of oil palm can produce approximately **4 tonnes of oil**, which is about **10 to 46 times** more productive than other oilseed crops.
 
 
 
• **Economic Significance:**
 
 
• India is the **world's largest importer** of edible oils, spending a massive amount of foreign exchange annually on imports primarily from **Indonesia** and **Malaysia**.
 
• The mission is a key component of the **Atmanirbhar Bharat** (Self-reliant India) initiative, aiming to achieve self-sufficiency in **vegetable oils** and enhance the income of **Indian farmers**.

question: Which scheme provides insurance to farmers against crop failure?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)** is a crop insurance scheme launched by the Government of India on **13th January 2016** to provide comprehensive insurance coverage to farmers against crop failure due to non-preventable natural calamities.
 
• The scheme aims to **stabilize farmers' income**, ensure the continuity of farming, and encourage farmers to adopt innovative and modern agricultural practices.
 
• Farmers are required to pay a **minimal premium rate** of 2% for Kharif crops, 1.5% for Rabi crops, and 5% for commercial and horticultural crops, with the remaining premium being subsidized by the government.
 
• **Coverage:** The scheme covers risks such as drought, flood, hailstorm, cyclone, pest infestation, and other similar non-preventable risks.
 
• The scheme is implemented through **private and public insurance companies** under the coordination of state governments and financial institutions, ensuring a seamless claim settlement process for farmers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Rashtriya Krishi Vikas Yojana (RKVY):**

 
 
• Launched in **2007**, RKVY aims to achieve 4% annual growth in agriculture by providing financial assistance to states for agriculture and allied sectors.
 
• It is a flexible and state-driven scheme that incentivizes states to increase investment in agriculture and allied sectors.
 
 
 
• **Sub-Mission on Agricultural Mechanization (SMAM):**
 
 
• Launched in **2014-15**, SMAM focuses on promoting agricultural mechanization to increase productivity and reduce labor dependency.
 
• It provides subsidies for the purchase of agricultural machinery and implements, particularly for small and marginal farmers.
 
 
 
• **Agriculture Infrastructure Fund (AIF):**
 
 
• Introduced in **2020**, AIF aims to provide medium to long-term debt financing for investment in viable projects for post-harvest management infrastructure and community farming assets.
 
• It is a part of the government's Atmanirbhar Bharat Abhiyan to strengthen agriculture infrastructure and supply chains.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of PMFBY:**
 
 
• It integrates technology like **remote sensing, GPS, and drones** for faster and more accurate assessment of crop loss.
 
• The scheme ensures **timely claim settlement**, with claims disbursed to the farmers' bank accounts directly.
 
• Coverage extends to **post-harvest losses** due to cyclones and unseasonal rains.
 
 
 
• **Important Points:**
 
 
• The **National Crop Insurance Portal** is the digital platform for PMFBY, allowing farmers to register and track claims online.
 
• PMFBY is applicable to **loanee farmers** (those who take loans from financial institutions) and non-loanee farmers.
 
• The scheme was revised in **2020** to make it voluntary for farmers and to address regional disparities in insurance coverage.
 
• It is considered the **world’s largest crop insurance scheme** based on farmer participation and coverage.

question: The Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK) aims to screen and manage children up to what age?
solution:
The correct answer is __**18 years**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Rashtriya Bal Swasthya Karyakram (RBSK)** is an initiative under the **National Health Mission (NHM)** launched by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare, Government of India** in **February 2013**.
 
• The program aims to provide early detection and intervention services for children from birth to **18 years** to address **defects at birth, deficiencies, diseases, and development delays including disabilities**.
 
• RBSK covers **children enrolled in Anganwadi centers and government and government-aided schools** across the country.
 
• Screening is conducted by **Mobile Health Teams** using a defined protocol, focusing on **4 Ds**: Defects, Deficiencies, Diseases, and Developmental Delays including disabilities.
 
• Children identified with health conditions are referred to **District Early Intervention Centers (DEICs)**, where they receive free treatment and management services.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Age Group Coverage:**

 
 
• The program focuses on children in the **age group of 0-18 years**, covering infants, preschool children, and school-going children.
 
• Services include screening for **newborns, children in Anganwadi centers (0-6 years), and school children (6-18 years).**
 
 
 
• **Defects at Birth:**
 
 
• Common birth defects screened include **neural tube defects, congenital heart disease, cleft lip/palate, and Down syndrome**.
 
• Early detection helps in timely medical intervention and management.
 
 
 
• **Deficiencies:**
 
 
• Screening is focused on conditions such as **anemia, vitamin deficiencies, and iodine deficiency disorders**.
 
• Children identified with deficiencies are provided **nutritional supplements and dietary guidance**.
 
 
 
• **Diseases:**
 
 
• RBSK addresses diseases such as **skin conditions, ear infections, dental caries, and febrile illnesses**.
 
• Timely treatment reduces the risk of long-term complications.
 
 
 
• **Developmental Delays:**
 
 
• Developmental delays and disabilities such as **cerebral palsy, autism, and vision/hearing impairments** are identified and managed.
 
• Special therapies like **speech therapy, occupational therapy, and physiotherapy** are provided at DEICs.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Implementation:** The program is implemented in collaboration with state governments and works through **mobile health teams, DEICs, and referral networks**.
 
• **Benefits:** RBSK ensures **free treatment and follow-up services** for children under its coverage, reducing the burden of healthcare costs for families.
 
• **Objective:** The primary aim of RBSK is to improve **child health indicators** and reduce childhood morbidity and mortality rates in India.
 
• **Target Population:** Approximately **270 million children** across the country benefit from the program.
 
• **Significance:** RBSK plays a crucial role in achieving **universal health coverage and improving the quality of life** for children with health challenges.

question: What is a key benefit provided under Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Free delivery and C-section services**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Janani Shishu Suraksha Karyakram (JSSK)** was launched by the **Ministry of Health and Family Welfare (MoHFW)** on **1st June 2011** to provide completely free and cashless services to pregnant women and sick newborns.
 
• The scheme guarantees **free and cashless delivery**, which includes both **normal vaginal deliveries** and surgical **Caesarean sections (C-sections)** at all public health institutions.
 
• It aims to eliminate **out-of-pocket expenses (OOPE)** incurred by pregnant women and their families, thereby encouraging **institutional deliveries** to reduce the **Maternal Mortality Ratio (MMR)** and **Infant Mortality Rate (IMR)**.
 
• Under JSSK, pregnant women are entitled to **free drugs and consumables**, **free diagnostics** (including blood and urine tests and ultrasounds), and **free blood transfusion** services if required.
 
• The initiative also provides a **free diet** for the duration of the hospital stay (up to **3 days** for normal delivery and up to **7 days** for a C-section).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Transport Services**:

 
 
• Contrary to the concept of 'paid transport', JSSK provides **free transport** from home to the health facility and between facilities in case of **referral**.
 
• It also includes a **free drop-back** from the facility to the patient's home after a mandatory stay of **48 hours** post-delivery.
 
 
 
• **Sick Infant Coverage**:
 
 
• The scheme covers **sick infants** up to **one year** of age (expanded from the initial 30 days) for all treatment-related costs in public hospitals.
 
• This includes **free medicines**, **diagnostics**, and **transportation** to ensure timely medical intervention for pediatric emergencies.
 
 
 
• **Exemption from User Charges**:
 
 
• JSSK mandates that no **user charges** are to be levied for any services provided to the mother or the infant, including registration fees or bed charges.

question: SHC scheme is implemented by which ministry?

options.text: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC)
Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoA & FW)
Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)

solution:
The correct answer is __**Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare (MoA & FW)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Soil Health Card (SHC) scheme was launched by the **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare** to promote soil testing and balanced use of fertilizers.
 
• The **SHC scheme** was launched by the Government of India in **February 2015** to address the issue of soil degradation and improve the overall productivity of agricultural land.
 
• The scheme aims to provide farmers with a **soil health card** that contains information about the nutrient status of their soil and recommendations for appropriate fertilizer application.
 
• The implementation of the SHC scheme involves **soil sample collection, testing, and issuing cards to farmers**, enabling them to make informed decisions for crop production.
 
• The Soil Health Card scheme has been implemented across all states and union territories of India, covering millions of farmers and agricultural holdings.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of the SHC Scheme:**

 
 
• To assess the soil quality and nutrient composition for better agricultural practices.
 
• To promote the balanced use of fertilizers and reduce the excessive application of chemical fertilizers.
 
• To improve the **long-term soil health** and enhance agricultural productivity sustainably.
 
 
 
• **Process of Soil Health Card Generation:**
 
 
• Soil samples are collected from the farmer's field based on a **grid of 2.5 hectares for irrigated areas** and **10 hectares for rainfed areas**.
 
• The samples are tested in **soil testing laboratories** to determine the nutrient composition.
 
• A Soil Health Card is generated, providing farmers with crop-specific recommendations on **nutrient management**.
 
 
 
• **Functions of the SHC Scheme:**
 
 
• Guiding farmers on using fertilizers based on soil type and nutrient deficiency.
 
• Encouraging farmers to adopt organic farming and integrated nutrient management practices.
 
• Creating awareness about soil health and **educating farmers** on sustainable agricultural practices.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of the SHC Scheme:**
 
 
• As of **2023**, millions of soil health cards have been distributed to farmers across India.
 
• Studies have shown that the use of SHC has led to better fertilizer application practices and increased productivity in certain crops.
 
• The scheme has contributed significantly to promoting sustainable farming practices and reducing environmental degradation.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare:**

 
 
• The ministry is responsible for the development and implementation of policies related to agriculture, farmers' welfare, and rural development.
 
• It oversees schemes such as the **Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana (PMFBY)**, **National Food Security Mission (NFSM)**, and **Paramparagat Krishi Vikas Yojana (PKVY)**.
 
 
 
• **Other Ministries Mentioned:**
 
 
• **Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change (MoEFCC):** Focuses on environmental protection, biodiversity conservation, and climate change mitigation.
 
• **Ministry of Jal Shakti:** Works on water resource management and the implementation of schemes like **Har Ghar Jal** and **Namami Gange**.
 
• **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI):** Responsible for statistical data collection and monitoring of government programs.

question: Under PM Gati Shakti, who is responsible for nodal planning?
solution:
The correct answer is __**DPIIT**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **PM Gati Shakti** is a transformative initiative launched by the Government of India to improve the efficiency of infrastructure projects and reduce the cost and time overruns in their implementation.
 
• The **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)** under the **Ministry of Commerce and Industry** is the **nodal agency** responsible for the planning and coordination of this initiative.
 
• **DPIIT** ensures that the planning and implementation of infrastructure projects are carried out in a synchronized manner by integrating various ministries and state governments.
 
• The initiative leverages a digital platform, enabling ministries and departments to coordinate for integrated planning and implementation of infrastructure connectivity projects.
 
• Key objectives include **reducing logistic costs**, improving connectivity, and ensuring sustainable development.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT):**

 
 
• DPIIT was established in 1995 and is responsible for the overall industrial policy formulation and promotion of industrial growth in India.
 
• It plays a crucial role in facilitating investments and fostering innovation and entrepreneurship in the country.
 
• DPIIT is also responsible for initiatives such as **Make in India**, **Startup India**, and **Ease of Doing Business**.
 
 
 
• **About PM Gati Shakti:**
 
 
• Launched on **13 October 2021**, the **PM Gati Shakti National Master Plan** aims to create a digitally integrated infrastructure network.
 
• The focus is on **multi-modal connectivity**, integrating roads, railways, airways, and waterways to achieve seamless logistics.
 
• The initiative targets sectors such as power transmission, pipelines, industrial corridors, and urban infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Objectives of PM Gati Shakti:**
 
 
• Reducing **infrastructure development time** and associated costs.
 
• Promoting the use of **geospatial planning tools** for project synchronization.
 
• Improving India’s ranking in the **Logistics Performance Index (LPI)**.
 
 
 
• **Role of Other Stakeholders:**
 
 
• While DPIIT is the nodal agency, other ministries like the **Ministry of Road Transport and Highways**, the **Ministry of Railways**, and the **Ministry of Power** play significant roles in project execution.
 
• State governments are also involved in ensuring regional development and inter-state connectivity.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Significance of PM Gati Shakti:**

 
 
• It aims to **reduce logistics costs**, which currently account for approximately **13-14% of India’s GDP**.
 
• The plan will help achieve the government’s target of making India a **$5 trillion economy** by 2025.
 
• It also focuses on adopting a **whole-of-government approach** to infrastructure development.
 
 
 
• **Technology Used:**
 
 
• The initiative leverages **GIS (Geographical Information System)** and **real-time data** for better planning and decision-making.
 
• It integrates data from **29 infrastructure ministries** and various government departments.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the National Electricity Plan 2023:

1. It projects over 50% installed power capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030.

2. It proposes nationwide shutdown of thermal plants older than 25 years.

Which of the following is/are Correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The **National Electricity Plan 2023** projects over **50% of installed power capacity from non-fossil sources** by **2030**. This aligns with India’s commitment to achieving net-zero emissions and its Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) under the Paris Agreement. *Hence, statement 1 is correct.*
 
• The plan does not propose a **nationwide shutdown of thermal plants older than 25 years**. Instead, it suggests a phased retirement of these plants based on their efficiency and economic viability. The focus is on reducing emissions without compromising energy security. *Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.*
 
• India aims to achieve an installed renewable energy capacity of **500 GW by 2030**, a target that aligns with the goals outlined in the National Electricity Plan 2023.
 
• The plan also highlights the importance of energy storage solutions, such as battery storage systems and pumped hydro storage, to address the intermittency of renewable energy sources.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Electricity Plan:**

 
 
• The plan is prepared by the **Central Electricity Authority (CEA)** under the Ministry of Power every five years. It serves as a roadmap for the development of the power sector in India.
 
• It includes projections for demand, generation capacity, transmission infrastructure, and policy recommendations to meet future energy needs.
 
 
 
• **India’s Renewable Energy Goals:**
 
 
• India has pledged to achieve **50% of its installed energy capacity from non-fossil sources by 2030**.
 
• It also aims to reduce the emission intensity of its GDP by **33-35% from 2005 levels by 2030**.
 
• As of 2023, India’s total installed renewable energy capacity is over **170 GW**, including solar, wind, bio-energy, and small hydro.
 
 
 
• **Thermal Power Plants in India:**
 
 
• India has a significant number of coal-based thermal power plants, many of which are over 25 years old.
 
• Phasing out older, inefficient plants is a priority to reduce emissions and improve energy efficiency.
 
• However, thermal power remains a crucial part of India’s energy mix to ensure grid stability.
 
 
 
• **Energy Transition Initiatives:**
 
 
• The government has launched schemes like the **National Solar Mission** and **National Wind-Solar Hybrid Policy** to boost renewable energy adoption.
 
• India is also investing in advanced energy storage technologies and grid modernization to support renewable energy integration.
 
 
 
• **Global Climate Commitments:**
 
 
• India’s commitments under the **Paris Agreement** include achieving net-zero carbon emissions by **2070**.
 
• The National Electricity Plan 2023 is a crucial step in meeting these international commitments while ensuring sustainable development.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Energy Demand:** India’s electricity demand is projected to grow at a compound annual growth rate (CAGR) of **6-7% by 2030**.
 
• **International Collaboration:** India is working with countries like the US and UK under initiatives like **Mission Innovation** and the **International Solar Alliance** to promote clean energy technologies.
 
• **Hydrogen Economy:** The government is also focusing on developing a **green hydrogen ecosystem** as a clean energy alternative.
 
• **Decarbonization:** The plan emphasizes the decarbonization of the power sector while maintaining energy security and affordability.

question: What is the impact of PSU disinvestment on the government's financial structure?

options.text: It increases the government's earnings permanently
It does not affect finances at all

solution:
The correct answer is __**It reduces government’s financial assets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Disinvestment** refers to the process by which the government sells its equity or stake in Public Sector Undertakings (**PSUs**) to private entities or the general public. This reduces the government’s ownership in these enterprises, leading to a decrease in its financial assets.
 
• The primary goal of disinvestment is often to **raise immediate revenue** for the government to meet its fiscal deficit targets or to fund development projects.
 
• When the government sells its equity in a PSU, it is essentially converting its equity into liquid cash. While this increases **short-term earnings**, it results in the reduction of long-term financial assets (**hence, the correct answer**).
 
• PSU disinvestment does not increase liabilities. Instead, it provides financial relief in many cases, especially if the PSU has been incurring losses or is underperforming. *Hence, option 1 is incorrect.*
 
• Disinvestment does not necessarily guarantee **permanent earnings**. Once the assets are sold, the government loses ownership and the future revenue streams associated with those assets. *Hence, option 3 is incorrect.*
 
• Disinvestment does have a financial impact on government accounts, as it changes the composition of its assets. Therefore, it is incorrect to say that it does not affect finances at all. *Hence, option 4 is also incorrect.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Objectives of Disinvestment:**

 
 
• **Raise Revenue:** Disinvestment allows the government to generate revenue for development projects, infrastructure building, or reducing fiscal deficits.
 
• **Encourage Private Participation:** It promotes greater private sector participation, making PSUs more efficient and competitive.
 
• **Reduce Government Burden:** Loss-making PSUs are a financial drain on government resources. Disinvestment helps reduce this burden.
 
• **Market Development:** Disinvestment, particularly through stock exchanges, develops the capital market in the country.
 
 
 
• **Disinvestment Mechanisms:**
 
 
• **Initial Public Offering (IPO):** Selling PSU shares to the public for the first time through the stock market.
 
• **Offer for Sale (OFS):** Shares of PSUs are offloaded to institutional and retail investors via stock exchanges.
 
• **Strategic Sale:** A significant portion of a PSU’s equity is sold to a private entity, often along with management control.
 
 
 
• **Examples of PSU Disinvestment:**
 
 
• In 2020, the Indian government sold its stake in **Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL)** as part of its strategic disinvestment plan.
 
• Other notable disinvestment cases include Air India, Hindustan Zinc, and Maruti Udyog.
 
 
 
• **Impact on the Economy:**
 
 
• While disinvestment provides short-term fiscal benefits, it may lead to concerns about **loss of public wealth** or strategic control in key sectors.
 
• It can also lead to better efficiency and productivity if PSUs are privatized and managed effectively.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Fiscal Deficit:** Disinvestment helps the government in reducing its fiscal deficit by generating one-time revenue. For example, in the Union Budget 2021-22, the government set a **disinvestment target of ₹1.75 lakh crore.**
 
• **National Investment Fund (NIF):** Proceeds from disinvestment are often routed through the **NIF** to be utilized for capital expenditure or for funding social sector schemes.
 
• **Challenges:** Some of the challenges of disinvestment include undervaluation of assets, resistance from labor unions, and public opposition due to fears of privatization.
 
• **Government Policies:** The government has adopted a **“strategic disinvestment” policy**, focusing on minimizing its role in sectors where it is not necessary.

question: What is the minimum amount which can be remitted through Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS)?
solution:
**__Rs. 2,00,000__** is the minimum amount that can be remitted through **Real Time Gross Settlement (RTGS).**

 
• The acronym **"RTGS"** stands for Real-Time Gross Settlement, which can be described as a mechanism where fund-transfers are settled continuously and in real-time, individually on a transaction basis (without netting).
 
• **"Real-Time"** means the delivery of instructions at the time of receipt; **"Gross Settlement**" means the settlement of instructions for the transfer of funds happens separately.
 
• The RTGS system is intended specifically for** large-value transactions.**
 
• The minimum amount to be remitted by RTGS is Rs. 2,00,000/- with no limit above or above.

question: Who was the 24th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India?

__
 
• Urjit Patel was the **24th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India** from 4 September 2016 to10 December 2018.
 
• He had also served as **Deputy Governor of RBI** from 11 January 2013 to 4 September 2016.
 
• Presently he is the **Chairman** of **National Institute of Public Finance and Policy (NIPFP)** is an autonomous research institute under Ministry of Finance, Government of India.

• **Expert Committee to Revise and Strengthen the Monetary Policy Framework**:
 
 
• **Objective** of the Committee is to recommend what needs to be done to revise and strengthen the current monetary policy framework with a view to, inter alia, making it transparent and predictable.
 
• **Suggestion:** The Committee suggested a five-member **Monetary Policy Committee (MPC)** - three members from the RBI and two nominated by the Government. 
 
 
 
• Presently the committee comprises six members - three officials of the RBI and three external members nominated by the Government of India.
 
 
• **The Governor of RBI is the ex officio chairperson of the committee**. 
 
• They need to observe a "silent period" seven days before and after the rate decision for "utmost confidentiality". Decisions are taken by majority with the Governor having the casting vote in case of a tie.
 
• The current mandate of the committee is to maintain **4% annual inflation until 31 March 2021** with an upper tolerance of 6% and a lower tolerance of 2%.

• He was the chairman of the **Fourteenth Finance Commission of India.**
 
 
 
• **Bimal Jalan** was the **20th Governor of the Reserve Bank of India.**
 
 
• He has also been the **Chairman of the Economic Advisory Council** to the **Prime Minister** between January 1991 to September 1992.

question: In the context of the banking sector, what does ‘F’ stand for in IFSC?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Financial**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• IFSC is short for **Indian Financial System Code**.
 
• It **represents** the **11 digit character** that you can usually see on your bank’s cheque leaves, or other bank sponsored material.
 
• This **11 character code helps identify the individual bank branches** that participate in the various online money transfer options like NEFT and RTGS.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **RTGS stands for real-time Gross Settlement**.

 
 
• It can be defined as the **continuous (real-time) settlement of funds** individually on an order by order basis (without netting). 
 
• Real-time means the processing of instructions at the time they are received rather than at some later time.
 
• The gross settlement means the settlement of funds transfer instructions occurs individually (on an instruction by instruction basis).
 
• Considering that the fund's settlement takes place in the books of the Reserve Bank of India, the payments are final and irrevocable.
 
• The RTGS system is **primarily meant for large value transactions**. The **minimum amount** to be remitted through RTGS is **Rs 2 lakh**. The **maximum limit** is Rs **10 lakh** per day.
 
 
 
• **NEFT - National Electronic Funds Transfer.**
 
 
• It is a nation-wide payment system facilitating **one-to-one funds transfer**. Under this Scheme, individuals can electronically transfer funds from any bank branch to any individual having an account with any other bank branch in the country participating in the Scheme.
 
 
 
• **The IMPS - Immediate Payment Service.**
 
 
• It helps you access your bank account and transfer funds instantly and securely.

question: ________ is the currency in the hands of the public plus commercial bank reserves, also called ‘high-powered money’.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Monetary base.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• High-powered money is a** macroeconomic term** pertaining to the financial base, which is controlled by the institution in a country that **controls financial policy.**
 
• This is generally either the** finance ministry or the central bank.**
 
• The financial base is called high-powered because the magnitude of changes in the financial base is greatly magnified by the plutocrat multiplier.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Desired reserve ratio:**

 
 
• The reserve ratio is an important tool of the monetary policy of an economy and plays an essential role in regulating the money supply.
 
• When the central bank wants to increase the money supply in the economy, it lowers the reserve ratio.
 
• As a result, commercial banks have higher funds to disburse as loans, thereby increasing the money supply in an economy.
 
 
 
• **Excess reserve:**
 
 
• Excess reserves are capital reserves held by a bank or financial institution in excess of what's needed by controllers, creditors, or internal controls.
 
• For marketable banks, redundant reserves are measured against standard reserve demand quantities set by central banking authorities.
 
 
 
• **Money multiplier:**
 
 
• The phenomenon in which money is created in the form of the creation of credits in the economy is referred to as the money multiplier and is based on the fractional reserve banking system.

question: In which year was the Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI) set up?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] 

**__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Small Industries Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** serves as the apex regulatory body for overseeing the licensing and regulation of micro, small, and medium enterprise finance companies in India.
 
• It operates under the purview of the Ministry of Finance, Government of India, with its headquarters located in Lucknow and offices across the country.
 
• Established on April 2, 1990, by the Government of India, SIDBI initially operated as a wholly owned subsidiary of IDBI Bank. However, it was delinked from IDBI on March 27, 2000.
 
• SIDBI's primary objective is to provide refinance facilities to banks and financial institutions, as well as offer term lending and working capital finance to industries, particularly those in the Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME) sector.
 
• SIDBI coordinates the activities of institutions involved in similar endeavors. Its establishment in 1990 was facilitated through an Act of Parliament.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• SIDBI is among the five All India Financial Institutions overseen by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI).**
 
• The other four institutions include the Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank), National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD), National Housing Bank (NHB), and National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NABFID).
 
• NHB came under government control after the government acquired more than a 51% stake in it. These institutions play a crucial statutory role in the financial markets, particularly through credit extension and refinancing operations, catering to the long-term financing requirements of the industrial sector. SIDBI actively contributes to the development of Micro Finance Institutions (MFIs) through the SIDBI Foundation for Micro Credit.
 
• It supports the extension of microfinance through the Micro Finance Institution (MFI) route, demonstrating its commitment to fostering financial inclusion and supporting the growth of small businesses.

• **Mutual Funds **is **NOT** an **example of small savings.**
 
• **Mutual funds** are** investment vehicles **managed by** professional fund managers.**

• **Post office deposits,** also known as Post-Office Term Deposits (POTDs) or National Savings Time Deposit Accounts, are investment savings accounts offered by India Post. subject: GK
question: Reserve ratio and money supply have ________ relationship.
solution:
The correct answer is __**a negative**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Reserve ratio and money supply have **a negative** relationship.
 
• The reserve ratio is the portion of depositors' balances that banks must have on hand as cash. This is a regulatory requirement set by central banks.
 
• When the reserve ratio is increased, banks have less money to lend out, which reduces the money supply in the economy.
 
• Conversely, when the reserve ratio is decreased, banks can lend more money, which increases the money supply.
 
• This relationship is crucial for central banks when they aim to control inflation and stabilize the economy.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The reserve ratio is a tool used in monetary policy to regulate the banking system and control the money supply.
 
• Other tools include open market operations and the discount rate.
 
• The reserve ratio is part of the broader set of policies known as reserve requirements.
 
• Changes in the reserve ratio can have significant impacts on the economy, influencing interest rates, borrowing, and spending.
 
• Central banks, such as the Federal Reserve in the United States or the Reserve Bank of India, adjust the reserve ratio as part of their efforts to maintain economic stability.

question: Which of the following is a selective credit instrument?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Credit rationing**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Credit rationing** is a selective credit instrument used by central banks to control the amount of credit that is available to the economy.
 
• This tool is used to ensure that credit is directed towards essential sectors and activities, thereby influencing the allocation of resources in the economy.
 
• Unlike tools like the Bank Rate or CRR, which affect the overall credit conditions in the economy, credit rationing specifically targets certain sectors or types of credit.
 
• This method can be particularly useful during times of economic stress or when certain sectors are deemed to be of strategic importance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Variable reserve ratio** refers to the changing reserve requirements that banks must hold, which influences their ability to lend money.
 
• **Bank rate** is the rate at which the central bank lends money to commercial banks, influencing the overall level of interest rates in the economy.
 
• **CRR (Cash Reserve Ratio)** is the percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the central bank in the form of liquid cash.
 
• Selective credit control measures like credit rationing are part of the broader monetary policy toolkit used by central banks to achieve economic stability and growth.

question: Selling of bonds by the RBI will cause money supply to __________.

options.text: No relationship exists between selling bonds and money supply

solution:
The correct answer is __**decrease**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Selling of bonds by the RBI** will cause the money supply to **decrease**.
 
• This is because when the RBI sells bonds, it takes money out of circulation, thereby reducing the overall money supply in the economy.
 
• The reduction in money supply can lead to higher interest rates as there is less money available for borrowing.
 
• This is a monetary policy tool used by the RBI to control inflation and stabilize the economy.

subject: GK
question: Assume that the value of the cash reserve ratio is 25%. What will be the value of money multiplier?
solution:
The correct answer is __**4**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The value of the **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is **25%**.
 
• The **money multiplier** is calculated as the reciprocal of the cash reserve ratio.
 
• Formula: **Money Multiplier = 1 / CRR**
 
• Given that CRR is 25%, the money multiplier is calculated as follows:
 
• **Money Multiplier = 1 / 0.25 = 4**
 
• Therefore, the value of the money multiplier is **4**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **cash reserve ratio** (CRR) is a percentage of a bank's total deposits that must be maintained with the central bank as reserves.
 
• The **money multiplier** effect describes how an initial deposit can lead to a larger final increase in the total money supply.
 
• A higher CRR means a lower money multiplier and vice versa.
 
• The central bank uses CRR as a tool to control liquidity in the banking system.

subject: GK
question: Which of the following is the mandatory requirement of setting aside in liquid assets, such as gold or Government securities, by commercial banks?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Statutory liquidity ratio**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Statutory Liquidity Ratio (SLR)** is a quantitative monetary policy tool used by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** that mandates **commercial banks** to maintain a specific proportion of their **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** in the form of liquid assets.
 
• These liquid assets must be kept in the form of **gold**, **cash**, or **unencumbered government securities** (such as **Treasury Bills** and **Dated Securities**) before the bank can offer credit to its customers.
 
• The primary legal authority for SLR is derived from **Section 24 (2A)** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**, which empowers the central bank to set and adjust this limit to ensure the **solvency** and **liquidity** of the banking system.
 
• By adjusting the **SLR**, the **RBI** can control the expansion of **bank credit**; an increase in **SLR** forces banks to invest more in **government securities**, thereby reducing the funds available for lending to the private sector and helping to curb **inflation**.
 
• Unlike the **Cash Reserve Ratio**, the assets under **SLR** are maintained by the banks themselves rather than being deposited with the **RBI**, and banks earn interest on the **securities** held under this requirement.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR)**:

 
 
• Refers to the share of **Net Demand and Time Liabilities (NDTL)** that **commercial banks** are mandated to maintain with the **RBI** strictly in the form of **liquid cash**.
 
• The **RBI** does not pay any **interest** on the amount maintained as **CRR**, and it serves as a primary tool to regulate **liquidity** and **money supply** in the economy.
 
 
 
• **Current Ratio**:
 
 
• A **liquidity ratio** that measures a company's ability to pay its **short-term obligations** or those due within one year.
 
• It is calculated by dividing **current assets** by **current liabilities** and is a key indicator of **financial health** for non-banking corporations.
 
 
 
• **Margin Requirement**:
 
 
• A qualitative **monetary policy** instrument that refers to the difference between the **market value of collateral** offered for a loan and the actual **loan amount** sanctioned.
 
• By increasing the **margin ratio**, the **central bank** can discourage borrowing for speculative purposes in specific sectors of the economy.

subject: GK
question: Marginal cost is directly proportional to its ________.
solution:
The correct answer is Option 3 i.e. __**Variable costs**__

__
 
• **Marginal cost is directly proportional ****to its Variable costs.**
 
• Marginal cost is the **increase in the total cost when one more product is produced**.
 
• In other words, it is the cost incurred in producing one more unit of goods.
 
• **Fixed costs** are costs that do not depend upon the output or number of units produced.
 
• The rent of a Factory does not depend upon the number of units produced and hence is a Fixed cost.
 
• **Thus, the marginal cost is directly proportional to the variable cost.**
 
• **For Example:-**__
 
 
• Space is rented to make wooden doors. The rent of the space is the Fixed cost.
 
• The cost of labour and the cost of wood are variable costs and depend upon the number of units to be produced.
 
• Thus, the marginal cost to produce one more unit of a door will include labour cost and cost of wood and not the rent of the space, which is a fixed cost and has already been paid for, irrespective of the output.

• **Intermediate Goods:**

 
 
• Intermediate goods are products used as inputs in the production of other goods. They are not final goods and are typically transformed or assembled into final products.

• **Medicine:** **This is not an intermediate good.**
 
 
• Medicine is a final good that is consumed directly by individuals for health purposes. It is not used as an input in the production of other goods.

The correct answer is __**Agriculture sector**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• At higher levels of development, the **Agriculture sector** contributes less to the GDP.
 
• As economies develop, there is a structural shift from agriculture to industrial and service sectors.
 
• In developed economies, the service sector typically becomes the dominant sector contributing to GDP.
 
• The industrial sector also plays a significant role in the GDP of developed countries, but the contribution from agriculture diminishes significantly.
 
• This shift reflects changes in productivity, labor force distribution, and economic priorities.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The transition from an agriculture-based economy to one dominated by industry and services is known as **economic development**.
 
• Economic development is often accompanied by urbanization, improved infrastructure, and higher standards of living.
 
• Policies and investments in education, technology, and infrastructure are key drivers of this structural transformation.
 
• Despite its reduced share in GDP, the agriculture sector remains crucial for food security, employment, and rural development.
 
• Developed countries often have advanced agricultural practices that are highly efficient, contributing to a smaller but more productive agricultural sector.

question: Which of the following attributes is generally present in a perfectly competitive market?

options.text: Companies can enter or exit the market freely
Each company determines its own price based on the cost of production
A few companies monopolize the supply of products
Sellers provide slightly varying forms of the same thing

solution:
The correct answer is __**Companies can enter or exit the market freely**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• A perfectly competitive market is characterized by **free entry and exit of firms**, which ensures that there are no barriers to competition.
 
• This attribute allows new firms to enter the market when profits are high and exit when losses occur, maintaining market equilibrium in the long run.
 
• Free entry and exit help maintain **economic efficiency** by ensuring that resources are allocated to their most productive uses.
 
• It prevents monopolistic practices, as **no single firm can dominate the market** or create obstacles for others to compete.
 
• This feature makes the market highly adaptable to changes in demand and supply, ensuring a steady balance over time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Option 2: Each company determines its own price based on the cost of production**

 
 
• This is a characteristic of **monopolistic competition or oligopoly markets**, not a perfectly competitive market.
 
• In a perfectly competitive market, **firms are price takers** and cannot set their prices. The market determines the price based on overall demand and supply.
 
• Firms in perfect competition can only adjust their production levels to maximize profits.
 
 
 
• **Option 3: A few companies monopolize the supply of products**
 
 
• This describes a **monopoly or oligopoly**, where a single firm or a few firms dominate the market.
 
• In a perfectly competitive market, there are **numerous buyers and sellers**, and no single firm has significant control over the market supply.
 
 
 
• **Option 4: Sellers provide slightly varying forms of the same thing**
 
 
• This refers to **product differentiation**, a feature of monopolistic competition.
 
• In perfect competition, the products are **homogeneous** and identical, with no variations in quality or features.
 
• Homogeneity ensures that consumers do not have any preference for products from one seller over another.

question: The World Happiness Report primarily relies on which type of data?

options.text: Subjective life evaluations and well-being measures

solution:
The correct answer is __**Subjective life evaluations and well-being measures**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The World Happiness Report assesses happiness levels globally by primarily using **subjective life evaluations**, where people are asked to rate their lives on a scale, typically from 0 to 10.
 
• The report incorporates data from the **Gallup World Poll**, which collects individual responses regarding their well-being and satisfaction with life.
 
• Factors such as social support, freedom to make life choices, generosity, corruption perception, and income levels are included to provide a broader context for subjective life evaluations.
 
• Key indicators of happiness include both emotional components (positive and negative emotions) and cognitive evaluations, such as the Cantril Ladder method, where individuals rank their lives.
 
• The report’s focus on subjective measures highlights the importance of understanding how individuals perceive their own lives, rather than relying solely on objective metrics like GDP or employment rates.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Objective economic indicators only**

 
 
• Objective economic indicators include metrics like GDP, employment rates, income levels, and inflation rates.
 
• While these indicators provide measurable data about a country's economy, they do not capture individuals' personal perceptions of happiness or well-being.
 
• For instance, GDP growth might not directly translate to improved happiness if wealth distribution remains unequal.
 
 
 
• **Environmental sustainability metrics**
 
 
• Environmental sustainability metrics assess factors like carbon emissions, renewable energy usage, biodiversity, and ecological footprint.
 
• Though important for sustainable development, these metrics are not directly incorporated into the World Happiness Report.
 
• However, sustainable practices indirectly contribute to societal well-being by ensuring long-term resource availability and quality of life.
 
 
 
• **Military strength and geopolitical stability**
 
 
• Military strength includes a nation’s defense capabilities, while geopolitical stability refers to political relationships and conflict resolution among nations.
 
• Though stability can impact happiness indirectly by reducing fear and promoting security, it is not a primary focus of the World Happiness Report.
 
• The report prioritizes individuals' subjective experiences over these external factors.

question: Which of the following pairs correctly represent light industries?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Knitting needles and Electric bulbs**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Light industries** are those that typically require less capital investment, consume fewer raw materials, and produce smaller goods compared to heavy industries.
 
• **Knitting needles** and **electric bulbs** are examples of light industries because they involve lightweight production processes and cater to direct consumer needs. These industries do not involve extensive resource extraction or heavy machinery.
 
• Light industries focus primarily on **manufacturing goods for end consumers**, like textiles, household appliances, and electronics.
 
• Other examples of light industries include the production of **toys, garments, furniture, and paper products**.
 
• Options like "Oil and Shipbuilding" and "Sewing machines and Shipbuilding" involve heavy industry elements, as shipbuilding and oil production are associated with high resource use and industrial-scale operations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Light Industries vs. Heavy Industries:**

 
 
• Light industries produce **consumer goods** and are characterized by low energy consumption and less environmental impact.
 
• Examples of heavy industries include **steel production, shipbuilding, automobile manufacturing, and oil refining**.
 
• Heavy industries deal with large-scale production and require significant capital investment and infrastructure.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of Light Industries:**
 
 
• They are often located close to markets due to the **consumer-oriented nature** of their products.
 
• Light industries usually employ **skilled labor** and are more labor-intensive than heavy industries.
 
• Their products are typically lightweight, portable, and have a **shorter production cycle**.
 
 
 
• **Examples of Light Industries:**
 
 
• Textile and garment production: Includes clothing manufacturing and knitting.
 
• Food processing: Such as baking and beverage production.
 
• Electronics: Manufacturing of items like **televisions, mobile phones, and electric bulbs**.
 
• Plastic goods: Includes toys, containers, and household items.
 
 
 
• **Economic Importance:**
 
 
• Light industries contribute significantly to the **GDP of developing countries** by catering to the demand for consumer goods.
 
• They generate **employment opportunities** due to their labor-intensive nature.
 
• They are crucial for **export-oriented economic growth**, especially in sectors like textiles and electronics.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Global Examples:**

 
 
• Countries like **China, Bangladesh, and Vietnam** are known for their strong light industrial base in textiles and electronics.
 
• Japan is a leader in producing **electronics and small machinery**, which are part of light industries.
 
 
 
• **Environmental Impact:**
 
 
• Light industries generally have a **lower environmental footprint** compared to heavy industries.
 
• However, some light industries, such as electronics manufacturing, can contribute to **e-waste** if proper recycling measures are not implemented.

question: What is a quicker method for resolving disagreements between businesses?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Alternative dispute resolution**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR)** refers to a collection of processes, including **mediation**, **arbitration**, and **conciliation**, that allow parties to settle disputes outside the formal **courtroom** environment.
 
• It is significantly faster than traditional **litigation** because it avoids the **procedural complexities**, **pre-trial motions**, and **congested court dockets** that often delay cases for years.
 
• In **commercial disputes**, ADR offers a flexible schedule where parties can choose their own **neutral third party** who possesses specific industry expertise, leading to more efficient and relevant outcomes.
 
• These methods focus on **collaborative problem-solving** rather than adversarial competition, which helps in reaching a resolution in a fraction of the time required for **judicial proceedings**.
 
• Settlements reached through **Arbitration** are often legally binding and enforceable under national laws like the **Arbitration and Conciliation Act**, providing the same legal security as a court order but with greater speed.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Core Components of ADR:**

 
 
• **Arbitration:** A formal process where an **arbitrator** hears both sides and issues a binding decision known as an **award**. It is commonly used in **international trade**.
 
• **Mediation:** A non-binding, confidential process where a **mediator** assists parties in reaching a voluntary agreement without imposing a decision.
 
• **Confidentiality:** Unlike **public trials**, ADR keeps sensitive **business data** and trade secrets private, protecting the **brand reputation** of the companies involved.
 
• **Cost-Effectiveness:** By reducing **legal billable hours** and eliminating **court fees**, ADR significantly lowers the **administrative costs** of conflict resolution.
