question: In table tennis, how many consecutive serves does each player get before switching?
solution:
The correct answer is __**2**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Under the standard laws of **Table Tennis** established by the **International Table Tennis Federation (ITTF)**, the right to serve alternates between opponents after every **2 points** scored.
 
• The sequence of service remains constant throughout the game regardless of which player wins the point, ensuring each player receives an equal number of opportunities to initiate play.
 
• This rotation continues until the game ends or until the score reaches **10-10**, at which point the game enters a phase known as a **Deuce**.
 
• In a **standard match**, a game is won by the first player or pair to score **11 points**, provided there is a margin of at least **2 points** over the opponent.
 
• The **server** must strike the ball so that it first touches their court and then touches the receiver's court directly, passing over or around the **net assembly**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Service Exceptions and Variations**:

 
 
• **Deuce Scenarios**: When the score is tied at **10-10**, the sequence of serving and receiving remains the same, but each player shall serve for only **1 point** in turn until a lead of **2 points** is established.
 
• **Expedite System**: If a game is not finished after **10 minutes** of play (unless both players have scored at least 9 points), the **Expedite System** is implemented. Under this rule, service alternates after every **single point**.
 
• **Doubles Play**: The service rotation involves four players. The server first serves to the receiver, then the receiver becomes the server, and the partner of the initial server becomes the new receiver.
 
• **Service Technique**: The ball must be placed on the **open palm** of the stationary free hand and thrown at least **16 cm** into the air without imparting spin before being struck.

__
 
• The **National Games of India** are organized every **2 years**, although the schedule may occasionally vary due to logistical, administrative, or unforeseen challenges.
 
• The event is conducted under the supervision of the **Indian Olympic Association (IOA)**, which is responsible for organizing and managing the games.
 
• The National Games serve as a platform to promote sports at the grassroots level and provide an opportunity for athletes from different states and union territories to compete at a national level.
 
• The games include a wide range of sports, such as **athletics, swimming, hockey, football, shooting, wrestling, and cycling**, among others.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• **History of the National Games:**

 
 
• The National Games were first held as the **Indian Olympic Games** in **1924** in Lahore (now in Pakistan).
 
• The name was later changed to the National Games of India in **1940**.

• **Yellow Ball:** This was briefly experimented with in early **night cricket** attempts in the late 1970s, but was ultimately rejected in favor of white and pink variations due to poor tracking against certain backgrounds.

question:
Consider the following statements regarding the strategic objectives and features of IMEC:

1) IMEC is both an economic and political project linking Asia, the Gulf, and Europe.

2) IMEC cuts transport time and cost to Europe by 20% and 15% via maritime routes.

Which of the above statements is/are correct?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Only 1 is correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **India-Middle East-Europe Economic Corridor (IMEC)** is a massive **multi-modal** infrastructure project designed to integrate **railway**, **ship-to-rail**, and **road** transport networks. It functions as both an **economic** catalyst for trade and a **political** instrument to strengthen strategic ties between **India**, the **Arabian Gulf**, and the **European continent**. ***Hence, statement 1 is correct.***
 
• The project aims to provide a reliable and cost-effective **cross-border** transit network. Official projections from the **European Commission** and signatory nations suggest that **IMEC** will make trade **40% faster** and **30% cheaper** than the existing maritime route through the **Suez Canal**, rather than the 20% and 15% reductions stated. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **IMEC** was officially launched via a **Memorandum of Understanding (MoU)** during the **G20 Summit** in **New Delhi** in **September 2023**.

 
 
• **Geographical Scope**: It consists of two distinct corridors: the **East Corridor**, connecting **India** to the **Arabian Gulf** via sea lanes, and the **Northern Corridor**, connecting the **Arabian Gulf** to **Europe** via rail.
 
• **Strategic Partners**: The primary signatories include **India**, the **United States**, **Saudi Arabia**, the **United Arab Emirates**, the **European Union**, **France**, **Germany**, and **Italy**.
 
• **Digital and Energy Infrastructure**: Beyond logistics, the corridor plans to include an **electricity cable**, a **high-speed data cable**, and a **hydrogen pipeline** to facilitate the trade of **clean energy**.
 
• **Geopolitical Significance**: It is often characterized as a democratic and high-standard alternative to China's **Belt and Road Initiative (BRI)**, emphasizing **sovereignty** and **financial sustainability**.

• The phrase ‘**gross national happiness** was first coined by the 4th King of Bhutan, King Jigme Singye Wangchuck, in 1972 when he declared, **“Gross National Happiness is more important than Gross Domestic Product.”**

• **The GNH measure has been designed to include nine core domains** that are regarded as components of happiness in Bhutan and are constructed of indicators that are robust and informative with respect to each of the domains.
 
• The **nine domains** are:
 
 
• Psychological wellbeing.
 
• Health.
 
• Time use.
 
• Education.
 
• Cultural diversity and resilience.
 
• Good Governance.
 
• Community vitality.
 
• Ecological diversity and resilience.
 
• Living standard.

The Correct answer is France

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****The Seven Years’ War**, also known as the **French and Indian War**, was a global conflict fought primarily between **Great Britain** (supported by Prussia) and **France** (backed by Spain, Saxony, Sweden, and Russia) from 1756 to 1763. This war had significant implications for both Europe and the Americas. 

__
 
• **Background**__:

 __
 
• The Seven Years’ War emerged from ongoing tensions between European powers after the War of the Austrian Succession (which ended in 1748).
 
• Colonial disputes between Britain and France in North America escalated, leading to the outbreak of the French and Indian War in 1754.
 
• Traditional alliances shifted during the so-called 1756 Diplomatic Revolution: Prussia allied with Britain.
 
• Austria signed a treaty with France, ending the long-running French–Habsburg rivalry.
 
 
 
• **Participants**__:
 __
 
• Great Britain, primarily supported by Prussia.
 
• France, backed by Spain, Saxony, Sweden, and Russia.
 
 
 
• **Outcomes**__:
 __
 
• France ceded its North American possessions east of the Mississippi River, Canada, and several Caribbean islands to Britain.
 
• Spain ceded Florida to Britain in exchange for the return of Havana and Manila.
 
• The war concluded with the **1763 Treaty of Paris**__.

• In some countries, Good Friday is a public holiday, allowing people to attend religious services and spend time in reflection and prayer.
 
• The significance of Good Friday lies in its reminder of the ultimate sacrifice and love of **Jesus Christ**, which is central to Christian faith.

question: In India, the International Day of Non-Violence is also celebrated as __________.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Gandhi Jayanti**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Gandhi Jayanti** is celebrated on 2nd October every year to mark the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the leader of the Indian independence movement and a pioneer of the philosophy and strategy of non-violence.
 
• The **International Day of Non-Violence** was established by the United Nations General Assembly in 2007, and it coincides with Gandhi Jayanti to honor Mahatma Gandhi's contributions to the philosophy and practice of non-violence.
 
• Mahatma Gandhi's principles of non-violence have inspired many global movements for civil rights and social change.
 
• On this day, various events are organized across India and worldwide, including prayer meetings, commemorative ceremonies, and cultural programs that reflect Gandhi's teachings and values.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Mahatma Gandhi**, also known as the "Father of the Nation" in India, was born on 2nd October 1869 in Porbandar, Gujarat.
 
• He led India to independence through his non-violent civil disobedience movement and played a key role in India's freedom struggle against British rule.
 
• Gandhi's ideas and practices of non-violence and peaceful resistance have had a lasting impact on global peace movements and leaders such as Martin Luther King Jr. and Nelson Mandela.
 
• In India, 2nd October is a national holiday, and it is observed with various activities that promote non-violence, peace, and harmony.

question: What was the core theme of India's BRICS Chairship in 2021?
solution:
The correct answer is __**BRICS continuity and consensus**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The core theme of India's BRICS Chairship in **2021** was **"BRICS @ 15: Intra-BRICS Cooperation for Continuity, Consolidation, and Consensus"**.
 
• This theme emphasized fostering **collaboration and continuity** among BRICS nations, with a focus on strengthening their partnership and achieving consensus on key global issues.
 
• During its Chairship, India highlighted **multilateralism, reform of multilateral institutions, and socio-economic recovery** from the COVID-19 pandemic.
 
• India organized **over 150 BRICS meetings and events**, including the 13th BRICS Summit, which focused on topics like healthcare, technology, and economic recovery.
 
• The agenda included key areas such as **counter-terrorism, economic growth, sustainable development goals (SDGs), and people-to-people exchanges**.
 
• The theme aligned with the overall vision of BRICS to work towards **constructive and positive global governance** and address shared challenges.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **BRICS Overview:**

 
 
• **BRICS** is an acronym for the grouping of five major economies: **Brazil, Russia, India, China, and South Africa**.
 
• It was formally established in **2009**, with South Africa joining the group in **2010**.
 
• BRICS nations collectively represent about **42%** of the global population and account for approximately **24% of global GDP**.
 
 
 
• **India’s Priorities During BRICS Chairship 2021:**
 
 
• **Healthcare Cooperation:** Focused on equitable access to COVID-19 vaccines and strengthening the global supply chain for medicines and medical equipment.
 
• **Technology and Digital Innovation:** Promoted the use of digital tools to enhance public service delivery and economic growth.
 
• **Counter-Terrorism:** Advocated for a stronger stance against terrorism and its financing through international cooperation.
 
• **Trade and Economic Recovery:** Worked on creating resilient supply chains and enhancing intra-BRICS trade.
 
• **Climate Change:** Highlighted the need for sustainable development and adherence to global climate goals.
 
 
 
• **BRICS Mechanism:**
 
 
• BRICS functions through various mechanisms such as **summits, ministerial meetings, and working groups**.
 
• It includes institutions like the **New Development Bank (NDB)**, established in **2014**, which provides funding for infrastructure and sustainable development projects in member countries.
 
 
 
• **Key Facts About BRICS Chairship 2021:**
 
 
• India hosted the **13th BRICS Summit** virtually on **9th September 2021**.
 
• The summit was chaired by Indian Prime Minister **Narendra Modi**, marking his third leadership of the grouping.
 
• The summit declaration highlighted the need for **strengthening multilateral systems**, global economic recovery, and collective responses to emerging threats.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Option 1: Economic Protectionism:** BRICS nations oppose protectionist policies and advocate for **free and fair trade**. This option is incorrect as it does not align with the cooperative agenda of BRICS.
 
• **Option 3: Cultural Heritage Digitization:** While BRICS emphasizes cultural exchanges, this is not the core theme of the 2021 Chairship.
 
• **Option 4: Military Coordination:** BRICS is primarily an economic and development-oriented group; military coordination is not a focus.

question: Which of the following statements about E. Sreedharan is factually correct?

options.text: He led the development of the Mumbai-Pune Expressway.
He was popularly known as the 'Metro Man of India'.
He drafted the Indian Road Safety Code.
He was responsible for launching the Swachh Bharat Mission.

solution:
The correct answer is __**He was popularly known as the 'Metro Man of India'**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• E. Sreedharan did not lead the development of the **Mumbai-Pune Expressway**, as that project was a landmark achievement of the **Maharashtra State Road Development Corporation (MSRDC)**. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• He is famously known as the **'Metro Man of India'** for his transformative leadership in the **Delhi Metro** project and for completing the **Konkan Railway** project against extreme geographical odds. ***Hence, statement 2 is correct.***
 
• Drafting the **Indian Road Safety Code** was not among his primary professional contributions, as his expertise focused on civil engineering and **railway infrastructure**. ***Hence, statement 3 is incorrect.***
 
• The **Swachh Bharat Mission** is a nationwide cleanliness campaign launched by **Prime Minister Narendra Modi** on **2nd October 2014**, not by E. Sreedharan. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **E. Sreedharan**:

 
 
• He is a retired **Indian Engineering Service (IES)** officer who served as the first Managing Director of the **Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC)**.
 
• He is credited with the restoration of the **Pamban Bridge** in just 46 days after it was damaged by a cyclone in **1964**.
 
• In recognition of his service, the Government of India awarded him the **Padma Shri** in **2001** and the **Padma Vibhushan** in **2008**.
 
• He was also conferred with the **Chevalier de la Légion d'honneur** by the French government in **2005** for his work on the Delhi Metro.
 
• His tenure at **Konkan Railway** is celebrated for implementing a 760-km track through 2,000 bridges and 91 tunnels in record time.

__
 
• **The India Meteorological Department (IMD), **established by the **Government of India in 1875**, serves as the **nation's primary National Meteorological Service**, overseeing** all meteorology-related matters**.
 
• Operating under the Ministry of Earth Sciences, IMD holds primary responsibility for meteorological observations, weather forecasting, and seismology in the country. 
 
• Headquartered in Delhi, IMD manages a vast network of observation stations spread across India and Antarctica, ensuring comprehensive coverage.
 
• Regional offices located in Chennai, Mumbai, Kolkata, Nagpur, Guwahati, and New Delhi facilitate efficient operations and localized services.
 
• Recognized as one of the six Regional Specialised Meteorological Centres by the World Meteorological Organisation, IMD plays a crucial role in forecasting and managing tropical cyclones in the Northern Indian Ocean region.
 
• This includes issuing warnings and naming cyclones affecting areas such as the Malacca Straits, the Bay of Bengal, the Arabian Sea, and the Persian Gulf.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• After India gained independence on 27 April 1949, IMD became a member of the **World Meteorological Organisation**.
 
• The agency's importance has grown significantly due to the crucial role of monsoon rains in Indian agriculture.
 
• It is instrumental in forecasting the annual monsoon and monitoring its progress across the country each season.
 
• The IMD is led by the Director General of Meteorology, presently Mrutyunjay Mohapatra.
 
• In January 2016, IMD initiated the System of Aerosol Monitoring and Research (SAMAR) to analyze the concentration of Black carbon, radiative properties of aerosols, environmental visibility, and their climatic impacts. SAMAR comprises a network of 16 aethalometers, 12 sky radiometers, and 12 nephelometers.

question:
Choose the correct statement(s) related to ‘continentality’.

a. The sea exerts a moderating influence on climate.

b. As the distance from the sea increases, the people experience extreme weather conditions.

c. As one goes from the surface of the earth to higher altitudes, the atmosphere becomes less dense and temperature decreases.
solution:
**The correct answer is: A and B only**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

 

__
 
• **The sea exerts a moderating influence on climate:**

 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• Large bodies of water, such as seas and oceans, have a high capacity for heat storage and release. This results in a moderating effect on the climate of coastal areas, leading to milder winters and cooler summers.
 
• For example, London (close to the Atlantic Ocean) has a more moderate climate compared to Moscow, which is further inland.
 
 
 
• **As the distance from the sea increases, the people experience extreme weather conditions:**
 
 
• This statement is **correct**.
 
• Continental regions, which are far from the sea, often experience more extreme temperature variations. This is because they lack the moderating influence of the ocean, resulting in hotter summers and colder winters.
 
• For example, areas like Siberia (inland Russia) and Central Canada exhibit extreme temperatures due to their distance from the moderating effects of large water bodies.
 
 
 
• **As one goes from the surface of the earth to higher altitudes, the atmosphere becomes less dense and temperature decreases:**
 
 
• This statement is **incorrect**.
 
• Although this statement is true in a general sense (i.e., atmospheric density decreases with altitude and temperatures drop in a typical troposphere), it is not directly related to the concept of 'continentality', which deals specifically with distance from large water bodies.
 
• This concept is more relevant to the study of vertical climate zones and phenomena like the adiabatic lapse rate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Continentality:**

 
 
• Continentality refers to the climatic condition of areas located far from the influence of the ocean, leading to greater temperature extremes.
 
• Land heats up and cools down more quickly than water, which is why inland areas experience more significant temperature variations compared to coastal areas.
 
 
 
• **Moderating Influence of the Sea:**
 
 
• The ocean's ability to store and release large amounts of heat moderates the climate of coastal regions.
 
• This effect can reduce the severity of temperature extremes, leading to more stable and mild climates in areas close to large bodies of water.
 
 
 
• **Impact of Altitude on Climate:**
 
 
• While altitude does indeed affect temperature and atmospheric density, it is a separate concept from continentality.
 
• Higher altitudes generally experience cooler temperatures and thinner air compared to sea level, which is a factor considered in vertical climate zonation.

question: In which of the following regions is convectional rainfall generally more intense due to higher availability of moisture ?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Over oceans**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Convectional rainfall** occurs due to the heating of the Earth's surface, causing air to rise, cool, and condense, forming rain.
 
• **Oceans** have a vast expanse of water, which provides abundant **moisture** for evaporation. This makes convectional rainfall more intense in such regions.
 
• In areas like **deserts**, the moisture content is extremely low despite high temperatures, resulting in negligible convectional rainfall. *Hence, deserts are not favorable for intense convectional rainfall.*
 
• **Inland plateaus** typically experience dry conditions and lack sufficient moisture availability, which limits the occurrence of convectional rainfall. *Hence, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Leeward slopes** are usually dry due to the rain shadow effect. They do not receive much rainfall as the moisture is blocked by the windward side of mountains. *Thus, this option is incorrect.*
 
• **Oceans** are the primary source of evaporation due to their large surface area and continuous heat absorption. This process ensures a high supply of moisture, leading to intense convectional rainfall. *Hence, this option is correct.*

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Convectional rainfall:**

 
 
• Occurs when the ground heats up, warming the air above it.
 
• The warm air rises, cools, and condenses to form clouds and precipitation.
 
• It is common in **tropical regions** where temperatures are high throughout the year.
 
 
 
• **Characteristics of deserts:**
 
 
• Low humidity and moisture availability.
 
• High temperatures but minimal rainfall due to lack of water sources.
 
 
 
• **Inland plateaus:**
 
 
• Located away from large water bodies, limiting moisture availability.
 
• Generally experience dry climates with sporadic rainfall.
 
 
 
• **Leeward slopes:**
 
 
• Situated on the side of a mountain away from prevailing winds.
 
• Rainfall is blocked by the windward slope, resulting in a dry rain shadow region.
 
 
 
• **Importance of oceans:**
 
 
• Act as the primary source for water vapor through evaporation.
 
• Support weather systems like cyclones and convectional rainfall due to high moisture levels.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Evaporation:** The process by which water changes into vapor due to heat.
 
• **Rain shadow effect:** An area of reduced rainfall on the leeward side of mountains.
 
• **Moisture availability:** Key factor determining the intensity of convectional rainfall.
 
• **Tropical regions:** These regions often experience convectional rainfall due to high temperatures and abundant moisture.

solution:

• The Coriolis impact describes the pattern of deflection taken by objects not firmly connected to the ground as they travel long distances around the Earth.
 
• The Coriolis impact is responsible for many massive-scale weather patterns.
 
• The key to the Coriolis effect lies in Earth’s rotation. Earth rotates faster at the Equator than it does on the poles.
 
• Earth is wider on the Equator, so to make a rotation in a 24-hour period.

question: Which of the following is **NOT **one of the major tectonic plates of the earth?

options.text: Africa with the eastern Atlantic floor plate

solution:
The correct answer is __**Nazca plate**__**.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** 

__
 
• Tectonic Plates

 
 
• A tectonic plate (also called a lithospheric plate) is a massive, irregularly-shaped slab of solid rock, generally composed of both continental and oceanic lithosphere.
 
• The lithosphere includes the crust and top mantle with its thickness range varying between 5-100 km in oceanic parts and about 200 km in the continental areas.
 
• The concept of Tectonic Plates was first introduced in **1967**.
 
• A tectonic plate may be a continental plate or an oceanic plate, depending on which of the two occupies the larger portion of the plate.
 
• The Pacific plate is largely an oceanic plate whereas the Eurasian Plate is a continental plate.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Major and Minor Plates

 
 
• The Earth’s lithosphere is divided into seven major and some minor plates.
 
• Young Fold Mountain ridges, oceanic trenches, and/or transform faults surround the major plates. These include:
 
• The Antarctic (and the surrounding oceanic) plate
 
• The North American plate (with the western Atlantic floor separated from the South American plate along with the Caribbean islands)
 
• The South American plate (with the western Atlantic floor separated from the North American plate along with the Caribbean islands)
 
• The Pacific plate
 
• The India-Australia-New Zealand plate
 
• Africa with the eastern Atlantic floor plate
 
• Eurasia and the adjacent oceanic plate
 
 
 
• Some important minor plates include:
 
 
• Cocos plate: Between Central America and the Pacific plate
 
• Nazca plate: Between South America and the Pacific plate
 
• Arabian plate: Mostly the Saudi Arabian landmass
 
• Philippine plate: Between the Asiatic and Pacific plate
 
• Caroline plate: Between the Philippine and Indian plates (North of New Guinea)
 
• Fuji plate: North-east of Australia
 
• Juan De Fuca plate: South-East of North American Plate.
 
 
 
• Hence, Option 1 is correct.

options.text: A tectonic plate is a massive, regularly-shaped slab of solid rock.

Plates move vertically over the asthenosphere as rigid units.

solution:
The correct answer is __**The theory of plate tectonics proposes that the earth’s lithosphere is divided into seven major and some minor plates.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The theory of plate tectonics proposes that the earth’s lithosphere is divided **into seven major and some minor plates**.
 
• **Major plates are**:
 
 
• African plate,
 
• Antarctic plate,
 
• Eurasian plate,
 
• Indo-Australian plate,
 
• North American plate,
 
• Pacific plate and
 
• South American plate.
 

 
 
• **Hence Statement 2 is correct.**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cb6ce0b9a80bc6d98b22a089420b1abf8c5b9ed04bc4641130e138fed7177f4e.png] 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Oceanic and continental plates come together, spread apart, and interact at boundaries all over the planet.
 
• Each type of plate boundary generates distinct geologic processes and landforms.
 
• At convergent boundaries, plate collides with one another.
 
• Herry Hess first attempt to explain the problems of continental drift theory using the plate tectonic mechanism during the 1960s. 
 
• The mobile rock beneath the rigid plates is believed to be moving in a circular manner.
 
• The heated material rises to the surface, spreads and begins to cool, and then sinks back into deeper depths.
 
• This cycle is repeated over and over to generate what scientists call a convection cell or convective flow.
 
• Heat within the earth comes from two main sources: radioactive decay and residual heat.
 
• Arthur Holmes first considered this idea in the 1930s, which later influenced Harry Hess’s thinking about seafloor spreading.
 
• The slow movement of the hot, softened mantle that lies below the rigid plates is the driving force behind the plate movement
 
• The plate tectonic mechanism also becomes helpful to explain the mountain building, the origin of the earthquake, and Seafloor spreading

question: The earth's perihelion occurs in:
solution:
The correct answer is __**January**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The Earth's perihelion** occurs in** early January**, although the exact date varies due to the discrepancy** between the calendar year and Earth's orbit**.
 
• In **2024**, perihelion happened at 7:38 p.m. ET on Jan. 2 (0038 GMT on Jan. 3), as reported by Time and Date. During this event, Earth was situated 91,404,095 miles (147,100,632 kilometers) away from the sun.
 
• Conversely, the aphelion of 2024 occurred on July 5, with Earth positioned 94,510,538 miles (152,099,968 km) distant from the sun.
 
• The difference in Earth's distance from the sun between perihelion and aphelion amounts to approximately 3 million miles (5 million km), which accounts for slightly over 3% of the average sun-Earth distance.
 
• However, this seasonal variation minimally impacts the planet's climate, as Earth's seasons are primarily influenced by the tilt of its axis relative to its orbital plane.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The term **"perihelion" **derives from Greek, meaning "around" (peri) the sun (helios), denoting the point in an astronomical body's orbit when it is closest to the sun. Conversely, aphelion refers to the point when the orbiting body is farthest from the sun.
 
• Natural bodies in the universe typically follow elliptical orbits rather than perfectly circular paths. These orbits can vary in eccentricity, ranging from nearly circular (low eccentricity) to highly elongated (high eccentricity).
 
• Unlike a static placement at the center, the sun traces its own small elliptical path around the system's center of gravity, known as the barycenter, which encompasses both the sun and the orbiting planets.
 
• This barycenter, not necessarily aligned with the ellipse's center, often exhibits a slight offset towards one side of the orbit.

question: What is the name of the large supercontinent that existed 200 million years ago when all the continents were together?
solution:
The Correct Answer is **__Pangea__.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Pangea **is the name of the large supercontinent that existed **200 million years **ago when all the continents were together.
 
• **Pangaea, **the supercontinent, emerged during the **late Paleozoic and early Mesozoic periods.**
 
• One notable segment of this ancient supercontinent was Gondwana Land, situated in the **southern part of Pangaea**, with Angara Land occupying the northern region.
 
• Initially, Gondwana was not classified as a supercontinent due to the separation of landmasses such as Baltica, Laurentia, and Siberia.
 
• Gondwana eventually emerged as the largest continental landmass during the** Paleozoic Era**, spanning approximately 100,000,000 square kilometers, or about one-fifth of Earth's surface.
 
• Areas once part of Gondwana continue to exhibit shared botanical and zoological characteristics that endure to the present day.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **A supercontinent** is a vast landmass comprising most or all of **Earth's continents**.
 
• Some geologists characterize a supercontinent as an amalgamation of once-disparate continents.
 
• These supercontinents have cyclically formed and fragmented over the course of Earth's history.
 
• The most recent supercontinent, Pangea, coalesced between 450 and 320 million years ago.
 
• Its fragmentation commenced approximately 185 million years ago and continues to disperse to this day.

• Radiometric dating calculates an age in years for geologic materials by measuring the presence of a short-life radioactive element.
 
• Radiocarbon dating uses the carbon isotopes **carbon-14 and carbon-12.**

question: The depositional pattern of CaCO₃ and other materials that extend upwards from the floor of a limestone cavern is known as:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Stalagmite**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• A **stalagmite** is a type of rock formation that rises from the floor of a cave due to the accumulation of material deposited on the floor from ceiling drippings.
 
• These formations are typically composed of **calcium carbonate (CaCO3)** and other minerals.
 
• Stalagmites grow upwards from the floor, as opposed to **stalactites**, which hang from the ceiling of caves.
 
• The growth of stalagmites is influenced by the rate of dripping water and the concentration of minerals in the water.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Stalactites** and stalagmites are often found in pairs, with stalactites hanging from the ceiling and stalagmites growing from the ground directly below them.
 
• When a stalactite and stalagmite meet, they form a column or pillar.
 
• The formation of these structures can take thousands of years, depending on the environmental conditions within the cave.
 
• Both formations are key attractions in many limestone caves around the world, drawing interest from tourists and geologists alike.

subject: GK
question: Which is the most widely accepted model to explain the formation and evaluation of the solar system?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Nebular hypothesis**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Nebular hypothesis:-**

 
 
• **The nebular hypothesis proposes that the solar system formed from a giant cloud of gas and dust called a nebula.**
 
• This nebula was mostly composed of hydrogen, with smaller amounts of helium and other elements.
 
• The nebula was also very cold, with temperatures around -270 degrees Celsius (-454 degrees Fahrenheit). 
 
• Over time, the nebula began to collapse under its own gravity. As the nebula collapsed, it spun faster and faster.
 
• This spinning caused the nebula to flatten out into a disk, with the sun forming at the center of the disk.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Gas hypothesis:-**

 
 
• It was proposed by Immanuel Kant in the 18th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a cloud of gas that had been heated by a passing star.**
 
• The heat from the star caused the gas to expand, and this expansion eventually caused the cloud to collapse.
 
• As the cloud collapsed, it spun faster and faster, and this spinning caused the cloud to flatten out into a disk.
 
• The sun formed at the center of the disk, and the planets formed from the remaining material in the disk.
 
 
 
• **Solar hypothesis:-**
 
 
• It was proposed by René Descartes in the 17th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a vortex of matter that was ejected from the sun. **
 
• The vortex of matter eventually cooled and solidified, and this solidified matter formed the planets and other bodies in the solar system.
 
 
 
• **Cloud hypothesis:-**
 
 
• It was proposed by Thomas Wright in the 18th century.
 
• **It proposed that the solar system formed from a cloud of dust that had been ejected from a much larger star. **
 
• The cloud of dust eventually cooled and solidified, and this solidified matter formed the planets and other bodies in the solar system.

subject: GK
question: How many controls are there globally that influence the climate of a particular zone?
solution:
The correct answer is __**6**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• Six major controls influence the climate of a particular zone globally:
 
 
• **Latitude:** The latitude of a location determines the angle at which sunlight strikes the Earth's surface. Locations closer to the equator receive more direct sunlight and have warmer temperatures, while locations farther from the equator receive less direct sunlight and have cooler temperatures.
 
• **Altitude**: Altitude refers to the elevation of a location above sea level. As altitude increases, the atmosphere becomes thinner, and air pressure decreases. This reduced air pressure leads to cooler temperatures.
 
• **Distance from the sea:** Land heats up and cools down more quickly than water. Coastal areas tend to have more moderate temperatures than inland areas because the ocean moderates the temperature fluctuations.
 
• **Ocean currents:** Ocean currents transport heat around the globe. Warm ocean currents can bring warmer temperatures to coastal areas, while cold ocean currents can bring cooler temperatures.
 
• **Topography:** Topography refers to the physical features of a landscape, such as mountains and valleys. Mountains can block wind and precipitation patterns, while valleys can trap heat and moisture.
 
• **Prevailing winds:** Prevailing winds are the dominant wind patterns in a region. They can bring warm or cold air masses to an area, influencing the local climate.

question: Which of the following States/Union Territories of India receives the highest average annual rainfall?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Meghalaya**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Meghalaya** receives the highest average annual rainfall in India.
 
• It is home to Mawsynram, which holds the record for being the wettest place on Earth, with an average annual rainfall of about 11,871 millimeters.
 
• The heavy rainfall in Meghalaya is primarily due to its geographic location, being situated in the windward side of the Khasi Hills, which traps moisture-laden monsoon winds from the Bay of Bengal.
 
• The region's unique topography and climate contribute to its high levels of precipitation, supporting lush greenery and diverse ecosystems.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Delhi** receives an average annual rainfall of around 800 millimeters, primarily during the monsoon season.
 
• **Ladakh** is a cold desert and receives very little rainfall, averaging less than 100 millimeters annually.
 
• **Rajasthan** is also a dry region, with an average annual rainfall varying significantly across the state but generally low, especially in the western parts.
 
• The monsoon winds play a crucial role in determining the rainfall patterns across different regions of India.

• Lucknow is the **capital city** of Uttar Pradesh.
 
• Gomati River is the tributary of the river **Ganga**, originates from **Gomat Taal **in the **Pilibhit district** of **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• It is the only **tributary of Ganga which originates from land**.

question: The Chambal, Hindon and Tons rivers are tributaries of the river:

__
 
• **The significant tributaries of the Yamuna River** include the **Tons, Chambal, Hindon, Betwa, and Ken.**
 
• Originating from the Bhadakla Falls in the Janapav Hills near Mandav, Madhya Pradesh, the Chambal River stretches approximately 1,024 kilometers (636 miles) before joining the Yamuna River in Central and Northern India.
 
• The Hindon River, spanning 400 kilometers in length, serves as another tributary of the Yamuna River. It originates from the Shakumbhari Devi range in the Saharanpur district of Uttar Pradesh, traversing six districts including Saharanpur, Muzaffarnagar, and Meerut.
 
• Flowing through the Garhwal region in Uttarakhand and touching Himachal Pradesh, the Tons River contributes as a tributary to the Yamuna River. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

__
 
• **The Yamuna River, **a prominent waterway in northern India, holds the distinction of being the longest tributary and the second-largest contributor to the Ganges River by discharge.
 
• Stretching across a length of 1,376 kilometers, it encompasses a vast basin area spanning 366,223 square kilometers.
 
• Originating from the Yamunotri glacier nestled in the Himalayan Mountains at an elevation of 6,387 meters, the Yamuna meanders through Yamunanagar before converging at the Triveni Sangam in Prayagraj.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• Flowing through the states of Karnataka and Tamil Nadu, the **Kaveri River **stands as one of the major rivers in India.
 
• In central India, the **Tapi River** emerges as a notable waterway, coursing from east to west for approximately 724 kilometers.

question: Which east-flowing river basin covers the states of Jharkhand, Chhattisgarh and Orissa and has a Drainage area of 39,033 sq km?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Brahmani**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

• **The Brahmani sub-basin** spans an area of **39,033 square kilometers** and exhibits a long, sausage-like shape.
 
• The **Baitarni sub-basin **covers an area of **12,789 square kilometers** and is roughly circular in shape.
 
• Originating near **Nagri village in Ranchi district of Jharkhand** at an elevation of approximately 600 meters, the Brahmani River, also known as **South Koel in its upper reaches**, is a significant seasonal river in the eastern Indian state of Odisha.
 
• The Brahmani is formed by the merging of the** Sankh and South Koel rivers **and traverses through various districts including Sundargarh, Deogarh, Angul, Dhenkanal, Cuttack, Jajapur, and Kendrapara.
 
• South Koel serves as the upper reaches of the Brahmani. Along with the river Baitarani, the Brahmani forms a substantial delta before eventually discharging into the Bay of Bengal at Dhamra.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **The Baitarani River** holds a significant position among the six major rivers of Odisha, India. Revered in popular epics and folklore, the Baitarani River serves as a vital water source for agricultural irrigation in the region.
 
• **The River Nagavali,** also referred to as Langulya, stands as one of the primary rivers in Southern Odisha and Andhra Pradesh states in India. It is situated between the Rushikulya and Godavari basins, contributing to the socio-economic landscape of the area.
 
• **The Sarada River** finds its source in the Ananthagiri hills nestled within the Eastern Ghats of Andhra Pradesh, India.

question: Which river originates south of the equator and flows north through north-eastern Africa to drain into the Mediterranean Sea?
solution:
The correct answer is the __**Nile River.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Origin:** South of the equator in **East Africa**, with the primary source being **Lake Victoria.**
 
• **Flow:** North through **northeastern Africa.**
 
• **Drainage:** Empties into the **Mediterranean Sea.**
 
• **Length:** Approximately 6,650 kilometers (4,130 miles), making it one of the **longest rivers** in the world.
 
• **Significance:** Vital for agriculture in **Egypt** and **Sudan**; historically important for ancient civilizations, especially Egypt.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Congo River:**

__
 
• **Origin:** Begins in the highlands of** northeastern Zambia.**
 
• **Flow:** Flows through the **Congo Basin** in Central Africa, mostly westward.
 
• **Drainage:** Empties into the Atlantic Ocean.
 
• **Length: **About 4,700 kilometers (2,920 miles).
 
• **Significance:** **Second longest** river in Africa; major transportation route in the Congo Basin.

​**Amazon River:**

 
• **Origin:** Originates in the **Andes Mountains **of Peru.
 
• **Flow:** Flows eastward across northern South America.
 
• **Drainage:** Empties into the **Atlantic Ocean**.
 
• **Length:** Approximately 7,000 kilometers (4,350 miles), **considered the longest river by some measurements**.
 
• **Significance:** Largest river by discharge volume of water; vital to the Amazon rainforest ecosystem.

**Lena River:**

 
• **Origin:** Originates in the **Baikal Mountains** of Siberia, Russia.
 
• **Flow:** Flows northward across Siberia.
 
• **Drainage:** Empties into the Arctic Ocean.
 
• **Length: **About 4,400 kilometers (2,736 miles).
 
• **Significance:** One of the major rivers in **Russia**; important for **Arctic navigation** and regional ecology. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__** [IMAGE: https://www.researchgate.net/publication/317372179/figure/fig4/AS:667934481469447@1536259398320/Map-showing-the-Nile-River-with-its-main-branches-White-and-Blue-Niles-and-the-site-of.png] 

**Map Description of the Nile River:**

 
• **Source:**

 
 
• **Lake Victoria:** The Nile's primary source is **Lake Victoria**, located in East Africa.
 
• **Other Important Sources: The Blue Nile**, originating from Lake Tana in Ethiopia, also contributes significantly to the Nile’s flow.
 
 
 
• **Course:**
 
 
• **Northward Flow:** The Nile flows northward through Uganda, then enters Sudan.
 
• **Egyptian Stretch:** It continues through Egypt, passing through major cities such as** Cairo.**
 
 
 
• **Delta:**
 
 
• **Nile Delta:** The river fans out into the Nile Delta before draining into the Mediterranean Sea.
 
 
 
• It has historically been considered the **longest river in the world**, though this has been contested by research suggesting that the **Amazon River** is slightly longer.
